## Reviewer's Guide This PR wires the AgentBridgeService to be instantiated per (db, userId), lazily loads the user’s timezone from settings, and passes it into the bot progress message template, while also auto-detecting and persisting the browser timezone on first load and extending user settings to store it. #### Sequence diagram for Discord bot mention handling with timezone loading ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant DiscordGateway participant BotMessageRouter participant ChatInstance as Chat participant AgentBridgeService participant UserModel participant Database as LobeChatDatabase participant AiAgentService participant ReplyTemplate User->>DiscordGateway: Send mention message DiscordGateway->>BotMessageRouter: Webhook with message BotMessageRouter->>BotMessageRouter: createBot(adapters, agentId) BotMessageRouter->>BotMessageRouter: registerHandlers(bot, serverDB, info) BotMessageRouter->>AgentBridgeService: new AgentBridgeService(serverDB, userId) ChatInstance->>AgentBridgeService: handleMention(thread, message, opts) AgentBridgeService->>AgentBridgeService: safeReaction(mark received, typing) AgentBridgeService->>AgentBridgeService: executeWithWebhooks(...) AgentBridgeService->>AiAgentService: new AiAgentService(db, userId) AgentBridgeService->>AgentBridgeService: loadTimezone() alt timezone_not_loaded AgentBridgeService->>UserModel: new UserModel(db, userId) AgentBridgeService->>UserModel: getUserSettings() UserModel->>Database: read user settings Database-->>UserModel: UserSettings(general.timezone) UserModel-->>AgentBridgeService: UserSettings AgentBridgeService->>AgentBridgeService: cache timezone, set timezoneLoaded else timezone_already_loaded AgentBridgeService-->>AgentBridgeService: reuse cached timezone end AgentBridgeService->>ReplyTemplate: renderStart(userMessage.text, timezone) ReplyTemplate-->>AgentBridgeService: progressContent AgentBridgeService->>ChatInstance: post(progressContent) AiAgentService->>Database: run agent with context Database-->>AiAgentService: agent result AiAgentService-->>AgentBridgeService: reply, topicId AgentBridgeService->>ChatInstance: update progress message with reply ChatInstance-->>User: Show agent reply ``` #### ER diagram for user settings including timezone ```mermaid erDiagram USER ||--|| USER_SETTINGS : has USER_SETTINGS ||--|| USER_GENERAL_CONFIG : has USER { string id string email } USER_SETTINGS { string user_id } USER_GENERAL_CONFIG { string language string primaryColor string responseLanguage boolean telemetry string timezone string transitionMode } ``` #### Class diagram for updated bot services and timezone handling ```mermaid classDiagram class BotMessageRouter { - Map~string, Chat~any~~ botInstancesByToken - Map~string, Chat~any~~ botInstances + initializeDiscordBot(serverDB: LobeChatDatabase, info: ResolvedAgentInfo & DiscordCredentials): Promise~void~ - registerHandlers(bot: Chat~any~, serverDB: LobeChatDatabase, info: ResolvedAgentInfoExtended): void } class AgentBridgeService { - LobeChatDatabase db - string userId - string timezone - boolean timezoneLoaded + AgentBridgeService(db: LobeChatDatabase, userId: string) + handleMention(thread: Thread, message: Message, opts: BridgeHandlerOpts): Promise~void~ + handleSubscribedMessage(thread: Thread, message: Message, opts: BridgeHandlerOpts): Promise~void~ + executeWithWebhooks(thread: Thread, userMessage: Message, opts: ExecuteOpts): Promise~ReplyResult~ + executeWithInMemoryCallbacks(thread: Thread, userMessage: Message, opts: ExecuteOpts): Promise~ReplyResult~ - new Upstash Workflow-backed API route, and wires it into the existing memory extraction executor and workflow service, with tests for the user selection logic and pagination. #### Sequence diagram for hourly user memory extraction workflow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Cron participant UpstashWorkflowRoute as call_cron_hourly_analysis_route participant MemoryExtractionExecutor as MemoryExtractionExecutor participant UserModel as UserModel participant WorkflowService as MemoryExtractionWorkflowService participant QStash as UpstashQStash Cron->>UpstashWorkflowRoute: POST /api/workflows/memory-user-memory/call-cron-hourly-analysis UpstashWorkflowRoute->>UpstashWorkflowRoute: resolveBaseUrl UpstashWorkflowRoute->>MemoryExtractionExecutor: create MemoryExtractionExecutor-->>UpstashWorkflowRoute: executor loop Page eligible users UpstashWorkflowRoute->>MemoryExtractionExecutor: getUsersForHourlyExtraction(limit, cursor) MemoryExtractionExecutor->>UserModel: listUsersForHourlyMemoryExtractor(db, options) UserModel-->>MemoryExtractionExecutor: userRows MemoryExtractionExecutor-->>UpstashWorkflowRoute: UserPaginationResult alt No eligible users UpstashWorkflowRoute-->>Cron: { message, processedUsers: 0 } else Eligible users found UpstashWorkflowRoute->>UpstashWorkflowRoute: compute nextCursor alt dryRun is false UpstashWorkflowRoute->>WorkflowService: triggerProcessUsers(payload, options) WorkflowService->>QStash: client.trigger(body, headers, url) QStash-->>WorkflowService: accepted WorkflowService-->>UpstashWorkflowRoute: ok end alt nextCursor exists UpstashWorkflowRoute->>WorkflowService: triggerHourly({ baseUrl, cursor, dryRun }, options) WorkflowService->>QStash: client.trigger(body, headers, url) QStash-->>WorkflowService: accepted WorkflowService-->>UpstashWorkflowRoute: ok else UpstashWorkflowRoute-->>Cron: { hasNextPage: false } end end end ``` #### Entity relationship diagram for hourly memory eligibility query ```mermaid erDiagram users { string id PK timestamp createdAt } userSettings { string id PK, FK jsonb memory } topics { string id PK string userId FK } messages { string id PK string topicId FK string userId FK text role } users ||--|{ userSettings : has_optional users ||--o{ topics : owns topics ||--o{ messages : has users ||--o{ messages : authored %% Eligibility logic in listUsersForHourlyMemoryExtractor: %% - memory enabled: COALESCE(userSettings.memory.enabled, true) = true %% - has chatted: EXISTS topic with at least one message where messages.role = user ``` #### Updated class diagram for hourly memory extraction components ```mermaid classDiagram class UserModel { +listUsersForHourlyMemoryExtractor(db, options) Query } class ListUsersForMemoryExtractorOptions { +cursor ListUsersForMemoryExtractorCursor +limit number +whitelist string[] } class ListUsersForHourlyMemoryExtractorOptions { +cursor ListUsersForMemoryExtractorCursor +limit number +whitelist string[] } class ListUsersForMemoryExtractorCursor { +createdAt Date +id string } class MemoryExtractionHourlyWorkflowPayload { +baseUrl string +cursor MemoryExtractionWorkflowCursor +dryRun boolean } class MemoryExtractionWorkflowCursor { +createdAt string +id string } class UserPaginationResult { +cursor ListUsersForMemoryExtractorCursor +ids string[] } class MemoryExtractionExecutor { +create() MemoryExtractionExecutor +getUsersForHourlyExtraction(limit, cursor) Promise~UserPaginationResult~ } class MemoryExtractionWorkflowService { +triggerHourly(payload, options) Promise +triggerProcessUsers(payload, options) Promise } class HourlyWorkflowRoute { +POST(context) Result -resolveBaseUrl() string } UserModel ..> ListUsersForHourlyMemoryExtractorOptions : uses ListUsersForHourlyMemoryExtractorOptions --|> ListUsersForMemoryExtractorOptions MemoryExtractionExecutor ..> UserModel : queries MemoryExtractionExecutor ..> UserPaginationResult : returns MemoryExtractionHourlyWorkflowPayload ..> MemoryExtractionWorkflowCursor : has HourlyWorkflowRoute ..> MemoryExtractionExecutor : creates HourlyWorkflowRoute ..> MemoryExtractionHourlyWorkflowPayload : receives HourlyWorkflowRoute ..> MemoryExtractionWorkflowService : calls MemoryExtractionWorkflowService ..> MemoryExtractionHourlyWorkflowPayload : consumes ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add a query method to list users eligible for hourly memory extraction and cover it with tests. |
  • Introduce ListUsersForHourlyMemoryExtractorOptions type alias to reuse existing cursor/whitelist/limit options.
  • Implement UserModel.listUsersForHourlyMemoryExtractor that joins users with userSettings, applies cursor and whitelist predicates, treats missing settings as memory enabled via COALESCE, and requires at least one topic with a user message via EXISTS on topics/messages.
  • Order results deterministically by createdAt and id and support optional limit.
  • Add tests that verify filtering by memory enabled flag and chatted topics, and that whitelist + cursor pagination behave correctly.
| `packages/database/src/models/user.ts`
`packages/database/src/models/__tests__/user.test.ts` | | Extend the memory extraction executor to support hourly extraction pagination over users. |
  • Define MemoryExtractionHourlyWorkflowPayload to describe baseUrl, cursor, and dryRun parameters for hourly workflows.
  • Add MemoryExtractionExecutor.getUsersForHourlyExtraction to call the new UserModel query with limit, cursor, and a whitelist from privateConfig, returning ids and a next cursor.
  • Register an hourly workflow path in WORKFLOW_PATHS for triggering the new hourly analysis endpoint.
| `src/server/services/memory/userMemory/extract.ts` | | Introduce an Upstash Workflow endpoint to drive the hourly memory extraction cron and fan out per-user processing. |
  • Create /api/workflows/memory-user-memory/call-cron-hourly-analysis/route.ts served by Upstash Workflow with flow control (single parallel execution, 1 rps).
  • Resolve a baseUrl from workflow config or app env, validate and deserialize the incoming cursor, and call MemoryExtractionExecutor.getUsersForHourlyExtraction in paged chunks of USER_PAGE_SIZE.
  • When users are found and not in dryRun mode, chunk userIds into USER_BATCH_SIZE and trigger existing MemoryExtractionWorkflowService.triggerProcessUsers for each batch using normalizeMemoryExtractionPayload and buildWorkflowPayloadInput.
  • If a next cursor exists, schedule the next page by calling MemoryExtractionWorkflowService.triggerHourly recursively with the updated cursor and dryRun flag.
  • Return a summary object indicating dryRun, hasNextPage, processedUsers, and scheduledBatches; configure a custom QStash client so internal workflow calls include required extra headers.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Adds an optionIndex field to RouteAttemptResult and wires it through the router runtime so onRouteAttempt callbacks can distinguish between primary and fallback route options. #### Sequence diagram for router runtime onRouteAttempt with optionIndex ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant RouterRuntime participant RouteOption participant Provider participant OnRouteAttemptCallback Client->>RouterRuntime: route(request) loop For each option index RouterRuntime->>RouteOption: selectOption(index) RouterRuntime->>Provider: sendRequest(model, payload) activate Provider alt Provider success Provider-->>RouterRuntime: response RouterRuntime->>OnRouteAttemptCallback: onRouteAttempt(RouteAttemptResult) note over RouterRuntime,OnRouteAttemptCallback: RouteAttemptResult.optionIndex = index else Provider error Provider-->>RouterRuntime: error RouterRuntime->>OnRouteAttemptCallback: onRouteAttempt(RouteAttemptResult) note over RouterRuntime,OnRouteAttemptCallback: RouteAttemptResult.optionIndex = index end deactivate Provider end RouterRuntime-->>Client: route result ``` #### Updated class diagram for RouteAttemptResult with optionIndex ```mermaid classDiagram class RouteAttemptResult { +string channelId +number durationMs +unknown error +string model +number optionIndex +string providerId +string remark +string routerId +boolean success } class RouterRuntime { +route(request) } class OnRouteAttemptCallback { +onRouteAttempt(result RouteAttemptResult) } RouterRuntime ..> RouteAttemptResult : creates RouterRuntime ..> OnRouteAttemptCallback : invokes OnRouteAttemptCallback --> RouteAttemptResult : consumes ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Extend RouteAttemptResult with optionIndex and plumb the current option array index into onRouteAttempt results for both success and error paths. |
  • Add numeric optionIndex property to RouteAttemptResult interface to represent the index in the route options array.
  • Populate optionIndex with the loop index when invoking onRouteAttempt for successful routing attempts.
  • Populate optionIndex with the loop index when invoking onRouteAttempt for failed routing attempts to maintain consistent shape and semantics.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/RouterRuntime/createRuntime.ts` |

You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. body:
## Reviewer's Guide Adds support for the LongCat (美团) LLM provider by wiring environment flags, registering it in model-bank and model-runtime, and introducing LongCat model metadata and an OpenAI-compatible runtime adapter. #### Sequence diagram for LongCat chat completion via OpenAI-compatible runtime ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Developer participant App participant LobeLongCatAI participant OpenAICompatibleClient as createOpenAICompatibleRuntime_client participant LongCatAPI as LongCat_API Developer->>App: callChat(model = LongCat, messages) App->>LobeLongCatAI: chatCompletion(model, messages, apiKey) LobeLongCatAI->>OpenAICompatibleClient: buildRequest(baseURL, provider) OpenAICompatibleClient->>LongCatAPI: POST /openai/v1/chat/completions LongCatAPI-->>OpenAICompatibleClient: 200 OK (completion) OpenAICompatibleClient-->>LobeLongCatAI: normalizeResponse() LobeLongCatAI-->>App: ChatCompletionResult App-->>Developer: render assistant reply ``` #### Class diagram for LongCat model provider and runtime ```mermaid classDiagram class ModelProvider { <> OpenAI Anthropic LongCat Minimax Mistral } class AIChatModelCard { +abilities_functionCall boolean +abilities_reasoning boolean +contextWindowTokens number +description string +displayName string +enabled boolean +id string +pricing object +releasedAt string +type string } class LongCatModelsModule { +allModels AIChatModelCard[] } class ModelProviderCard { +id string +name string +description string +url string +modelsUrl string +checkModel string +chatModels AIChatModelCard[] +settings object } class LongCatProviderCard { +id = "longcat" +name = "LongCat" +description string +url string +modelsUrl string +checkModel = "LongCat-Flash-Lite" +chatModels AIChatModelCard[] +settings_sdkType = "openai" +settings_showModelFetcher boolean } class LobeLongCatAI { +baseURL = "https://api.longcat.chat/openai/v1" +provider ModelProvider +chatCompletion(parameters) Promise } class providerRuntimeMap { +longcat LobeLongCatAI } LongCatModelsModule "1" --> "*" AIChatModelCard : contains LongCatProviderCard --> LongCatModelsModule : uses LongCatProviderCard --|> ModelProviderCard LobeLongCatAI --> ModelProvider : identifies providerRuntimeMap --> LobeLongCatAI : maps_to providerRuntimeMap --> ModelProvider : keyed_by ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Wire LongCat provider environment configuration into the shared LLM config. |
  • Extend zod schema to include ENABLED_LONGCAT and LONGCAT_API_KEY fields.
  • Populate ENABLED_LONGCAT and LONGCAT_API_KEY from process.env, enabling automatic activation when an API key is present.
| `src/envs/llm.ts` | | Expose LongCat models and provider metadata through model-bank. |
  • Register the new './longcat' aiModels entry point in the model-bank package exports.
  • Define a LongCat AI model list with several chat models and capabilities, mirroring other providers’ model cards.
  • Create a LongCat ModelProviderCard with OpenAI-compatible SDK settings and model fetcher enabled.
  • Include LongCatProvider in the default model provider list and exports so it is available in the UI and configuration.
| `packages/model-bank/package.json`
`packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/longcat.ts`
`packages/model-bank/src/modelProviders/index.ts`
`packages/model-bank/src/modelProviders/longcat.ts`
`packages/model-bank/src/const/modelProvider.ts` | | Integrate LongCat into the runtime layer via an OpenAI-compatible adapter. |
  • Export a new LobeLongCatAI runtime from the model-runtime public index.
  • Map the 'longcat' provider enum to LobeLongCatAI in providerRuntimeMap so routing works.
  • Create an OpenAI-compatible runtime instance with LongCat’s base URL and a DEBUG_LONGCAT_CHAT_COMPLETION flag for debugging chat completions.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/index.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/runtimeMap.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/providers/longcat/index.ts` | ---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. body:
## Reviewer's Guide Deduplicates tools at both the agent-config merge layer and the Google/Gemini context builder to prevent duplicate function declarations from being sent to Vertex AI, which were causing 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT errors. #### Sequence diagram for deduplicated tool flow to Vertex AI ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ChatUI participant ChatAgent participant AgentConfig participant GoogleContextBuilder participant VertexAIGemini User->>ChatUI: Send message ChatUI->>ChatAgent: handleMessage(message, activateTools) ChatAgent->>AgentConfig: createAgentExecutors(context) Note over AgentConfig,ChatAgent: Merge default tools with dynamically activated tools ChatAgent->>AgentConfig: dedupeBy on enabledManifests ChatAgent->>AgentConfig: Set based dedupe on enabledToolIds ChatAgent->>AgentConfig: dedupeBy on tools by function.name AgentConfig-->>ChatAgent: resolvedAgentConfig with deduplicated tools ChatAgent->>GoogleContextBuilder: buildGoogleTools(resolvedAgentConfig.tools) GoogleContextBuilder->>GoogleContextBuilder: filter uniqueTools by tool.function.name GoogleContextBuilder-->>ChatAgent: GoogleFunctionCallTool with unique functionDeclarations ChatAgent->>VertexAIGemini: sendChatRequest(tools=functionDeclarations) VertexAIGemini-->>ChatAgent: 200 response (no duplicate function declarations) ChatAgent-->>ChatUI: formatted answer ChatUI-->>User: Display answer ``` #### Updated class diagram for agent tool configuration and Google tools building ```mermaid classDiagram class AgentConfig { +ToolManifest[] enabledManifests +string[] enabledToolIds +Tool[] tools } class ToolManifest { +string identifier } class ToolFunction { +string name } class Tool { +ToolFunction function } class GoogleFunctionCallTool { +GoogleFunctionDeclaration[] functionDeclarations } class GoogleFunctionDeclaration { } class CreateAgentExecutorsModule { +dedupeBy(items, getKey) T[] +createAgentExecutors(context) AgentExecutors } class GoogleContextBuildersModule { +buildGoogleTools(tools) GoogleFunctionCallTool[] +buildGoogleTool(tool) GoogleFunctionDeclaration } class AgentExecutors { } AgentConfig "*" o-- "*" ToolManifest : enabledManifests AgentConfig "*" o-- "*" Tool : tools AgentConfig "*" o-- "*" ToolFunction : via Tool Tool o-- ToolFunction : has GoogleFunctionCallTool "1" o-- "*" GoogleFunctionDeclaration : functionDeclarations CreateAgentExecutorsModule ..> AgentConfig : reads and merges CreateAgentExecutorsModule ..> ToolManifest : dedupeBy(manifest.identifier) CreateAgentExecutorsModule ..> Tool : dedupeBy(tool.function.name) GoogleContextBuildersModule ..> Tool : buildGoogleTools input GoogleContextBuildersModule ..> GoogleFunctionDeclaration : buildGoogleTool output GoogleContextBuildersModule ..> GoogleFunctionCallTool : wraps declarations ``` #### Flow diagram for tool deduplication during agent configuration merge ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start merge additional tools] --> B[Read context.agentConfig.enabledManifests or empty] B --> C[Concat with additional.enabledManifests] C --> D[Apply dedupeBy using manifest.identifier] D --> E[mergedEnabledManifests] A --> F[Read context.agentConfig.enabledToolIds or empty] F --> G[Concat with additional.enabledToolIds] G --> H[Create Set from combined toolIds] H --> I[Expand Set back to array] I --> J[mergedEnabledToolIds] A --> K[Read context.agentConfig.tools or empty] K --> L[Concat with additional.tools] L --> M[Apply dedupeBy using tool.function.name] M --> N[mergedTools] E --> O[Build resolvedAgentConfig enabledManifests = mergedEnabledManifests enabledToolIds = mergedEnabledToolIds tools = mergedTools] N --> O J --> O O --> P[Pass resolvedAgentConfig.tools to buildGoogleTools] P --> Q[In buildGoogleTools: filter tools by unique tool.function.name] Q --> R[Map uniqueTools to functionDeclarations] R --> S[Send deduplicated functionDeclarations to Vertex AI] S --> T[End] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add a generic helper and use it to deduplicate agent tools, manifests, and tool IDs when merging dynamically activated tools into the existing agent configuration. |
  • Introduce a generic dedupeBy utility that filters an array by a derived string key using a Set to track seen keys.
  • When additional tools are present, compute mergedEnabledManifests by concatenating existing and additional manifests and deduplicating by manifest.identifier.
  • Compute mergedEnabledToolIds by concatenating existing and additional tool IDs and deduplicating via a Set on the ID value.
  • Compute mergedTools by concatenating existing and additional tools and deduplicating by tool.function.name before updating resolvedAgentConfig.
| `src/store/chat/agents/createAgentExecutors.ts` | | Deduplicate Google function declarations before sending tools to Gemini to avoid duplicate function names in the Vertex AI request payload. |
  • Track seen tool.function.name values in buildGoogleTools using a Set and filter the incoming tools to a uniqueTools list.
  • Build functionDeclarations from uniqueTools instead of the original tools array so that each function name is declared only once.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Adds a new Jest unit test suite for the error utility functions in packages/utils/src/error.ts, exercising their behavior across a wide range of valid, invalid, and edge-case inputs to solidify contract and prevent regressions. ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce a comprehensive unit test suite for error utility functions. |
  • Create a new test file that groups tests by utility function (isError, isErrorLike, errorNameFrom, errorMessageFrom, errorStackFrom, errorCauseFrom).
  • Add test cases for primitive, null/undefined, plain-object, and genuine Error instances to verify type guards and detection behavior.
  • Cover behavior with Error subclasses and error-like objects that mimic Error shape (name, message, stack, cause).
  • Validate extraction helpers’ behavior when properties are missing, non-string, or malformed, including default/undefined return paths.
  • Align naming, structure, and assertions with existing project test conventions.
| `packages/utils/src/error.test.ts` |

You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. ## Reviewer's Guide This PR ensures topic, thread, and generation topic titles are summarized in the user’s configured AI response language when set, falling back to the UI language, by wiring a new responseLanguage selector into all relevant summarization call sites. #### Sequence diagram for thread/topic title summarization language resolution ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ChatUI participant ChatThreadActionImpl participant useUserStore participant userGeneralSettingsSelectors participant globalHelpers participant chainSummaryTitle participant chatService User->>ChatUI: Send_messages_in_thread ChatUI->>ChatThreadActionImpl: summarizeThreadTitle(messages) ChatThreadActionImpl->>useUserStore: getState() useUserStore-->>ChatThreadActionImpl: userStoreState ChatThreadActionImpl->>userGeneralSettingsSelectors: responseLanguage(userStoreState) userGeneralSettingsSelectors-->>ChatThreadActionImpl: responseLanguage_or_undefined ChatThreadActionImpl->>globalHelpers: getCurrentLanguage() globalHelpers-->>ChatThreadActionImpl: uiLanguage ChatThreadActionImpl->>chainSummaryTitle: chainSummaryTitle(messages, responseLanguage_or_uiLanguage) chainSummaryTitle-->>ChatThreadActionImpl: summaryTitleParams ChatThreadActionImpl->>chatService: fetchPresetTaskResult(params_with_summaryTitleParams) chatService-->>ChatThreadActionImpl: summarizedTitle ChatThreadActionImpl-->>ChatUI: update_thread_title(summarizedTitle) ``` #### Class diagram for updated userGeneralSettingsSelectors and consumers ```mermaid classDiagram class UserStore { } class userGeneralSettingsSelectors { +language(UserStore) string +fontSize(UserStore) string +mermaidTheme(UserStore) string +neutralColor(UserStore) string +primaryColor(UserStore) string +responseLanguage(UserStore) string +telemetry(UserStore) boolean +transitionMode(UserStore) string } class ChatThreadActionImpl { +summarizeThreadTitle(messages) void } class ChatTopicActionImpl { +summarizeTopicTitle(messages) void } class GenerationTopicActionImpl { +summarizeImageGenerationTitle(prompts) void } class VideoGenerationTopicSlice { +summarizeVideoGenerationTitle(prompts) void } UserStore <.. userGeneralSettingsSelectors : reads_state ChatThreadActionImpl --> userGeneralSettingsSelectors : uses_responseLanguage ChatTopicActionImpl --> userGeneralSettingsSelectors : uses_responseLanguage GenerationTopicActionImpl --> userGeneralSettingsSelectors : uses_responseLanguage VideoGenerationTopicSlice --> userGeneralSettingsSelectors : uses_responseLanguage ``` #### Flow diagram for responseLanguage fallback to UI language ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start] --> B[Read responseLanguage from userGeneralSettingsSelectors] B --> C{Is responseLanguage set?} C -- Yes --> D[Use responseLanguage for summarization] C -- No --> E[Call getCurrentLanguage from globalHelpers] E --> F[Use UI language for summarization] D --> G[Generate title via chainSummaryTitle or chainSummaryGenerationTitle] F --> G[Generate title via chainSummaryTitle or chainSummaryGenerationTitle] G --> H[End] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Use the user’s configured AI response language for thread title summarization, with fallback to UI language. |
  • Update thread title summarization params to obtain responseLanguage from the user store via userGeneralSettingsSelectors.
  • Pass responseLanguage || getCurrentLanguage() into chainSummaryTitle for thread title generation.
| `src/store/chat/slices/thread/action.ts` | | Use the user’s configured AI response language for topic title summarization, with fallback to UI language. |
  • Update topic title summarization params to obtain responseLanguage from the user store via userGeneralSettingsSelectors.
  • Pass responseLanguage || getCurrentLanguage() into chainSummaryTitle for topic title generation.
| `src/store/chat/slices/topic/action.ts` | | Use the user’s configured AI response language for image generation topic title summarization, with fallback to UI language. |
  • Update image generation topic summarization params to read responseLanguage from the user store.
  • Pass responseLanguage || getCurrentLanguage() into chainSummaryGenerationTitle for image generation titles.
| `src/store/image/slices/generationTopic/action.ts` | | Use the user’s configured AI response language for video generation topic title summarization, with fallback to UI language. |
  • Update video generation topic summarization params to read responseLanguage from the user store.
  • Pass responseLanguage || getCurrentLanguage() into chainSummaryGenerationTitle for video generation titles.
| `src/store/video/slices/generationTopic/action.ts` | | Expose responseLanguage from user general settings via a selector for reuse at call sites. |
  • Add responseLanguage selector that reads generalConfig(s).responseLanguage.
  • Export responseLanguage through userGeneralSettingsSelectors for use in summarization flows.
| `src/store/user/slices/settings/selectors/general.ts` | ---

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Replaces an expired Discord invitation URL with the new official LobeHub Discord link across documentation and one code constant so all user-facing references point to the active community server. ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Update shared Discord link reference in top-level README files. |
  • Replace the old Discord invite URL reference with the new lobehub invite in the link reference section.
  • Ensure both English and Chinese READMEs reference the same new Discord URL.
| `README.md`
`README.zh-CN.md` | | Update application-level Discord social URL constant. |
  • Change the SOCIAL_URL.discord constant to use the new invite URL so any UI using this constant links to the correct server.
| `packages/business/const/src/branding.ts` | | Update embedded Discord link in web crawler terms HTML template. |
  • Replace the hard-coded Discord href in the terms HTML with the new invite URL so generated/served HTML points to the correct server.
| `packages/web-crawler/src/utils/html/terms.html` | ### Assessment against linked issues | Issue | Objective | Addressed | Explanation | | ------ | ------- | ----- | ----- | | https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/10580 | Update the expired Discord invitation link in README.md to a valid, active Discord server link. | ✅ | | ### Possibly linked issues - **#10580**: The PR replaces the expired Discord invite link with the new lobehub server URL in all occurrences.
---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).

body:
This PR formalizes an accidental removal rather than fixing the regression. 

The real bug is in #10264, which silently stopped consuming `provider_settings` / `showProvider` with no doc update, no deprecation notice, and no changelog entry — clear signs this was unintentional, not a deliberate product decision.

The flag has been part of the public config contract since v1, and issue #12579's Expected behavior confirms it should still work. The correct fix is to restore the flag's behavior at the point #10264 broke it, not delete it.
author: zhangt2333

body: Closing this PR based on @zhangt2333's feedback. The correct approach is to restore the UI consumption of `provider_settings`, not remove the flag. See the replacement PR for the proper fix.
author: LuisSambrano

body:
Thanks for the thorough review @zhangt2333 — you're absolutely right.

After digging into the #10264 diff, the issue becomes clear: when `language_model_settings` and the old `showLLM` variable were removed, the consumption of `showProvider` in the Settings page was dropped along with it. The flag itself survived in the schema and the state mapper, but nothing in the UI was reading it anymore. So it wasn't dead code — it was a silently broken feature.

I've closed this PR and opened #12680 with the correct fix: both the desktop and mobile `useCategory` hooks now extract `showProvider` from the feature flags store and conditionally render the Provider tab, restoring the original contract for enterprise deployments using `FEATURE_FLAGS="-provider_settings"`.

Appreciate the clarity on the intended behavior — learned a lot from this one.

body:
Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Extends the device gateway authentication to support a privileged service token flow and hardens request validation by explicitly requiring userId in both auth paths before routing to the Durable Object stub. #### Sequence diagram for extended device gateway authentication flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Client participant DeviceGatewayWorker participant AuthService participant DEVICE_GATEWAY participant DeviceGatewayDO Client->>DeviceGatewayWorker: HTTP request with token (and optional userId) DeviceGatewayWorker->>DeviceGatewayWorker: Extract token from query alt Missing token DeviceGatewayWorker-->>Client: 401 Missing token else Token present alt token equals env.SERVICE_TOKEN DeviceGatewayWorker->>DeviceGatewayWorker: Read userId from query alt Missing userId DeviceGatewayWorker-->>Client: 400 Missing userId for service token auth else userId present DeviceGatewayWorker->>DEVICE_GATEWAY: idFromName user:userId DEVICE_GATEWAY-->>DeviceGatewayWorker: DeviceGatewayDO id DeviceGatewayWorker->>DEVICE_GATEWAY: get id DEVICE_GATEWAY-->>DeviceGatewayWorker: DeviceGatewayDO stub DeviceGatewayWorker->>DeviceGatewayDO: fetch(request) DeviceGatewayDO-->>Client: Response end else token is JWT DeviceGatewayWorker->>AuthService: verifyDesktopToken(env, token) alt Verification fails AuthService-->>DeviceGatewayWorker: Error DeviceGatewayWorker-->>Client: 401 Unauthorized else Verification succeeds AuthService-->>DeviceGatewayWorker: userId DeviceGatewayWorker->>DEVICE_GATEWAY: idFromName user:userId DEVICE_GATEWAY-->>DeviceGatewayWorker: DeviceGatewayDO id DeviceGatewayWorker->>DEVICE_GATEWAY: get id DEVICE_GATEWAY-->>DeviceGatewayWorker: DeviceGatewayDO stub DeviceGatewayWorker->>DeviceGatewayDO: fetch(request) DeviceGatewayDO-->>Client: Response end end end ``` #### Flow diagram for device gateway queue endpoint userId validation ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start queue endpoint handler] --> B[Clone request and parse JSON body] B --> C{body.userId present?} C -- No --> D[Return 400 Missing userId] C -- Yes --> E[Compute id with DEVICE_GATEWAY.idFromName user:body.userId] E --> F[Get stub with DEVICE_GATEWAY.get id] F --> G[Forward request to stub.fetch] G --> H[Return response to client] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add dual authentication path to support both service token and JWT-based desktop auth while consistently deriving userId for the gateway stub. |
  • Introduce a local userId variable to hold the authenticated user identifier across auth branches
  • Add a service-token-based auth branch that trusts env.SERVICE_TOKEN and reads userId from the request URL query string for CLI debugging
  • Retain the existing JWT auth flow using verifyDesktopToken(env, token) and map its result to the shared userId variable
  • Preserve existing error handling for missing token and extend it for missing userId under the service token path
| `apps/device-gateway/src/index.ts` | | Tighten validation of the JSON POST body used to resolve the target Durable Object instance. |
  • Parse the request body as JSON expecting an object with userId
  • Add an explicit guard that returns HTTP 400 when body.userId is missing before computing the Durable Object id
  • Reuse the userId from the body to resolve the DEVICE_GATEWAY Durable Object stub and forward the request as before
| `apps/device-gateway/src/index.ts` |
---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Updates the device gateway deployment GitHub Actions workflow to pass a domain-specific route to the Cloudflare Wrangler deploy command using a new DEVICE_GATEWAY_DOMAIN secret. #### Flow diagram for deploy-device-gateway GitHub Actions job ```mermaid flowchart TD start[Start deploy-device-gateway workflow] --> checkout[Checkout repository] checkout --> tsc_check[Run npx tsc --noEmit in apps/device-gateway] tsc_check --> deploy[Run npx wrangler deploy --route DEVICE_GATEWAY_DOMAIN] deploy --> end_node[Deployment complete] subgraph Environment_variables cf_token[CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN from secrets] cf_account[CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID from secrets] device_domain[DEVICE_GATEWAY_DOMAIN from secrets] end cf_token --> deploy cf_account --> deploy device_domain --> deploy ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Configure the device gateway CI deployment step to deploy to a specific Cloudflare route using a secret-provided domain. |
  • Modify the wrangler deploy command to include the --route flag parameterized by an environment variable
  • Introduce DEVICE_GATEWAY_DOMAIN as an environment variable mapped from the corresponding GitHub Actions secret

## Reviewer's Guide Updates search configuration for several model providers and models (search1api, Qwen, Qiniu, Zenmux) and aligns Qwen runtime reasoning flag logic, ensuring internal vs parameter-based search is wired correctly across model-bank, runtime, and database defaults. #### Sequence diagram for searchImpl selection during chat request ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI as UI_client participant Orchestrator as Chat_orchestrator participant ModelBank as Model_bank participant DB as PROVIDER_SEARCH_DEFAULTS participant QwenRT as LobeQwenAI_runtime participant Provider as Model_provider User->>UI: Start_chat_with_model UI->>Orchestrator: send_chat_request(model_id, query) Orchestrator->>ModelBank: get_model_card(model_id) ModelBank-->>Orchestrator: AIChatModelCard(settings) Orchestrator->>DB: get_provider_defaults(provider) DB-->>Orchestrator: search_defaults(searchImpl) Orchestrator->>Orchestrator: resolve_searchImpl(card.settings.searchImpl, search_defaults) alt searchImpl_is_internal Orchestrator->>Provider: call_with_internal_search(query) Provider-->>Orchestrator: answer_with_search_context else searchImpl_is_params Orchestrator->>QwenRT: build_params(model, enableThinking, thinkingBudget, baseParams) QwenRT->>QwenRT: set_enable_thinking_when_model_contains_keywords QwenRT-->>Orchestrator: provider_params_with_search_flags Orchestrator->>Provider: call_with_params(query, provider_params_with_search_flags) Provider-->>Orchestrator: answer_with_search_applied_by_provider end Orchestrator-->>UI: final_answer UI-->>User: display_answer ``` #### Class diagram for updated model search settings and Qwen runtime ```mermaid classDiagram class AIChatModelCard { string id string type number maxOutput Abilities abilities Settings settings string releasedAt } class Abilities { boolean functionCall boolean reasoning boolean search boolean vision } class Settings { string searchImpl string[] extendParams } class ProviderSearchSetting { string searchImpl string searchProvider } class ProviderSearchDefaults { Record~string,ProviderSearchSetting~ PROVIDER_SEARCH_DEFAULTS } class LobeQwenAI { +createOpenAICompatibleRuntime() +mapChatParams(model, enableThinking, thinkingBudget, restParams) } class QwenChatModelThinking { id qwen_thinking_variants settings.searchImpl params settings.extendParams enableReasoning, reasoningBudgetToken } class QwenChatModelDeepseekR1 { id qwen_deepseek_r1_variants settings.searchImpl params settings.extendParams reasoningBudgetToken } class Search1apiChatModelDeepseekR1 { id deepseek_r1_online_variants settings.searchImpl internal } class QiniuDeepSeekR1 { id qwen_longdeepseek_r1 abilities.reasoning true abilities.search true } class ZenmuxDeepSeekR1 { id zenmux_deepseek_r1 abilities.reasoning true abilities.search true abilities.vision true } ProviderSearchDefaults --> ProviderSearchSetting AIChatModelCard --> Abilities AIChatModelCard --> Settings QwenChatModelThinking --|> AIChatModelCard QwenChatModelDeepseekR1 --|> AIChatModelCard Search1apiChatModelDeepseekR1 --|> AIChatModelCard QiniuDeepSeekR1 --|> AIChatModelCard ZenmuxDeepSeekR1 --|> AIChatModelCard LobeQwenAI ..> AIChatModelCard LobeQwenAI ..> ProviderSearchDefaults ProviderSearchDefaults ..> AIChatModelCard ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Set explicit search implementation settings for search1api DeepSeek online models. |

agentConfig.systemRole end resolveAgentConfig-->>ChatService: agentConfig with resolvedSystemRole ChatService-->>User: Inbox reply using resolved systemRole ``` #### Flow diagram for inbox systemRole resolution logic in resolveAgentConfig ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start systemRole resolution] --> B[Check slug] B -->|slug is inbox| C[Read agentConfig.systemRole] B -->|slug is not inbox| G[Use runtimeConfig.systemRole ?? agentConfig.systemRole] C --> D{agentConfig.systemRole is non-empty string} D -->|yes| E[resolvedSystemRole = agentConfig.systemRole] D -->|no| F{runtimeConfig.systemRole is defined} F -->|yes| I[resolvedSystemRole = runtimeConfig.systemRole] F -->|no| J[resolvedSystemRole = empty string] G --> K[resolvedSystemRole set for non inbox agent] E --> L[Return resolvedSystemRole] I --> L J --> L K --> L L --> M[End systemRole resolution] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Change systemRole resolution for the inbox builtin agent so user-edited systemRole takes priority over the builtin template, with sensible fallbacks. |

## Reviewer's Guide Routes malformed `default`-type builtin tool calls through the builtin executor instead of the plugin gateway by adding a registry check in `internal_invokeDifferentTypePlugin`, and adds targeted tests to verify routing for builtin vs non-builtin identifiers. #### Sequence diagram for routing default-type tool calls through builtin executor ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor ModelProvider participant ChatStore as ChatStore_useChatStore participant PluginApi as PluginPublicApiActionImpl participant Registry as BuiltinExecutorRegistry participant Builtin as BuiltinExecutor participant Gateway as PluginGateway ModelProvider->>ChatStore: emit ChatToolPayload (type=default) ChatStore->>PluginApi: internal_invokeDifferentTypePlugin(messageId, payload, stepContext) PluginApi->>Registry: hasExecutor(payload.identifier, payload.apiName) alt builtin executor exists Registry-->>PluginApi: true PluginApi->>Builtin: invokeBuiltinTool(messageId, payload, stepContext) Builtin-->>PluginApi: result PluginApi-->>ChatStore: result else no builtin executor Registry-->>PluginApi: false PluginApi->>Gateway: invokeDefaultTypePlugin(messageId, payload) Gateway-->>PluginApi: result PluginApi-->>ChatStore: result end ``` #### Class diagram for updated PluginPublicApiActionImpl routing logic ```mermaid classDiagram class ChatToolPayload { string apiName string arguments string id string identifier string type } class PluginPublicApiActionImpl { - getState() any + internal_invokeDifferentTypePlugin(id string, payload ChatToolPayload, stepContext RuntimeStepContext) Promise any + invokeBuiltinTool(id string, payload ChatToolPayload, stepContext RuntimeStepContext) Promise any + invokeStandaloneTypePlugin(id string, payload ChatToolPayload) Promise any + invokeDefaultTypePlugin(id string, payload ChatToolPayload) Promise any } class BuiltinExecutorRegistry { + hasExecutor(identifier string, apiName string) boolean } class RuntimeStepContext { } PluginPublicApiActionImpl --> ChatToolPayload : uses PluginPublicApiActionImpl --> RuntimeStepContext : uses PluginPublicApiActionImpl --> BuiltinExecutorRegistry : calls hasExecutor note for PluginPublicApiActionImpl "internal_invokeDifferentTypePlugin now checks hasExecutor for type=default and routes to invokeBuiltinTool when true, otherwise to invokeDefaultTypePlugin" ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add compatibility fallback in internal tool routing to detect builtin executors for `type=default` payloads and route them via the builtin tool path instead of the plugin gateway. |
  • In `internal_invokeDifferentTypePlugin`, when `payload.type === 'default'`, check `hasExecutor(payload.identifier, payload.apiName)` to see if a builtin executor exists.
  • If a matching builtin executor is found, call `invokeBuiltinTool(id, payload, stepContext)` and return early, skipping the plugin gateway routing.
  • Preserve existing switch-based routing for all other payload types and for `default` payloads without a matching builtin executor.
| `src/store/chat/slices/plugin/actions/publicApi.ts` | | Add unit tests to verify routing behavior for `internal_invokeDifferentTypePlugin` for builtin and non-builtin `default`-type tool calls. |
  • Add a test case asserting that a `default`-type payload whose identifier/apiName corresponds to a builtin executor triggers `invokeBuiltinTool` and not `invokeDefaultTypePlugin`.
  • Add a test case asserting that a `default`-type payload with a non-builtin identifier continues to call `invokeDefaultTypePlugin` and not `invokeBuiltinTool`.
  • Use `useChatStore.setState` to inject mocked `invokeBuiltinTool` and `invokeDefaultTypePlugin` and assert invocations with the expected arguments.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Adds a comprehensive unit test suite for SocialService (src/services/social.ts), focusing on follow/favorite/like operations, pagination mapping, and polymorphic input handling by mocking lambdaClient and asserting correct API interactions. ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce unit tests for SocialService covering follow, favorite, and like flows with pagination and polymorphic inputs. |
  • Create a new test suite for SocialService that mocks lambdaClient using vi.mock and verifies correct method calls and argument mappings for each service function.
  • Add tests for follow/unfollow flows, including status checks, follow counts, and follower/following retrieval with page/pageSize to limit/offset conversion.
  • Add tests for favorite-related methods, including add/remove, status checks, retrieval of current user favorites, and user-specific favorite agents/plugins.
  • Add tests for like/unlike/toggleLike behavior and retrieval of liked agents/plugins, validating correct handling of numeric IDs versus string identifiers.
  • Add tests for setAccessToken to ensure lambdaClient is correctly configured for authenticated calls and error/edge-case handling is covered where relevant.
| `src/services/social.test.ts` |

Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Disables the fade-in animation and styling behavior for short, single-line assistant messages that appear adjacent to tool calls, to prevent visual flicker caused by component remounts during streaming updates. #### Sequence diagram for streaming assistant messages with tool calls and animation behavior ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant UI as ConversationUI participant Stream as StreamingAPI participant Parser as ConversationFlowParse participant React as ReactRenderer participant Msg as MarkdownMessage User->>UI: Send prompt UI->>Stream: Start streaming response Stream-->>UI: Reasoning block UI->>Parser: parse content with hasTools=false Parser-->>UI: assistantGroup tree (no tools) UI->>React: render assistantGroup React->>Msg: mount with animated=true Stream-->>UI: Short single-line text UI->>Parser: parse content with hasTools=true Parser-->>UI: rebuilt assistantGroup children UI->>React: re-render assistantGroup (components remount) React->>Msg: mount MarkdownMessage alt Before fix React->>Msg: animated=true for single-line tool-adjacent text Msg->>Msg: fadeIn animation replays (flicker) else After fix React->>Msg: animated=false when hasTools=true and isSingleLine=true Msg->>Msg: render without fadeIn (no flicker) end Stream-->>UI: Tool call block UI->>Parser: parse content with hasTools=true Parser-->>UI: updated assistantGroup including tool call UI->>React: re-render assistantGroup React->>Msg: mount or update MarkdownMessage with animated=false for tool-adjacent single-line messages ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Adjust rendering of tool-adjacent single-line assistant messages to disable animation while keeping specific styling. |
  • Compute a dedicated isToolSingleLine flag when a message is both associated with tools and considered single-line.
  • Pass an explicit animated={false} prop to MarkdownMessage for tool-adjacent single-line messages, otherwise fall back to the existing markdownProps.animated value.
  • Simplify the CSS class application so that styles.pWithTool is applied only when isToolSingleLine is true.

# TL;DR: The docs and code for `provider_settings` don't currently align. To keep things consistent, we could either restore the flag or update the docs.


@arvinxx 

The problem is real and unresolved.

The official documentation **still** documents `provider_settings` as a supported feature flag:

https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/97ea30e48baf5ddc5f96ead62bc611d3535a394a/docs/self-hosting/advanced/feature-flags.mdx?plain=1#L40

The flag definition in `schema.ts` also still maps `provider_settings` → `showProvider`. But PR #10264 removed all the code that actually consumed `showProvider`, making `FEATURE_FLAGS=-provider_settings` silently non-functional.

So currently the situation is: the docs tell self-hosting users they can use this flag, but it does nothing. This is either:

1. **A bug** — then please reopen this PR and restore the flag's functionality, or
2. **An intentional deprecation** — then please update the documentation and note it as a breaking change.

Either way, closing while the docs still advertise the feature is misleading to self-hosting users.

## Reviewer's Guide Adjusts UserMemory association parsing to be resilient to non-JSON extra fields and adds tests ensuring plain-text extras are preserved instead of causing failures. #### Sequence diagram for updated UserMemory association extra parsing ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UserMemoryModel participant AssociatedObjectSchema participant parseAssociationExtra loop for each association item UserMemoryModel->>AssociatedObjectSchema: safeParse(item) alt schema validation succeeds AssociatedObjectSchema-->>UserMemoryModel: parsed.data UserMemoryModel->>parseAssociationExtra: parseAssociationExtra(parsed.data.extra) alt extraObject returned parseAssociationExtra-->>UserMemoryModel: extraObject UserMemoryModel->>UserMemoryModel: set parsed.data.extra = extraObject else null returned parseAssociationExtra-->>UserMemoryModel: null UserMemoryModel->>UserMemoryModel: delete parsed.data.extra end UserMemoryModel->>UserMemoryModel: push parsed.data to associations else schema validation fails AssociatedObjectSchema-->>UserMemoryModel: error UserMemoryModel->>UserMemoryModel: skip item end end ``` #### Flow diagram for parseAssociationExtra helper behavior ```mermaid flowchart TD A[start parseAssociationExtra] B[check if value is null undefined or empty string] C[return null] D[try to JSON.parse value] E{parsed is non null object and not array} F[return parsed as Record string unknown] G[return object with property value set to parsed] H[catch parse error] I[return object with property raw set to original value] J[end] A --> B B -->|yes| C --> J B -->|no| D D --> E E -->|yes| F --> J E -->|no| G --> J D --> H H --> I --> J ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Make association `extra` parsing robust to non-JSON and non-object values and normalize them into structured shapes. |

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Configures long-lived immutable cache headers for SPA static assets under /spa to prevent origin overload and chunk load failures in self-hosted deployments behind CDNs. #### Sequence diagram for SPA asset loading through CDN cache ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant Browser participant CDN as CDN_Cache participant Origin as Next_js_App_Container User->>Browser: Navigate_and_log_in Browser->>CDN: Request_multiple_/spa/assets/*.js CDN-->>Browser: Partial_cache_miss CDN->>Origin: Forward_requests_for_missing_assets Origin->>Origin: Match_/spa/:path*.(js|css|woff2?|wasm) Origin-->>CDN: Responses_with_Cache_Control_public_max_age_31536000_immutable CDN-->>Browser: Serve_assets_and_store_in_cache User->>Browser: Reload_or_navigate Browser->>CDN: Request_/spa/assets/*.js CDN-->>Browser: Serve_all_assets_from_cache_cf_cache_status_HIT ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add immutable, long-lived cache headers for SPA asset files served under /spa to align their caching behavior with Next.js static assets and reduce origin load. |
  • Extend Next.js custom headers configuration to include a new rule targeting /spa/:path*.(js|css|woff2?|wasm).
  • Configure Cache-Control header to public, max-age=31536000, immutable for these SPA assets, matching the behavior of hashed static assets.
  • Add a CDN-Cache-Control header with the same value so CDNs cache SPA assets for 1 year independently of browser caching.
  • Document in comments that the rule addresses concurrent loading of 450+ JS chunks and ERR_ABORTED failures on critical route chunks.

## Reviewer's Guide Introduces a new parseDefaultAgentSettings helper that separates DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG into config vs meta buckets, wires it into server global config, and documents the new meta keys (avatar, displayName/title, description, backgroundColor, tags) for the default agent. #### Sequence diagram for DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG parsing and UI usage ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Admin participant Server as ServerGlobalConfig participant Parser as parseDefaultAgentSettings participant UI as WebUI Admin->>Server: Set DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG env and start server Server->>Parser: parseDefaultAgentSettings(DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG) Parser-->>Server: { config, meta } Server->>UI: GET /api/global-config Server-->>UI: { defaultAgent: { config, meta } } UI->>UI: Read defaultAgent.meta.title, avatar, description UI->>UI: Read defaultAgent.config.model, provider, systemRole UI-->>Admin: Render branded default agent in sidebar and chat header ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add parseDefaultAgentSettings to split DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG into config and meta sections with alias handling. |
  • Define META_KEYS set for meta-only keys (avatar, backgroundColor, description, title, tags).
  • Define META_ALIASES to map displayName → title for MetaData.
  • Implement parseDefaultAgentSettings to reuse parseAgentConfig, then distribute keys into config or meta objects, returning only populated sections.
  • Ensure empty or unparsable DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG yields undefined.
| `src/server/globalConfig/parseDefaultAgent.ts` | | Add targeted unit tests for parseDefaultAgentSettings behavior. |
  • Verify model/provider and other non-meta keys go to config.
  • Verify avatar, description, backgroundColor, tags go to meta, with tags parsed to array.
  • Verify displayName is mapped to meta.title and title is respected directly.
  • Verify mixed config+meta strings, and omission of empty config/meta sections and empty strings.
| `src/server/globalConfig/parseDefaultAgent.test.ts` | | Wire parseDefaultAgentSettings into global config while preserving existing server-side merge behavior. |
  • Update getServerGlobalConfig to use parseDefaultAgentSettings so defaultAgent now exposes config and meta correctly to the UI.
  • Keep getServerDefaultAgentConfig using parseAgentConfig and document that it returns only the flat config for merge logic, with meta handled via getServerGlobalConfig.
| `src/server/globalConfig/index.ts` | | Document DEFAULT_AGENT_CONFIG meta keys and combined usage examples in both English and Chinese docs. |
  • Add rows describing displayName, avatar, description, backgroundColor, tags, and a full example to the English basic environment variables doc.

## Reviewer's Guide Implements full OAuth 2.0 device code (device flow) support for the OIDC provider, including provider configuration, dedicated UI pages, localized copy, a native CLI client, and an adapter safeguard to keep DeviceCode authorization state consistent with oidc-provider’s expectations. #### Sequence diagram for OAuth 2.0 device code flow with new OIDC deviceFlow hooks ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant LobehubCLI participant OIDCProvider participant Browser participant NextApp Note over LobehubCLI,OIDCProvider: Device authorization initiation LobehubCLI->>OIDCProvider: POST /oidc/device/auth (device_authorization) OIDCProvider-->>LobehubCLI: device_code, user_code, verification_uri LobehubCLI-->>User: Display user_code and verification_uri User->>Browser: Open verification_uri (e.g. /oauth/device) Note over Browser,NextApp: Initial device code input UI Browser->>NextApp: GET /oauth/device?user_code=XXXX-XXXX&xsrf=secret NextApp-->>Browser: Render DeviceInputPage Browser-->>User: Show DeviceCodeInput form User->>Browser: Enter or confirm user_code, submit form Browser->>OIDCProvider: POST /oidc/device with xsrf and user_code Note over OIDCProvider,Browser: userCodeConfirmSource redirect OIDCProvider->>OIDCProvider: Validate user_code (inFlight) OIDCProvider->>Browser: HTTP 302 to /oauth/device/confirm?xsrf&user_code&client_id&client_name Browser->>NextApp: GET /oauth/device/confirm?... NextApp-->>Browser: Render DeviceConfirmPage with DeviceCodeConfirm Browser-->>User: Show confirmation screen with clientName and userCode User->>Browser: Click Authorize or Deny Browser->>OIDCProvider: POST /oidc/device with xsrf, user_code, confirm/abort OIDCProvider->>OIDCProvider: Complete device authorization Note over OIDCProvider,Browser: successSource redirect OIDCProvider->>Browser: HTTP 302 to /oauth/device/success Browser->>NextApp: GET /oauth/device/success NextApp-->>Browser: Render DeviceSuccessPage with DeviceSuccess Browser-->>User: Show success message Note over LobehubCLI,OIDCProvider: Token polling with guarded DeviceCode adapter LobehubCLI->>OIDCProvider: POST /oidc/token (device_code grant) OIDCProvider->>OIDCProvider: Check DeviceCode record (accountId unset until consent) OIDCProvider-->>LobehubCLI: Pending or tokens LobehubCLI-->>User: Start using API once tokens received ``` #### Class diagram for new device flow React components and pages ```mermaid classDiagram class DeviceCodeInputProps { +string errorKey +string userCode +string xsrf } class DeviceCodeConfirmProps { +string clientName +string userCode +string xsrf } class DeviceCodeInput { +DeviceCodeInput(props DeviceCodeInputProps) } class DeviceCodeConfirm { +DeviceCodeConfirm(props DeviceCodeConfirmProps) } class DeviceSuccess { +DeviceSuccess() } class DeviceInputPage { +DeviceInputPage(props searchParamsPromise) -getErrorMessage(error) } class DeviceConfirmPage { +DeviceConfirmPage(props searchParamsPromise) } class DeviceSuccessPage { +DeviceSuccessPage() } class AuthEnv { +bool ENABLE_OIDC } class OIDCProviderRoutes { +string authorization +string code_verification +string device_authorization +string end_session +string token } DeviceCodeInput --> DeviceCodeInputProps : uses DeviceCodeConfirm --> DeviceCodeConfirmProps : uses DeviceInputPage --> AuthEnv : checks DeviceConfirmPage --> AuthEnv : checks DeviceSuccessPage --> AuthEnv : checks DeviceInputPage --> DeviceCodeInput : renders DeviceConfirmPage --> DeviceCodeConfirm : renders DeviceSuccessPage --> DeviceSuccess : renders OIDCProviderRoutes <.. DeviceCodeInput : posts_to /oidc/device OIDCProviderRoutes <.. DeviceCodeConfirm : posts_to /oidc/device ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Enable and configure OAuth 2.0 device flow in the OIDC provider, including custom routes and UX hooks. |
  • Turn on oidc-provider deviceFlow with base-20 charset, mask, and custom success, confirmation, and input handlers that redirect into Next.js pages with XSRF and contextual params.
  • Add OIDC provider routes for device code verification and device authorization endpoints to align with the new flow.
| `src/libs/oidc-provider/provider.ts` | | Add a native OIDC client configuration for the LobeHub CLI using the device_code grant type. |
  • Register a new native client metadata entry for lobehub-cli using the device_code and refresh_token grant types and no client secret.
| `src/libs/oidc-provider/config.ts` | | Adjust the OIDC adapter to avoid prematurely setting accountId in DeviceCode payloads while still indexing userId at the database level. |
  • Change the adapter’s upsert logic to only inject accountId from the auth context for non-DeviceCode models, while still persisting userId on the record for DeviceCode rows.
  • Document the rationale that oidc-provider uses absence of accountId in DeviceCode payloads to signal in-flight authorization, and that injecting it would cause premature token issuance.
| `src/libs/oidc-provider/adapter.ts` | | Extend tests to cover DeviceCode accountId behavior and ensure existing accountId injection is preserved for other models. |
  • Mock getUserAuth in adapter tests and reset between cases.
  • Add tests verifying that DeviceCode payloads do not get accountId injected from auth context but still store DB userId, that explicit accountId from oidc-provider is preserved, and that non-DeviceCode models (e.g., Interaction) still receive accountId injection.
| `packages/database/src/server/models/__tests__/adapter.test.ts` | | Introduce device flow UI pages for code input, confirmation, and success, wired to oidc-provider POST endpoints and XSRF tokens. |
  • Create a device code input page and component rendering a form posting user_code (and xsrf) to /oidc/device, with error mapping from query strings to i18n keys.
  • Create a confirmation page and component that shows the user code and prompts for authorize/deny, posting confirmation or abort signals to /oidc/device.
  • Create a success page and component that shows a localized success state after device authorization completes, gated by ENABLE_OIDC checks.
| `src/app/[variants]/(auth)/oauth/device/DeviceCodeInput.tsx`
`src/app/[variants]/(auth)/oauth/device/confirm/DeviceCodeConfirm.tsx`
`src/app/[variants]/(auth)/oauth/device/success/DeviceSuccess.tsx`
`src/app/[variants]/(auth)/oauth/device/page.tsx`
`src/app/[variants]/(auth)/oauth/device/confirm/page.tsx`
`src/app/[variants]/(auth)/oauth/device/success/page.tsx` | | Add localized strings for the device authorization flow across all supported locales, keyed under the oauth namespace. |
  • Introduce translation keys for device code input, confirmation, error states, and success messages in the default oauth locale file.
  • Propagate corresponding device-related keys into each locale-specific oauth.json (and related) files to keep i18n coverage consistent.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds first-class Lark/Feishu bot integration by wiring webhook handling, message routing, and configuration UI, including a lightweight Lark REST client and platform abstractions shared with Feishu. #### Sequence diagram for Lark/Feishu webhook handling and agent execution ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor LarkUser participant LarkPlatform participant BotWebhook as BotMessageRouter participant LarkRest as LarkRestApi participant Redis participant DB as ServerDB participant AiAgent as AiAgentService LarkUser->>LarkPlatform: Send text message in chat LarkPlatform->>BotWebhook: HTTP POST /bot/webhook (Lark or Feishu) activate BotWebhook BotWebhook->>BotWebhook: Parse JSON body alt Encrypted event BotWebhook->>BotWebhook: decryptLarkEvent(encrypted, encryptKey) end alt URL verification BotWebhook-->>LarkPlatform: 200 { challenge } deactivate BotWebhook end BotWebhook->>BotWebhook: Validate verificationToken BotWebhook->>BotWebhook: Check event_type == im.message.receive_v1 BotWebhook->>BotWebhook: Extract chatId, sender, messageText BotWebhook->>BotWebhook: Lookup agentMap and credentialsByKey BotWebhook->>+BotWebhook: processLarkMessage(agentId, chatId, credentials, messageText, platform, userId) BotWebhook-->>LarkPlatform: 200 { ok: true } deactivate BotWebhook activate BotWebhook BotWebhook->>LarkRest: sendMessage(chatId, renderStart(messageText)) LarkRest-->>BotWebhook: { messageId: progressMessageId } BotWebhook->>Redis: GET lark-thread:platform:chatId Redis-->>BotWebhook: { topicId } or null BotWebhook->>DB: getServerDB() DB-->>BotWebhook: serverDB BotWebhook->>AiAgent: new AiAgentService(serverDB, userId) BotWebhook->>AiAgent: execAgent(agentId, topicId, messageText, webhooks, botContext) AiAgent-->>BotWebhook: { operationId, topicId } BotWebhook->>Redis: SET lark-thread:platform:chatId { topicId } Redis-->>BotWebhook: OK deactivate BotWebhook ``` #### Sequence diagram for bot-callback webhook updating Lark/Feishu messages ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AgentExec as AgentExecution participant BotCallback as bot-callback route participant DB as ServerDB participant LarkRest as LarkRestApi participant LarkPlatform AgentExec->>BotCallback: HTTP POST /api/agent/webhooks/bot-callback activate BotCallback BotCallback->>BotCallback: Parse body (platformThreadId, progressMessageId, fragments) BotCallback->>BotCallback: detectPlatform(platformThreadId) BotCallback->>DB: SELECT provider by applicationId and platform DB-->>BotCallback: provider row with credentials BotCallback->>BotCallback: Validate appId and appSecret for Lark/Feishu BotCallback->>LarkRest: new LarkRestApi(appId, appSecret, platform) BotCallback->>BotCallback: extractLarkChatId(platformThreadId) BotCallback->>BotCallback: createLarkMessenger(LarkRest, chatId) loop For each step or completion event BotCallback->>LarkRest: editMessage(progressMessageId, renderedContent) LarkRest-->>BotCallback: OK end BotCallback-->>AgentExec: 200 { ok: true } deactivate BotCallback ``` #### Updated class diagram for Lark/Feishu bot types and routing ```mermaid classDiagram class BotMessageRouter { - Map~string, any~ agentMap - Map~string, StoredCredentials~ credentialsByKey + routeWebhook(req Request, platform string, appId string) Promise~Response~ - handleTelegramWebhook(req Request, appId string) Promise~Response~ - handleLarkWebhook(req Request, platform string, appId string) Promise~Response~ - processLarkMessage(agentId string, chatId string, credentials StoredCredentials, messageText string, platform string, userId string) Promise~void~ - decryptLarkEvent(encrypted string, encryptKey string) string - loadProviders() Promise~void~ } class StoredCredentials { + appId string + appSecret string + botToken string + encryptKey string + publicKey string + secretToken string + verificationToken string + webhookProxyUrl string } class LarkRestApi { - appId string - appSecret string - baseUrl string - cachedToken string - tokenExpiresAt number + LarkRestApi(appId string, appSecret string, platform string) + sendMessage(chatId string, text string) Promise~SendResult~ + editMessage(messageId string, text string) Promise~void~ + replyMessage(messageId string, text string) Promise~SendResult~ + getTenantAccessToken() Promise~string~ - truncateText(text string) string - call(method string, path string, body Record) Promise~any~ } class SendResult { + messageId string } class PlatformBot { <> + platform string + applicationId string + start() Promise~void~ + stop() Promise~void~ } class Lark { + platform string + applicationId string - config LarkBotConfig + Lark(config LarkBotConfig) + start() Promise~void~ + stop() Promise~void~ } class LarkBotConfig { + appId string + appSecret string + encryptKey string + platform string + verificationToken string } class AiAgentService { + AiAgentService(serverDB LobeChatDatabase, userId string) + execAgent(agentId string, appContext any, autoStart boolean, botContext any, completionWebhook any, prompt string, stepWebhook any, title string, trigger string, userInterventionConfig any, webhookDelivery string) Promise~AgentExecResult~ } class AgentExecResult { + operationId string + topicId string } class IntegrationProvider { + id string + name string + description string + color string + icon FC + authMode string + autoAppId boolean + docsLink string + webhookMode string + fieldTags IntegrationProviderFieldTags } class IntegrationProviderFieldTags { + appId string + appSecret string + encryptKey string + publicKey string + secretToken string + token string + verificationToken string + webhook string } class PlatformDetailFormValues { + applicationId string + appSecret string + botToken string + encryptKey string + publicKey string + secretToken string + verificationToken string + webhookProxyUrl string } BotMessageRouter --> LarkRestApi : uses BotMessageRouter --> AiAgentService : uses BotMessageRouter --> StoredCredentials : uses LarkRestApi ..> SendResult : returns Lark ..|> PlatformBot Lark --> LarkRestApi : verifies credentials IntegrationProvider --> IntegrationProviderFieldTags PlatformDetailFormValues --> IntegrationProvider : rendered by ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Route Lark/Feishu webhooks through BotMessageRouter and execute agents via AiAgentService with Redis-backed thread state. |
  • Add handleLarkWebhook to parse, decrypt, validate, and filter Lark/Feishu webhook events, and dispatch only text messages to processing
  • Implement processLarkMessage to send an initial ack via LarkRestApi, restore/store topicId in Redis for multi-turn conversations, and invoke AiAgentService.execAgent with step/completion webhooks
  • Add decryptLarkEvent AES-256-CBC helper and register lark/feishu platforms and credentials in agentMap during init, extending supported platforms list
| `src/server/services/bot/BotMessageRouter.ts` | | Introduce LarkRestApi and Lark platform bot to send/edit messages and validate credentials for both Lark and Feishu. |
  • Create LarkRestApi wrapper that manages tenant_access_token auth, message send/edit/reply APIs, and text truncation
  • Add Lark PlatformBot implementation that verifies appId/appSecret on start and supports both lark and feishu via a shared config
  • Register Lark as the implementation for both lark and feishu in the platformBotRegistry
| `src/server/services/bot/larkRestApi.ts`
`src/server/services/bot/platforms/lark.ts`
`src/server/services/bot/platforms/index.ts` | | Extend bot-callback webhook to support Lark/Feishu delivery using the shared completion/step webhook pipeline. |
  • Add extractLarkChatId and LARK_CHAR_LIMIT, plus a Lark PlatformMessenger that uses LarkRestApi for create/edit operations
  • Validate per-platform credentials by checking appId/appSecret for Lark/Feishu and botToken for others
  • Wire Lark/Feishu branch in platform switch to construct messenger and enforce char limit while keeping existing Discord/Telegram behavior
| `src/app/(backend)/api/agent/webhooks/bot-callback/route.ts` | | Update integration UI and configuration model to support Lark/Feishu app-secret auth and extra security fields. |
  • Extend IntegrationProvider with authMode and new fieldTags (appSecret, encryptKey, verificationToken) and add provider entries for Feishu and Lark with links and icons
