body:
## Reviewer's Guide Refactors agent context compression so that GeneralChatAgent can automatically trigger a dedicated compress_context executor between tool/task results and the next LLM call, with runtime-side execution of compression and reuse of shared agent logic for server runtime flows, covered by new tests. #### Sequence diagram for automatic context compression between tools/tasks and LLM ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant GeneralChatAgent participant RuntimeExecutors participant MessageService participant ModelRuntime participant LLM User->>GeneralChatAgent: send user_input GeneralChatAgent->>GeneralChatAgent: createPostCompressionInstruction(state_messages) alt needs_compression_before_first_llm GeneralChatAgent-->>RuntimeExecutors: AgentInstructionCompressContext compress_context else no_compression GeneralChatAgent-->>RuntimeExecutors: call_llm end rect rgb(230,230,255) note over GeneralChatAgent,RuntimeExecutors: Post tool_result phase RuntimeExecutors-->>GeneralChatAgent: tool_result context GeneralChatAgent->>GeneralChatAgent: createPostCompressionInstruction(state_messages) alt needs_compression_after_tool GeneralChatAgent-->>RuntimeExecutors: AgentInstructionCompressContext compress_context else no_compression GeneralChatAgent-->>RuntimeExecutors: call_llm end end rect rgb(230,255,230) note over GeneralChatAgent,RuntimeExecutors: tasks_batch_result with messageSuffix RuntimeExecutors-->>GeneralChatAgent: tasks_batch_result context GeneralChatAgent->>GeneralChatAgent: createPostCompressionInstruction(state_messages, messageSuffix) alt needs_compression_with_suffix GeneralChatAgent-->>RuntimeExecutors: compress_context including messageSuffix else no_compression GeneralChatAgent-->>RuntimeExecutors: call_llm end end opt compress_context_executor_path RuntimeExecutors->>RuntimeExecutors: compress_context(instruction, state) alt has_topicId_and_userId_and_messageIds RuntimeExecutors->>MessageService: createCompressionGroup(topicId, messageIds) MessageService-->>RuntimeExecutors: compressionResult(messagesToSummarize, messageGroupId) RuntimeExecutors->>ModelRuntime: initModelRuntimeFromDB(compressionModel) ModelRuntime-->>RuntimeExecutors: compressionRuntime RuntimeExecutors->>LLM: chat(stream, compressionPayload) LLM-->>RuntimeExecutors: streamed_summary_tokens RuntimeExecutors->>RuntimeExecutors: consumeStreamUntilDone RuntimeExecutors->>MessageService: finalizeCompression(messageGroupId, summaryContent) MessageService-->>RuntimeExecutors: finalCompression(compressedMessages) RuntimeExecutors->>RuntimeExecutors: update_state_messages_to_compressed RuntimeExecutors-->>GeneralChatAgent: compression_result with compressedMessages and messageSuffix else skip_compression RuntimeExecutors-->>GeneralChatAgent: compression_result with skipped=true and original messages end end GeneralChatAgent->>GeneralChatAgent: handle compression_result GeneralChatAgent->>GeneralChatAgent: merge compressedMessages + messageSuffix GeneralChatAgent-->>RuntimeExecutors: call_llm with merged messages RuntimeExecutors->>ModelRuntime: initModelRuntimeFromDB(modelRuntimeConfig) ModelRuntime-->>RuntimeExecutors: runtime RuntimeExecutors->>LLM: chat(stream, merged_messages) LLM-->>RuntimeExecutors: streamed_completion RuntimeExecutors-->>User: final assistant response ``` #### Updated class diagram for GeneralChatAgent compression flow and payload types ```mermaid classDiagram class GeneralChatAgent { - config - findExistingSummary(messages) - createPostCompressionInstruction(messages, options) + handle(context, state) } class AgentInstructionCompressContextPayload { + number currentTokenCount + string existingSummary + any[] messageSuffix + any[] messages } class AgentInstructionCompressContext { + string type + AgentInstructionCompressContextPayload payload } class GeneralAgentCompressionResultPayload { + any[] compressedMessages + string groupId + any[] messageSuffix + string parentMessageId + boolean skipped } class RuntimeExecutors { + compress_context(instruction, state) } class MessageService { + createCompressionGroup(topicId, messageIds, metadata) + finalizeCompression(messageGroupId, summaryContent, metadata) } class ModelRuntimeConfig { + string provider + string model } class AgentConfig { + ModelRuntimeConfig modelRuntimeConfig + CompressionConfig compressionConfig } class CompressionConfig { + boolean enabled + number maxWindowToken } GeneralChatAgent --> AgentConfig : has AgentConfig --> ModelRuntimeConfig : has AgentConfig --> CompressionConfig : has GeneralChatAgent ..> AgentInstructionCompressContext : creates AgentInstructionCompressContext --> AgentInstructionCompressContextPayload : has RuntimeExecutors ..> AgentInstructionCompressContext : executes RuntimeExecutors ..> GeneralAgentCompressionResultPayload : returns RuntimeExecutors ..> MessageService : uses RuntimeExecutors ..> ModelRuntimeConfig : reads GeneralChatAgent ..> GeneralAgentCompressionResultPayload : consumes ``` #### Flow diagram for compress_context runtime executor ```mermaid flowchart TD A_start["Start compress_context(instruction, state)"] --> B_extract["Extract payload: messages, currentTokenCount, messageSuffix"] B_extract --> C_checkTopicUser{Has topicId and userId?} C_checkTopicUser -- No --> D_skipNoContext["Build compression_result with original messages, skipped=true"] D_skipNoContext --> Z_done["Return events, newState, nextContext"] C_checkTopicUser -- Yes --> E_queryMessages["Query DB messages by agentId, threadId, topicId"] E_queryMessages --> F_filterIds["Filter non compressedGroup messages and collect ids"] F_filterIds --> G_hasIds{Any messageIds?} G_hasIds -- No --> D_skipNoContext G_hasIds -- Yes --> H_latestAssistant["Find last assistant message"] H_latestAssistant --> I_createService["Create MessageService"] I_createService --> J_createGroup["createCompressionGroup(topicId, messageIds, metadata)"] J_createGroup --> K_pickModel["Select compressionModel from state.modelRuntimeConfig"] K_pickModel --> L_hasModel{Has compression model and provider?} L_hasModel -- No --> M_skipNoModel["Build compression_result with original messages, skipped=true, parentMessageId=latestAssistant"] M_skipNoModel --> Z_done L_hasModel -- Yes --> N_buildPayload["Build compressionPayload via chainCompressContext(messagesToSummarize)"] N_buildPayload --> O_initRuntime["initModelRuntimeFromDB(serverDB, userId, provider)"] O_initRuntime --> P_streamChat["compressionRuntime.chat(stream, compressionPayload)"] P_streamChat --> Q_consume["consumeStreamUntilDone, accumulate summaryContent, summaryUsage, summaryError"] Q_consume --> R_hasError{summaryError?} R_hasError -- Yes --> S_throw["Throw error"] S_throw --> X_catch["catch(error)"] R_hasError -- No --> T_finalize["finalizeCompression(messageGroupId, summaryContent, metadata)"] T_finalize --> U_pickCompressed["Pick compressedMessages from finalCompression or messagesToSummarize"] U_pickCompressed --> V_updateState["Replace newState.messages with compressedMessages"] V_updateState --> W_usage{Has summaryUsage?} W_usage -- Yes --> W1_updateUsage["UsageCounter.accumulateLLM and update newState.usage and newState.cost"] W1_updateUsage --> Y_buildSuccess W_usage -- No --> Y_buildSuccess["Push compression_complete event and build compression_result with compressedMessages, groupId, messageSuffix, parentMessageId"] Y_buildSuccess --> Z_done X_catch --> X1_log["Log compression failure with currentTokenCount and error"] X1_log --> X2_event["Push compression_error event"] X2_event --> X3_buildErrorResult["Build compression_result with original messages, skipped=true"] X3_buildErrorResult --> Z_done ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add a dedicated compress_context runtime executor that performs DB-backed message compression and returns a compression_result context. |
  • Introduce a compress_context handler that clones state, gathers topic messages from the database, and skips compression when topic or user context is missing or there are no eligible messages.
  • Integrate MessageService.createCompressionGroup/finalizeCompression to manage compressed history groups, filtering out compressedGroup messages from the input set.
  • Resolve the compression model from modelRuntimeConfig, initialize a streaming model runtime via initModelRuntimeFromDB, and stream-compute the summary using chainCompressContext and consumeStreamUntilDone.
  • Update agent state messages with compressed results, accumulate usage and cost via UsageCounter.accumulateLLM, and emit compression_complete or compression_error events.
  • Ensure all code paths return a compression_result phase payload containing compressedMessages, groupId, parentMessageId, messageSuffix, and skipped when applicable, with corresponding tests for success, skipped, and failure scenarios.
| `src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts`
`src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/__tests__/RuntimeExecutors.test.ts` | | Centralize compression decision logic in GeneralChatAgent and extend it to post-tool and post-task phases, including batch task flows with a preserved virtual user prompt. |
  • Add a private createPostCompressionInstruction helper that runs shouldCompress over messages plus optional messageSuffix, and when needed returns an AgentInstructionCompressContext with currentTokenCount, existingSummary, messageSuffix, and messages.
  • Refactor init/user_input phases to use createPostCompressionInstruction before issuing call_llm, preserving prior behavior but with shared logic.
  • Insert compression checks in tool_result, tools_batch_result, and task_result phases so that these phases may yield a compress_context instruction instead of directly calling LLM when the window is exceeded.
  • Extend tasks_batch_result to construct a messagesWithPrompt list, pass the synthetic follow-up user prompt as messageSuffix into compression, and use it when deciding whether to compress.
  • Update compression_result handling so that the next LLM call uses compressedMessages plus any messageSuffix, and add unit tests covering each new compression-triggering phase and the messageSuffix behavior.

`packages/agent-runtime/src/agents/__tests__/GeneralChatAgent.test.ts` | | Extend compression-related types to carry messageSuffix and simplify server AgentRuntimeService to rely on shared GeneralChatAgent behavior. |
  • Augment GeneralAgentCompressionResultPayload with an optional messageSuffix array to preserve synthetic messages through compression and back into the next LLM call.
  • Augment AgentInstructionCompressContext payload with an optional messageSuffix field so agents can instruct the runtime to append synthetic messages post-compression.
  • Adjust AgentRuntimeService to construct GeneralChatAgent without the previous eval-only wrapper and rely on chatConfig.enableContextCompression and shared compression logic.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds an optional injectable ISnapshotStore to AgentRuntimeService so snapshot persistence can be customized (e.g., S3) while preserving existing dev-only FileSnapshotStore behavior, and extends ExecutionSnapshot with optional agent/user identifiers for better downstream partitioning. #### Sequence diagram for per-step snapshot recording with injectable snapshotStore ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Caller participant AgentRuntimeService participant SnapshotStore as ISnapshotStore participant FileSnapshotStore Caller->>AgentRuntimeService: executeStep(operationId, stepIndex) activate AgentRuntimeService AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: compute stepResult and stepPresentationData AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: store = this.snapshotStore alt injected snapshotStore provided AgentRuntimeService->>SnapshotStore: loadPartial(operationId) activate SnapshotStore SnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: partialExecutionSnapshot deactivate SnapshotStore else no injected store alt NODE_ENV is development AgentRuntimeService->>FileSnapshotStore: new FileSnapshotStore() activate FileSnapshotStore FileSnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: store instance deactivate FileSnapshotStore AgentRuntimeService->>SnapshotStore: loadPartial(operationId) activate SnapshotStore SnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: partialExecutionSnapshot deactivate SnapshotStore else non-development without store AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: skip snapshot recording end end opt store is available AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: initialize partial fields (startedAt, model, provider) AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: append new StepSnapshot to partial.steps AgentRuntimeService->>SnapshotStore: savePartial(operationId, partialExecutionSnapshot) activate SnapshotStore SnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: void deactivate SnapshotStore end AgentRuntimeService-->>Caller: step result deactivate AgentRuntimeService ``` #### Sequence diagram for finalizing execution snapshot with injectable snapshotStore ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Caller participant AgentRuntimeService participant SnapshotStore as ISnapshotStore participant FileSnapshotStore Caller->>AgentRuntimeService: executeStep(operationId, lastStepIndex) activate AgentRuntimeService AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: detect completion and compute reason AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: store = this.snapshotStore alt injected snapshotStore provided AgentRuntimeService->>SnapshotStore: loadPartial(operationId) activate SnapshotStore SnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: partialExecutionSnapshot deactivate SnapshotStore else no injected store alt NODE_ENV is development AgentRuntimeService->>FileSnapshotStore: new FileSnapshotStore() activate FileSnapshotStore FileSnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: store instance deactivate FileSnapshotStore AgentRuntimeService->>SnapshotStore: loadPartial(operationId) activate SnapshotStore SnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: partialExecutionSnapshot deactivate SnapshotStore else non-development without store AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: skip snapshot finalization end end opt partialExecutionSnapshot exists and store is available AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: read agentId and userId from agentState.metadata AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: build ExecutionSnapshot with AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: agentId, userId, timing, steps, totals AgentRuntimeService->>SnapshotStore: save(executionSnapshot) activate SnapshotStore SnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: void AgentRuntimeService->>SnapshotStore: removePartial(operationId) SnapshotStore-->>AgentRuntimeService: void deactivate SnapshotStore end AgentRuntimeService-->>Caller: final step result deactivate AgentRuntimeService ``` #### Class diagram for injectable snapshotStore in AgentRuntimeService ```mermaid classDiagram class AgentRuntimeServiceOptions { +QueueService queueService +ISnapshotStore snapshotStore } class AgentRuntimeService { -ISnapshotStore snapshotStore +AgentRuntimeService(options: AgentRuntimeServiceOptions) +executeStep(operationId: string, stepIndex: number): Promise~void~ } class ISnapshotStore { +loadPartial(operationId: string): Promise~PartialExecutionSnapshot~ +savePartial(operationId: string, snapshot: PartialExecutionSnapshot): Promise~void~ +save(snapshot: ExecutionSnapshot): Promise~void~ +removePartial(operationId: string): Promise~void~ } class FileSnapshotStore { } class ExecutionSnapshot { +string agentId +number completedAt +string completionReason +object error +string model +string operationId +string provider +number startedAt +StepSnapshot[] steps +number totalCost +number totalSteps +number totalTokens +string traceId +string userId } class StepSnapshot { +number completedAt +string content +object context +object[] events +number executionTimeMs +number inputTokens +object[] messages +object[] messagesAfter +number outputTokens +string reasoning +number startedAt +number stepIndex +string stepType +object[] toolsCalling +object[] toolsResult +number totalCost +number totalTokens } AgentRuntimeServiceOptions --> ISnapshotStore : optional AgentRuntimeService --> AgentRuntimeServiceOptions : uses AgentRuntimeService --> ISnapshotStore : snapshotStore FileSnapshotStore ..|> ISnapshotStore ISnapshotStore --> ExecutionSnapshot ExecutionSnapshot --> StepSnapshot ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Make snapshot persistence pluggable in AgentRuntimeService via an optional snapshotStore while keeping legacy dev-only tracing as fallback. |
  • Extend AgentRuntimeServiceOptions with an optional snapshotStore field and document its behavior and dev fallback semantics.
  • Add a private snapshotStore property on AgentRuntimeService and initialize it from options, defaulting to null.
  • Refactor executeStep step-level snapshot recording to use the injected snapshot store when available, otherwise lazily instantiate FileSnapshotStore only in development mode, and add error logging on failures.
  • Refactor executeStep finalization logic to reuse the injected or dev FileSnapshotStore, finalizing snapshots through the common store interface and logging failures.
| `src/server/services/agentRuntime/AgentRuntimeService.ts` | | Augment execution snapshot metadata with agent and user identifiers for downstream storage partitioning. |
  • Add optional agentId field to ExecutionSnapshot to record which agent produced the trace.
  • Add optional userId field to ExecutionSnapshot to record which end user the trace belongs to.
  • Populate agentId and userId in the final snapshot using metadata from the agent state when finalizing snapshots.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Updates the desktop app to bundle agent-browser v0.20.1, removes the now-unnecessary AGENT_BROWSER_NATIVE runtime env override, and aligns the builtin agent-browser skill documentation and descriptions with the new default native-mode behavior. #### Sequence diagram for desktop app startup env configuration with agent-browser v0.20.1 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant DesktopMainProcess participant Env participant AgentBrowserCLI participant SystemChrome DesktopMainProcess->>Env: read existing PATH DesktopMainProcess->>Env: append desktop resources binDir to PATH Note right of Env: PATH now includes bundled agent-browser v0.20.1 DesktopMainProcess->>DesktopMainProcess: initialize App (no AGENT_BROWSER_NATIVE override) AgentBrowserCLI->>Env: read PATH AgentBrowserCLI->>SystemChrome: auto-detect Chrome/Chromium SystemChrome-->>AgentBrowserCLI: browser endpoint AgentBrowserCLI-->>DesktopMainProcess: execute browser automation in native mode by default ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Update bundled agent-browser binary version used by the desktop build pipeline. |
  • Bump the agent-browser VERSION constant from 0.17.0 to 0.20.1 used by the download script.
  • Ensure the desktop build/package flow pulls the new agent-browser v0.20.1 binary into the resources/bin directory.
| `apps/desktop/scripts/download-agent-browser.mjs` | | Remove explicit native-mode environment override in the desktop main process now that native mode is default. |
  • Delete setting of process.env.AGENT_BROWSER_NATIVE to '1' during app initialization so behavior relies on agent-browser defaults.
  • Keep PATH mutation logic intact to continue exposing the bundled binary on PATH.
| `apps/desktop/src/main/core/App.ts` | | Align builtin agent-browser skill documentation and metadata with agent-browser v0.20.1 and default native mode. |
  • Update the user-facing content to reference agent-browser v0.20.1 and clarify that native mode runs by default.
  • Adjust the builtin skill description string to include the agent-browser v0.20.1 version in the description text.
| `packages/builtin-skills/src/agent-browser/content.ts`
`packages/builtin-skills/src/agent-browser/index.ts` |

Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).

## Reviewer's Guide Fixes context compression so failed or empty summaries no longer wipe conversation history, adds a streaming onFinish fallback for non-chunking providers, and corrects compression threshold calculations to use the actual model context window and a 75% default ratio. #### Sequence diagram for updated context compression with rollback and onFinish fallback ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant StreamingExecutorActionImpl as StreamingExecutor participant TokenCounter participant AgentRuntime participant CreateAgentExecutors as CreateAgentExecutors participant ChatService participant MessageService participant Store User->>StreamingExecutor: sendMessage StreamingExecutor->>StreamingExecutor: buildCompressionModel(model, provider) StreamingExecutor->>StreamingExecutor: maxWindowToken = modelContextWindowTokens(model, provider) StreamingExecutor->>AgentRuntime: execute(agentConfig, compressionConfig(enabled, maxWindowToken)) AgentRuntime->>TokenCounter: shouldCompress(messages, maxWindowToken, thresholdRatio) TokenCounter-->>AgentRuntime: needsCompression, currentTokenCount, threshold alt needsCompression == true AgentRuntime->>CreateAgentExecutors: compressContext(state, opContext, messages) CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: startOperation(summaryOperationId) CreateAgentExecutors->>ChatService: fetchPresetTaskResult(params, onMessageHandle, onFinish, onError) par streaming text chunks ChatService-->>CreateAgentExecutors: onMessageHandle(chunk type=text) CreateAgentExecutors->>CreateAgentExecutors: hasSummaryTextChunk = true CreateAgentExecutors->>CreateAgentExecutors: append chunk.text to summaryContent CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: internal_dispatchMessage(updateMessage summaryContent) and nonStreaming provider ChatService-->>CreateAgentExecutors: onFinish(content) CreateAgentExecutors->>CreateAgentExecutors: finishContent = content and error case ChatService-->>CreateAgentExecutors: onError(error) CreateAgentExecutors->>CreateAgentExecutors: summaryError = error CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: completeOperation(summaryOperationId, error=summary_generation_failed) CreateAgentExecutors->>CreateAgentExecutors: summaryOperationCompleted = true end CreateAgentExecutors->>CreateAgentExecutors: if !hasSummaryTextChunk and finishContent then summaryContent = finishContent CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: internal_dispatchMessage(updateMessage summaryContent) CreateAgentExecutors->>CreateAgentExecutors: normalizedSummaryContent = summaryContent.trim() alt summaryError exists or normalizedSummaryContent is empty CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: completeOperation(summaryOperationId, error=summary_generation_failed) CreateAgentExecutors->>MessageService: cancelCompression(agentId, groupId, messageGroupId, threadId, topicId) MessageService-->>CreateAgentExecutors: rollbackResult(messages) CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: replaceMessages(restoredMessages) CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: completeOperation(compressOperationId, error=compression_failed) CreateAgentExecutors-->>AgentRuntime: compression_result(skipped=true, compressedMessages=restoredMessages) else summary successful CreateAgentExecutors->>MessageService: finalizeCompression(agentId, content=normalizedSummaryContent, messageGroupId, topicId) MessageService-->>CreateAgentExecutors: finalResult(messages) CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: completeOperation(summaryOperationId) CreateAgentExecutors->>Store: completeOperation(compressOperationId) CreateAgentExecutors-->>AgentRuntime: compression_result(skipped=false, compressedMessages=finalResult.messages) end else needsCompression == false AgentRuntime-->>StreamingExecutor: continue conversation without compression end StreamingExecutor-->>User: updated messages rendered ``` #### Updated class diagram for compression configuration and token counting ```mermaid classDiagram class TokenCounter { <> +number DEFAULT_MAX_CONTEXT +number DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_RATIO +getCompressionThreshold(maxWindowToken, thresholdRatio) number +shouldCompress(messages, maxWindowToken, thresholdRatio) CompressionDecision } class CompressionDecision { +boolean needsCompression +number currentTokenCount +number threshold } class StreamingExecutorActionImpl { +executeStreaming(model, provider, agentConfigData, params) void -buildCompressionConfig(model, provider, agentConfigData) CompressionConfig } class CompressionConfig { +boolean enabled +number maxWindowToken +CompressionModel compressionModel } class CompressionModel { +string model +string provider } class CreateAgentExecutors { +compressContext(state, opContext, messages) AgentRuntimeContext -generateSummary(messagesToSummarize, model, provider) void -handleSummarySuccess(normalizedSummaryContent) void -handleSummaryFailure(errorMessage) void } class AgentRuntimeContext { +string phase +CompressionResultPayload payload } class CompressionResultPayload { +number originalTokenCount +number compressedTokenCount +boolean skipped +Message[] compressedMessages } class Message { +string id +string role +string content +MessageMetadata metadata } class MessageMetadata { +Usage usage } class Usage { +number totalOutputTokens } class ChatService { +fetchPresetTaskResult(params, onMessageHandle, onFinish, onError) Promise~void~ } class MessageService { +finalizeCompression(agentId, content, messageGroupId, topicId) CompressionResult +cancelCompression(agentId, groupId, messageGroupId, threadId, topicId) CompressionResult } class CompressionResult { +Message[] messages } %% Relationships StreamingExecutorActionImpl --> CompressionConfig : builds CompressionConfig o-- CompressionModel StreamingExecutorActionImpl --> TokenCounter : uses_for_thresholds TokenCounter --> CompressionDecision CreateAgentExecutors --> ChatService : uses CreateAgentExecutors --> MessageService : uses CreateAgentExecutors --> AgentRuntimeContext : returns AgentRuntimeContext o-- CompressionResultPayload CompressionResultPayload o-- Message Message o-- MessageMetadata MessageMetadata o-- Usage MessageService --> CompressionResult ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Harden context compression flow to avoid data loss and support non-streaming providers when generating summaries. |
  • Track streamed text chunks, finish-only content, and errors separately when generating compression summaries.
  • Use onFinish callback to populate summary content when no text chunks are streamed, and update the compression group message accordingly.
  • Normalize and validate the summary content; if empty or errored, cancel compression via messageService.cancelCompression, restore original messages, and surface compression_error events.
  • Ensure summary and compression operations are completed exactly once, and only finalize compression when there is non-empty normalized summary content.
| `src/store/chat/agents/createAgentExecutors.ts` | | Align compression threshold calculation with model context window and updated default ratio, and update corresponding tests. |
  • Change DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.75 while keeping the default max context at 128k tokens.
  • Update getCompressionThreshold and shouldCompress tests to assert the new 96k default threshold and behavior below/at the threshold.
  • Ensure needsCompression is false for 70k tokens under the new 96k threshold and for exactly-at-threshold usage values.
| `packages/agent-runtime/src/utils/tokenCounter.ts`
`packages/agent-runtime/src/utils/tokenCounter.test.ts` | | Provide the model-specific context window to the compression configuration in the streaming executor. |
  • Look up contextWindowTokens for the active model/provider via aiModelSelectors and aiInfra store.
  • Pass maxWindowToken into compressionConfig when constructing the agent runtime context so threshold calculations use the correct window size.
| `src/store/chat/slices/aiChat/actions/streamingExecutor.ts` | | Bump project version and extend changelog metadata for the new release. |
  • Update package.json version from 2.1.41 to 2.1.42.
  • Add a new 2.1.42 section to CHANGELOG.md and update the v2 changelog JSON accordingly.
| `package.json`
`CHANGELOG.md`
`changelog/v2.json` | | Add regression tests around compression rollback and onFinish fallback behavior. |
  • Introduce a compress-context.test.ts suite for createAgentExecutors to cover rollback on empty/failed summary and onFinish-only providers.
  • Verify there are no regressions in existing streamingExecutor tests as part of the test plan.
| `src/store/chat/agents/__tests__/createAgentExecutors/compress-context.test.ts` | ### Possibly linked issues - **#12888**: PR fixes empty/failed compression summaries in multi-agent chats that caused history loss, matching the reported bug behavior. - **#**: PR fixes faulty context compression and threshold logic that cause long histories to be sent and hit token limits. ---

body:
Hi! Pushed fixes addressing the review feedback:

- **File ID bug** (Codex P1): Fixed — post-upload status dispatches now use `fileResult.id` (server ID) instead of `file.name`, which was already swapped by `uploadWithProgress`
- **Test mocks**: Updated `chat.test.ts` mocks from `isDesktopLocalStaticServerUrl` to `isLocalOrPrivateUrl` to match the code change (this was causing the CI test failure)
- **SSRF documentation**: Added a code comment explaining that server-side private URL conversion requires `SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IP_ADDRESS=1` for self-hosted deployments

@JC-lurker Good question! This is specifically about **image URLs in chat messages sent to LLM providers** (e.g. OpenAI Vision). When images are hosted on a private MinIO instance (192.168.x.x), the LLM provider can't reach that URL. This PR converts those private URLs to base64 inline before sending. Document attachments go through a different RAG pipeline. Making S3 public works too, but this approach keeps the storage private.

Would love a maintainer review — this is important for self-hosted deployments with private object storage. Thanks!
author: ghost

## Reviewer's Guide Rebrands the application from LobeHub/LobeChat to Pictura AI, updating branding constants, URLs, social links, copy, and removing GitHub- and community-centric UI elements that no longer apply. #### Class diagram for updated PicturaAI branding and URL configuration ```mermaid classDiagram class BrandingConst { +string LOBE_CHAT_CLOUD = "Pictura AI Cloud" +string BRANDING_NAME = "Pictura AI" +string BRANDING_LOGO_URL = "/images/pictura-icon.svg" +string ORG_NAME = "Pictura AI" +BrandingUrl BRANDING_URL +SocialUrl SOCIAL_URL +BrandingEmail BRANDING_EMAIL +string BRANDING_PROVIDER = "picturaai" +string COPYRIGHT +string COPYRIGHT_FULL } class BrandingUrl { +string help +string pricing +string download +string blog } class SocialUrl { +string telegram = "https://t.me/picturaai_bot" +string x = "https://x.com/GetPicturaAI" } class BrandingEmail { +string business = "info@picturaai.sbs" +string support = "support@picturaai.sbs" } class UrlConst { +string OFFICIAL_URL = "https://picturaai.sbs" +string OFFICIAL_SITE = "https://picturaai.sbs" +string OFFICIAL_DOMAIN = "picturaai.sbs" +string OG_URL = "/og/og.webp?v=1" +string GITHUB = "" +string GITHUB_ISSUES = "" +string CHANGELOG = "https://picturaai.sbs/changelog" +string DOCUMENTS +string USAGE_DOCUMENTS +string SELF_HOSTING_DOCUMENTS +string MANUAL_UPGRADE_URL +string BLOG +string ABOUT +string FEEDBACK = "" +string PRIVACY_URL +string TERMS_URL +string PLUGINS_INDEX_URL = "https://picturaai.sbs/plugins" +string MORE_MODEL_PROVIDER_REQUEST_URL = "" +string MORE_FILE_PREVIEW_REQUEST_URL = "" +string AGENTS_INDEX_GITHUB = "" +string AGENTS_INDEX_GITHUB_ISSUE = "" +string AGENTS_OFFICIAL_URL = "https://picturaai.sbs/agent" +string LOBE_URL_IMPORT_NAME = "settings" +string RELEASES_URL = undefined +string AES_GCM_URL +string BASE_PROVIDER_DOC_URL = "https://picturaai.sbs/docs/usage/providers" +string SITEMAP_BASE_URL +string CHANGELOG_URL +DownloadUrl DOWNLOAD_URL } class DownloadUrl { +string android = undefined +string ios = undefined +string default = undefined } class Meta { +generate(options) } class Ld { +genOrganization() } class AppVariantsMetadata { +generateMetadata(props) } class MdxLink { +A(href, children, props) -EXTERNAL_HREF_REGEX } class FollowFeature { +Follow() } class AboutFeature { +About(mobile) } class HomeFooter { +Footer() } class UserPanelMenuHook { +useMenu() } BrandingConst --> BrandingUrl : has BrandingConst --> SocialUrl : has BrandingConst --> BrandingEmail : has UrlConst --> DownloadUrl : has Meta --> UrlConst : uses Meta --> BrandingConst : uses ORG_NAME Ld --> UrlConst : uses OFFICIAL_URL, OFFICIAL_SITE Ld --> BrandingConst : uses SOCIAL_URL AppVariantsMetadata --> UrlConst : uses OG_URL AppVariantsMetadata --> BrandingConst : uses BRANDING_NAME, ORG_NAME MdxLink --> UrlConst : uses OG_URL (indirectly via routing) FollowFeature --> BrandingConst : uses SOCIAL_URL AboutFeature --> BrandingConst : uses SOCIAL_URL HomeFooter --> UrlConst : uses DOCUMENTS_REFER_URL HomeFooter --> BrandingConst : uses BRANDING_NAME (via translations) UserPanelMenuHook --> UrlConst : previously used DOWNLOAD_URL (now inactive) ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Simplified home footer by removing Product Hunt, GitHub, Discord, and feedback integrations while keeping changelog and dev-only Evaluation Lab entry. |
  • Removed Product Hunt promotion card state/logic and related analytics tracking
  • Removed feedback modal entry and Discord link from help menu
  • Removed conditional GitHub menu item and GitHub-related imports
  • Changed dev-mode menu icon for Evaluation Lab to use Settings2 and simplified help menu dependencies

  • Deleted GitHub star/feedback footer UI and related modals from settings footer
  • Replaced footer component implementation with a null-returning memoized component and kept exported class name for layout compatibility
| `src/features/Setting/Footer.tsx` | | Retargeted core URLs and feature links from lobehub/lobechat domains and GitHub resources to picturaai.sbs or disabled them where not applicable. |

  • Blanked GitHub/feedback-related URLs and request/issue links that are no longer valid
  • Disabled mobile/desktop download links and releases URL by setting them to undefined or empty strings
| `packages/const/src/url.ts` | | Updated branding and social constants to Pictura AI, including names, logo, emails, and social handles, and wired a custom logo asset. |

  • Set BRANDING_LOGO_URL to a new pictura icon SVG and added the asset under public/images

  • Updated support emails in discover/subscription locales to support@picturaai.sbs
  • Replaced occurrences of LobeHub/Lobe AI/LobeHub Cloud with Pictura AI or Pictura AI Cloud across discover, desktop-onboarding, file, image, oauth, subscription, and setting locales
  • Adjusted phrases referencing LobeHub-specific markets/skills/badges/tooltips to refer to Pictura AI equivalents

## Reviewer's Guide Adds New Relic as an opt-in analytics provider by wiring the Node.js APM agent into Next.js instrumentation and introducing a client-side Browser RUM component, controlled via new environment variables and Docker defaults, alongside registering the provider in the existing analytics framework. #### Sequence diagram for New Relic browser analytics on page load ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UserBrowser participant NextPage as NextPageComponent participant Analytics as AnalyticsRoot participant NRBrowser as NewRelicBrowser participant NRScript as NRBrowserScript participant NRBackend as NewRelicBrowserBackend UserBrowser->>NextPage: Request page NextPage->>Analytics: Render Analytics Analytics->>Analytics: Read analyticsEnv Analytics->>Analytics: Check ENABLED_NEW_RELIC_ANALYTICS alt New Relic browser enabled Analytics->>NRBrowser: Render with accountId, applicationId, licenseKey NRBrowser->>NRBrowser: Sanitize values NRBrowser->>NRBrowser: Validate non empty safe values NRBrowser->>NRScript: Create inline config snippet NRScript-->>UserBrowser: Inject beforeInteractive script UserBrowser->>NRBackend: Send RUM data using snippet config else New Relic browser disabled Analytics-->>NextPage: Skip NRBrowser render end NextPage-->>UserBrowser: Return final HTML and scripts ``` #### Class diagram for New Relic analytics components and env config ```mermaid classDiagram class AnalyticsEnvConfig { boolean ENABLED_NEW_RELIC_ANALYTICS string NEW_RELIC_BROWSER_ACCOUNT_ID string NEW_RELIC_BROWSER_APPLICATION_ID string NEW_RELIC_BROWSER_LICENSE_KEY getAnalyticsConfig() } class NewRelicBrowserProps { string accountId string applicationId string licenseKey } class NewRelicBrowser { +render(props NewRelicBrowserProps) -sanitize(value string) string } class AnalyticsRoot { +render() } AnalyticsRoot --> AnalyticsEnvConfig : uses AnalyticsRoot --> NewRelicBrowser : renders NewRelicBrowser ..|> NewRelicBrowserProps : receives props ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce New Relic browser analytics configuration in the shared analytics env schema and wire it into the runtime config. |
  • Extend the Zod schema with New Relic browser-related fields, including a derived boolean flag for enabling analytics.
  • Map New Relic browser env vars from process.env into the runtime analytics config, auto-enabling when a license key is present.
| `src/envs/analytics.ts` | | Expose New Relic APM and Browser env vars in the Docker image configuration. |
  • Add server-side New Relic APM env vars with sensible defaults for app name, config-file disabling, and log level.
  • Add New Relic Browser RUM env vars for account ID, application ID, and license key to the Docker ENV block.
| `Dockerfile` | | Register New Relic as a browser analytics provider in the React analytics entrypoint. |
  • Dynamically import the new New Relic analytics component using next/dynamic.
  • Render the New Relic component only when the ENABLED_NEW_RELIC_ANALYTICS flag is true, passing through the required IDs and license key from env config.
| `src/components/Analytics/index.tsx` | | Implement the client-side New Relic Browser RUM component that injects the configuration snippet safely. |
  • Create a client component that accepts accountId, applicationId, and licenseKey props and sanitizes them before use.
  • Construct the New Relic NREUM init/info/loader_config snippet with sanitized values, and inject it via next/script with beforeInteractive strategy.
  • Guard rendering so that if any sanitized value is empty, the component returns null (no script injection).
| `src/components/Analytics/NewRelic.tsx` | | Add New Relic Node.js APM agent configuration and runtime loading via Next.js instrumentation. |
  • Create a root-level newrelic.js config file that reads app name, license key, and log level from env vars and enables distributed tracing.
  • Add a dedicated instrumentation.newrelic module that conditionally requires the newrelic package when enabled and a license key is present.
  • Update the main instrumentation entrypoint to import the New Relic instrumentation only when running on the nodejs runtime and NEW_RELIC_ENABLED is true, before other telemetry gating.
| `newrelic.js`
`src/instrumentation.newrelic.ts`
`src/instrumentation.ts` | | Wire New Relic dependency into the project and adjust workspace dependency ordering. |
  • Add the newrelic npm package as a production dependency with a pinned semver version.
  • Slightly reorder two internal workspace dependencies without changing their versions.
| `package.json` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide This PR translates existing non-English (Chinese) comments and JSDoc blocks into English across several OpenAPI service files and the RBAC utility, without modifying any runtime logic or behavior. ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Translate shared BaseService permission and error-handling comments to English while preserving structure and intent. |
  • Updated JSDoc for error handling, permission checks, and resource ownership helpers to English while keeping parameter lists and return descriptions aligned with implementations.
  • Translated inline comments in permission resolution flows (single and batch operations) to clarify ALL vs owner permission semantics and logging behavior.
  • Clarified chat-permission aggregation JSDoc to enumerate required permissions in English.
| `packages/openapi/src/common/base.service.ts` | | Translate user service JSDoc and inline comments to English for CRUD, role, and query operations. |
  • Converted class-level and method-level JSDoc (getCurrentUser, queryUsers, create/update/delete user, role operations) to English, preserving tags and types.
  • Updated explanatory comments about concurrency (Promise.all), uniqueness checks, and RBAC interactions to English.
  • Ensured terminology consistency for "user info", "roles", and "message count" across the service.
| `packages/openapi/src/services/user.service.ts` | | Translate Agent service documentation and inline comments to English, clarifying CRUD and migration behaviors. |
  • Rewrote class and method JSDoc for querying, creating, updating, deleting, and fetching agents in English.
  • Clarified comments around permission checks, partial updates, params merging, and virtual-agent filtering.
  • Documented agent-session migration steps (read, delete+insert, uniqueness constraints) in English while leaving SQL/transaction logic unchanged.
| `packages/openapi/src/services/agent.service.ts` | | Translate Role service comments to English to better describe RBAC role and permission management. |
  • Updated permission-check comments to English for role/permission list, detail, and update endpoints.
  • Clarified comments around building list and count queries, and around conflict resolution between grant/revoke permission sets.
  • Translated checks for system roles and role existence, and comments for clearing role permissions, without altering query logic.
| `packages/openapi/src/services/role.service.ts` | | Translate Model service comments to English for model listing, detail, and mutation endpoints. |
  • Updated class-level description to explain Hono-API-specific model service responsibilities in English.
  • Translated comments for permission validation, query-condition construction, pagination, and parallel querying.
  • Renamed JSDoc descriptions for getModels, getModelDetail, createModel, and updateModel to English while keeping signatures intact.
| `packages/openapi/src/services/model.service.ts` | | Translate RBAC utility comments to English to clarify scope-permission helpers. |
  • Updated JSDoc for getAllScopePermissions and getScopePermissions to English, describing purpose, parameters, and return values.
  • Translated inline comments about allowed scopes and filtering of disallowed scopes, keeping the underlying RBAC_PERMISSIONS usage unchanged.
| `src/utils/rbac.ts` | ---

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Sets explicit no-cache headers on the SPA HTML entry route so clients always revalidate the HTML shell while continuing to rely on hashed JS/CSS assets for caching. #### Sequence diagram for SPA HTML request with no-cache header ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant Browser participant BrowserCache as Browser_Cache participant Server participant SpaRoute as Spa_HTML_Route User->>Browser: Navigate to SPA URL Browser->>BrowserCache: Lookup cached SPA HTML alt Cached copy exists BrowserCache-->>Browser: Return cached HTML + headers Browser->>Server: Conditional GET /spa with If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since else No cached copy Browser->>Server: GET /spa end Server->>SpaRoute: Invoke GET handler SpaRoute-->>Server: Response(html, headers{Cache-Control: no-cache}) Server-->>Browser: 200 OK HTML with Cache-Control: no-cache Browser->>BrowserCache: Store HTML with revalidation required Browser->>Server: Request hashed JS/CSS assets Server-->>Browser: 200 OK assets with long-lived caching Browser-->>User: Render updated SPA UI ``` #### Flow diagram for SPA HTML caching behavior with no-cache header ```mermaid flowchart TD A[User opens SPA URL] --> B[Browser checks cache for SPA HTML] B -->|Cache hit| C[Use cached HTML metadata] C --> D[Send conditional GET to server] B -->|Cache miss| E[Send normal GET to server] D --> F[Server SPA route handler] E --> F[Server SPA route handler] F --> G[Generate HTML response] G --> H[Set header Cache-Control: no-cache] H --> I[Return HTML to browser] I --> J[Browser stores HTML but always revalidates] J --> K[Browser requests hashed JS/CSS assets] K --> L[Assets served with long-lived caching] L --> M[SPA renders with latest code] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Ensure SPA HTML shell is never served stale by explicitly disabling caching on the HTML response while leaving asset caching behavior unchanged. |

regeneration logic, and normalizes markdown export content (including think tags) consistently across topic and message flows. #### Sequence diagram for PDF generation and regeneration flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant SharePdf participant UsePdfGenerationHook participant ExportPdfMutation participant ExporterService User->>SharePdf: click GeneratePDF SharePdf->>UsePdfGenerationHook: call generatePdf(content, sessionId, title, topicId) alt exportPdfMutation isPending UsePdfGenerationHook-->>SharePdf: return (ignore request) else not pending UsePdfGenerationHook->>UsePdfGenerationHook: setError(null) UsePdfGenerationHook->>UsePdfGenerationHook: setPdfData(null) UsePdfGenerationHook->>ExportPdfMutation: mutateAsync(content, sessionId, title, topicId) ExportPdfMutation->>ExporterService: exportPdf(content, sessionId, title, topicId) ExporterService-->>ExportPdfMutation: pdf, filename ExportPdfMutation-->>UsePdfGenerationHook: result UsePdfGenerationHook->>UsePdfGenerationHook: setPdfData(result.pdf) UsePdfGenerationHook->>UsePdfGenerationHook: setFilename(result.filename) end Note over User,UsePdfGenerationHook: User can now click RegeneratePDF even with same parameters User->>SharePdf: click RegeneratePDF SharePdf->>UsePdfGenerationHook: call generatePdf(content, sessionId, title, topicId) alt exportPdfMutation isPending UsePdfGenerationHook-->>SharePdf: return (ignore while in flight) else not pending UsePdfGenerationHook->>ExportPdfMutation: mutateAsync(content, sessionId, title, topicId) ExportPdfMutation->>ExporterService: exportPdf(content, sessionId, title, topicId) ExporterService-->>ExportPdfMutation: pdf, filename ExportPdfMutation-->>UsePdfGenerationHook: result UsePdfGenerationHook->>UsePdfGenerationHook: setPdfData(result.pdf) UsePdfGenerationHook->>UsePdfGenerationHook: setFilename(result.filename) end ``` #### Sequence diagram for single message share modal with PDF context ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ShareMessageModal participant ShareDataProvider participant SharePdf participant UsePdfGenerationHook User->>ShareMessageModal: open(message) ShareMessageModal->>ShareMessageModal: useConversationStore getContext ShareMessageModal->>User: show tabs Image, Text, Pdf User->>ShareMessageModal: select Pdf tab ShareMessageModal->>ShareDataProvider: render ShareDataProvider(context) ShareDataProvider->>SharePdf: render SharePdf(message) with context SharePdf->>UsePdfGenerationHook: init usePdfGeneration User->>SharePdf: click GeneratePDF SharePdf->>UsePdfGenerationHook: generatePdf(params) UsePdfGenerationHook->>UsePdfGenerationHook: request PDF as in generation flow ``` #### Updated class diagram imageType, widthMode, withBackground, withFooter) } class FieldType { +imageType ImageType +widthMode WidthMode +withBackground boolean +withFooter boolean } class WidthMode { <> +Wide +Narrow } class WidthMode +render() } class UsePdfGenerationHook { +pdfData string +filename string +error string +loading boolean +generatePdf(content, sessionId, title, topicId) +downloadPdf() +resetPdf() } class Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Removes an unnecessary nested MemoryRouter from the Skill Store modal, wraps the global ErrorBoundary render output in a ThemeProvider, and adjusts the Error page layout height to use viewport-relative units to prevent crashes or blank screens in the skill store flow. #### Sequence diagram for ErrorBoundary rendering with ThemeProvider ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AppRoot participant ErrorBoundary participant ThemeProvider participant ErrorCapture AppRoot->>ErrorBoundary: render_with_error(error) ErrorBoundary->>ErrorBoundary: notifyChunkError() ErrorBoundary->>ThemeProvider: render_theme(theme cssVar.key=lobe-vars) ThemeProvider->>ErrorCapture: render(error, reset) ErrorCapture-->>ThemeProvider: error_ui_via_Flexbox ThemeProvider-->>AppRoot: themed_error_ui ``` #### Class diagram for SkillStore modal and error handling components ```mermaid classDiagram direction LR class SkillStoreModal { +createSkillStoreModal() } class MarketAuthProvider { +isDesktop boolean } class SkillStoreContent class ErrorBoundary { +error Error +resetPath string } class ErrorCapture { +error Error +reset() void } class ThemeProvider { +theme object } SkillStoreModal --> MarketAuthProvider : wraps MarketAuthProvider --> SkillStoreContent : renders ErrorBoundary --> ThemeProvider : wraps_on_render ThemeProvider --> ErrorCapture : renders ErrorBoundary --> ErrorCapture : passes_error_and_reset ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Simplify Skill Store modal routing context to avoid nested MemoryRouter issues. |
  • Removed the MemoryRouter wrapper around the SkillStoreContent component within the Skill Store modal configuration.
  • Kept MarketAuthProvider as the sole wrapper for SkillStoreContent to rely on the existing router context instead of a nested in-memory router.
| `src/features/SkillStore/index.tsx` | | Ensure error boundary UI is rendered within a theme context. |
  • Wrapped the ErrorCapture component returned by ErrorBoundary in a ThemeProvider with the lobe-vars CSS variable configuration.
  • Replaced the createElement call with JSX syntax for clarity and to support the ThemeProvider wrapper.
| `src/utils/router.tsx` | | Stabilize error page layout height to cover the full viewport on all devices. |
  • Updated the Flexbox style in ErrorCapture from minHeight: 100% to minHeight: 100dvh to better match the viewport height and prevent layout issues when errors occur.
| `src/components/Error/index.tsx` |
---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. ## Reviewer's Guide Refines the model switch panel’s list interactions to properly control the model detail popup, prevent unwanted navigation/scroll behavior, and simplify model change handling by making it synchronous and scroll-aware. #### Sequence diagram for model selection and detail popup behavior ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ModelSwitchPanel participant List participant ListItemRenderer participant usePanelHandlers participant AgentStore User->>ModelSwitchPanel: Open model switch panel ModelSwitchPanel->>List: Render list with listItems List->>ListItemRenderer: Render item with onClose, onModelChange, scrollCount User->>ListItemRenderer: Click model item (unrestricted) activate ListItemRenderer ListItemRenderer->>ListItemRenderer: onClick handler ListItemRenderer->>ListItemRenderer: event.preventDefault() ListItemRenderer->>ListItemRenderer: setDetailOpen(false) ListItemRenderer->>List: onClose() deactivate ListItemRenderer List->>usePanelHandlers: handleModelChange(modelId, providerId) activate usePanelHandlers usePanelHandlers->>usePanelHandlers: setTimeout(callback) usePanelHandlers-->>AgentStore: callback -> updateAgentConfig(modelId, providerId) deactivate usePanelHandlers AgentStore-->>ModelSwitchPanel: State updated with new model ModelSwitchPanel-->>User: Panel re-renders with selected model active ``` #### Sequence diagram for scrolling closing the model detail popup ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant List participant ListItemRenderer User->>List: Scroll model list activate List List->>List: handleListScroll() List->>List: setScrollCount(c + 1) List-->>ListItemRenderer: Rerender with updated scrollCount prop deactivate List activate ListItemRenderer ListItemRenderer->>ListItemRenderer: useEffect on scrollCount change ListItemRenderer->>ListItemRenderer: setDetailOpen(false) deactivate ListItemRenderer ListItemRenderer-->>User: Detail popup is closed during scrolling ``` #### Class diagram for updated ModelSwitchPanel list components ```mermaid classDiagram class List { +number panelHeight +number activeKey +string newLabel +string proLabel +function handleModelChange(modelId, providerId) +function handleClose() +function handleListScroll() -number scrollCount } class ListItemRendererProps { +ListItem item +string newLabel +function onClose() +function onModelChange(modelId, providerId) +function onRestrictedModelClick() +string proLabel +number scrollCount } class ListItemRenderer { +ListItemRendererProps props -boolean detailOpen +function render() +function handleClickUnrestricted(modelId, providerId) +function handleClickRestricted() +function handleSubmenuOpenChange(open) +function useEffectOnScrollCount(scrollCount) } class usePanelHandlers { +function handleModelChange(modelId, providerId) } class AgentStore { +function updateAgentConfig(modelId, providerId) } List --> ListItemRendererProps : creates props for ListItemRendererProps --> ListItemRenderer : instantiated as props List --> ListItemRenderer : renders many List --> usePanelHandlers : uses usePanelHandlers --> AgentStore : calls updateAgentConfig ListItemRenderer --> usePanelHandlers : calls onModelChange via prop List --> ListItemRendererProps : passes scrollCount to ListItemRenderer --> ListItemRenderer : uses scrollCount to reset detailOpen ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Make model selection handler synchronous and adjust call order around panel closing. |
  • Change onModelChange type from returning a Promise to a synchronous void function in list item props and handler hook
  • Update model selection click handlers to call onClose before onModelChange to avoid popup flash and to better coordinate UI updates
  • Remove unnecessary async/await from click handlers and the model change hook
| `src/features/ModelSwitchPanel/components/List/ListItemRenderer.tsx`
`src/features/ModelSwitchPanel/hooks/usePanelHandlers.ts` | | Rework list item rendering to use dropdown submenu triggers for model entries and control the detail popup lifecycle. |
  • Wrap previously clickable Block-based list items in DropdownMenuSubmenuRoot/Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Popup to drive the ModelDetailPanel display
  • Ensure click handlers prevent default menu behavior, close the detail popup, and correctly branch on restricted vs unrestricted models
  • Render ModelDetailPanel with appropriate model/provider IDs for both single-provider and multi-provider entries with adjusted side offsets
| `src/features/ModelSwitchPanel/components/List/ListItemRenderer.tsx` | | Reset detail popup state when the list scrolls to avoid stale popups and improve scroll behavior. |
  • Add scrollCount state to the list component and increment it on scroll events
  • Pass scrollCount down to ListItemRenderer and use a useEffect hook to close the detail popup whenever scrollCount changes
  • Attach onScroll handler to the list Flexbox container
| `src/features/ModelSwitchPanel/components/List/index.tsx`
`src/features/ModelSwitchPanel/components/List/ListItemRenderer.tsx` | | Adjust styling for the model switch panel to improve usability and prevent unwanted selection/overscroll. |
  • Increase the detail popup width and disable user selection to make the content more readable and stable
  • Set overscroll-behavior: contain on the detail popup and the list to prevent scroll chaining outside the panel
  • Disable text selection on the dropdown menu and remove outline from the trigger for a cleaner interaction

## Reviewer's Guide Implements a generic hook system on ModelRuntime to allow pre/post chat lifecycle interception (e.g., billing/tracing), plumbs hook injection from business logic into runtime initialization, and adds metadata propagation from executors to the chat call. #### Sequence diagram for ModelRuntime initialization with business hooks ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant ChatService participant BusinessHooksModule participant InitModelRuntimeModule participant ModelRuntime ChatService->>BusinessHooksModule: getBusinessModelRuntimeHooks(userId, provider) BusinessHooksModule-->>ChatService: hooks ChatService->>InitModelRuntimeModule: initModelRuntimeWithUserPayload(provider, payload, params, hooks) alt runtimeProvider is vertex InitModelRuntimeModule->>ModelRuntime: new ModelRuntime(runtime, hooks) ModelRuntime-->>InitModelRuntimeModule: modelRuntime else other provider InitModelRuntimeModule->>ModelRuntime: initializeWithProvider(runtimeProvider, params, hooks) ModelRuntime-->>InitModelRuntimeModule: modelRuntime end InitModelRuntimeModule-->>ChatService: modelRuntime ``` #### Sequence diagram for ModelRuntime.chat lifecycle with hooks and metadata ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant RuntimeExecutors participant ModelRuntime participant LobeRuntimeAI participant Hooks as ModelRuntimeHooks RuntimeExecutors->>ModelRuntime: chat(payload, options{metadata:{operationId,topicId}}) ModelRuntime->>Hooks: beforeChat(payload, options) Hooks-->>ModelRuntime: resolved ModelRuntime->>ModelRuntime: merge onChatFinal into options.callback.onFinal ModelRuntime->>LobeRuntimeAI: chat(payload, finalOptions) LobeRuntimeAI-->>ModelRuntime: stream events LobeRuntimeAI-->>ModelRuntime: final data ModelRuntime->>Hooks: onChatFinal(data, {options, payload}) Hooks-->>ModelRuntime: resolved ModelRuntime-->>RuntimeExecutors: stream completion ``` #### Class diagram for ModelRuntime hooks and chat options ```mermaid classDiagram class ModelRuntimeHooks { +beforeChat(payload: ChatStreamPayload, options: ChatMethodOptions) Promise~void~ +onChatFinal(data: OnFinishData, context: OnChatFinalContext) void } class OnChatFinalContext { +options: ChatMethodOptions +payload: ChatStreamPayload } class ChatMethodOptions { +metadata: Record~string, unknown~ } class ModelRuntime { -_runtime: LobeRuntimeAI -_hooks: ModelRuntimeHooks +ModelRuntime(runtime: LobeRuntimeAI, hooks: ModelRuntimeHooks) +chat(payload: ChatStreamPayload, options: ChatMethodOptions) Promise~any~ +initializeWithProvider(provider: string, params: ProviderInitParams, hooks: ModelRuntimeHooks) ModelRuntime } class ProviderInitParams { +apiKey: string +apiVersion: string +baseURL: string } class BusinessHooksModule { +getBusinessModelRuntimeHooks(userId: string, provider: string) ModelRuntimeHooks } class InitModelRuntimeModule { +initModelRuntimeWithUserPayload(provider: string, payload: ClientSecretPayload, params: any, hooks: ModelRuntimeHooks) ModelRuntime +initModelRuntimeFromDB(userId: string, provider: string) ModelRuntime } ModelRuntime --> ModelRuntimeHooks : uses ModelRuntime --> ChatMethodOptions : uses ModelRuntimeHooks --> OnChatFinalContext : uses InitModelRuntimeModule --> ModelRuntime : creates InitModelRuntimeModule --> BusinessHooksModule : calls BusinessHooksModule --> ModelRuntimeHooks : returns ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add a hooks mechanism to ModelRuntime for chat lifecycle interception and propagate metadata into hook context. |
  • Introduce ModelRuntimeHooks interface with beforeChat and onChatFinal hooks using OnFinishData context.
  • Extend ModelRuntime to store optional hooks, run beforeChat prior to the underlying runtime.chat call, and merge onChatFinal into the onFinal callback using mergeMultipleChatMethodOptions.
  • Update ModelRuntime.initializeWithProvider and ModelRuntime constructor to accept and pass through hooks.
  • Extend ChatMethodOptions with a metadata field for passing billing/tracing context from callers into hooks.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/ModelRuntime.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/types/chat.ts` | | Wire hooks into runtime initialization paths and business layer so cloud can inject billing logic. |
  • Update initModelRuntimeWithUserPayload to accept hooks and forward them when constructing ModelRuntime instances for both Vertex and non-Vertex providers.
  • Update initModelRuntimeFromDB to obtain hooks from business logic and pass them into initModelRuntimeWithUserPayload.
  • Update ChatService to retrieve business hooks per user/provider and pass them into initModelRuntimeWithUserPayload when building modelRuntime.
  • Add a business stub getBusinessModelRuntimeHooks that returns undefined in OSS and re-export ModelRuntimeHooks from the model-runtime package for use by business code.
| `src/server/modules/ModelRuntime/index.ts`
`packages/openapi/src/services/chat.service.ts`
`src/business/server/model-runtime.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/index.ts` | | Propagate operation/topic metadata from runtime executors into chat call options for use by hooks. |
  • Extend RuntimeExecutors chat invocation to populate ChatMethodOptions.metadata with operationId and topicId from execution state.
| `src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide This PR fixes memory enablement precedence so that agent-level configuration overrides user settings across backend execution, frontend UI toggles, and client tool selection, and adds integration tests plus a small docs tweak for migration changelog authorship. #### Sequence diagram for backend memory enablement precedence in execAgent ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant Frontend as FrontendChatInput participant AiService as AiAgentService participant UserModel User->>Frontend: Send_message_with_agentId Frontend->>AiService: execAgent(agentConfig,userId) AiService->>AiService: agentMemoryEnabled = agentConfig.chatConfig.memory.enabled AiService->>UserModel: getUserSettings() UserModel-->>AiService: settings AiService->>AiService: userMemoryEnabled = settings.memory.enabled !== false AiService->>AiService: globalMemoryEnabled = agentMemoryEnabled ?? userMemoryEnabled AiService-->>Frontend: Response_with_or_without_memory_tools Frontend-->>User: Display_tools_based_on_globalMemoryEnabled ``` #### Flow diagram for effective memory enabled resolution across agent and user settings ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start_determine_memory_enabled] --> B{agentMemoryEnabled_is_defined?} B -->|yes| C[Use_agentMemoryEnabled] C --> Z[Effective_memory_enabled_result] B -->|no| D{User_memory_enabled_flag_is_false?} D -->|yes| E[Use_false_from_user_settings] E --> Z D -->|no| F[Fallback_to_true_default] F --> Z subgraph Frontend_hook_useMemoryEnabled A1[Read_agent_memory_from_agent_store] A2[Read_user_memory_from_user_store] A1 --> B A2 --> D end subgraph Tool_engine_memory_manifest_toggle T1[Read_current_agent_chat_config] T2[Read_user_memory_from_store] T1 --> B T2 --> D end subgraph Backend_execAgent_globalMemoryEnabled S1[Read_agent_chatConfig_memory_enabled] S2[getUserSettings_and_memory_enabled] S1 --> B S2 --> D end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Apply agent-over-user precedence for memory enablement in execAgent backend service. |
  • Derive agentMemoryEnabled from agentConfig.chatConfig?.memory?.enabled
  • Initialize globalMemoryEnabled from agentMemoryEnabled with a default of false
  • Load user settings and compute memorySettings?.enabled !== false for default user behavior
  • Set globalMemoryEnabled using agentMemoryEnabled when defined, otherwise fall back to user memory setting
| `src/server/services/aiAgent/index.ts` | | Unify frontend memory enabled state via a reusable hook that mirrors backend precedence logic. |
  • Introduce useMemoryEnabled hook that returns agent memory enabled when defined, otherwise user-level memory setting
  • Refactor Memory Controls and parent Memory component to use useMemoryEnabled instead of direct selectors
  • Keep effort level selection bound only to agent chat config while enable/disable reflects combined state
| `src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/Memory/useMemoryEnabled.ts`
`src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/Memory/Controls.tsx`
`src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/Memory/index.tsx` | | Align client-side tool engine memory tool enablement with new precedence logic and update unit test mocks. |
  • Use agentChatConfigSelectors.currentChatConfig(agentState).memory?.enabled as primary source of memory flag
  • Fallback to settingsSelectors.memoryEnabled from useUserStore when agent config is undefined
  • Mock agentChatConfigSelectors.currentChatConfig and user settings stores in toolEngineering tests to match new logic
| `src/helpers/toolEngineering/index.ts`
`src/helpers/toolEngineering/index.test.ts` | | Add integration tests to verify memory precedence behavior end-to-end using the real database and OpenAI response mocking. |
  • Set up Vitest environment with in-memory DB, test user lifecycle helpers, and OpenAI Responses.create spy
  • Implement helper to upsert user memory settings in userSettings table
  • Add four execAgent scenarios covering agent=false/user=true, agent=true/user=false, agent missing with user=false, and both missing (default enabled)
  • Assert presence or absence of memory tools in OpenAI Responses.create call arguments
| `src/server/services/aiAgent/__tests__/execAgent.memory.test.ts` | | Clarify documentation around assigning migration owner based on actual PR author for release-related agents. |
  • Replace escaped username placeholder with GitHub-style @{pr-author} in db migration changelog example
  • Add explicit instruction in patch-release scenarios doc to derive migration owner from PR author via gh or git, never hardcoding a username
  • Add note to Claude within docs to automatically replace {pr-author} using repository metadata
| `.agents/skills/version-release/reference/changelog-example/db-migration.md`
`.agents/skills/version-release/reference/patch-release-scenarios.md` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Ensures builtin tool invocations always return a structured error object instead of undefined when no executor is found, and adds a defensive fallback in the call_tool executor to handle null/undefined tool results gracefully so the agent loop can continue. #### Sequence diagram for updated builtin tool invocation error handling ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AgentLoop participant CallToolExecutor participant PluginTypesActionImpl participant BuiltinToolRegistry participant Context AgentLoop->>CallToolExecutor: executeTool(toolName, payload) CallToolExecutor->>PluginTypesActionImpl: invokeBuiltinTool(payload) PluginTypesActionImpl->>BuiltinToolRegistry: findExecutor(identifier, apiName) alt executor_found BuiltinToolRegistry-->>PluginTypesActionImpl: executor PluginTypesActionImpl->>BuiltinToolRegistry: executeTool(payload) BuiltinToolRegistry-->>PluginTypesActionImpl: resultOrError PluginTypesActionImpl-->>CallToolExecutor: resultOrError else executor_not_found BuiltinToolRegistry-->>PluginTypesActionImpl: null PluginTypesActionImpl-->>CallToolExecutor: ToolResult { content, error type ToolNotFound, success false } end alt result_is_undefined_or_null CallToolExecutor->>Context: failOperation(toolOperationId, ToolExecutionError) CallToolExecutor-->>AgentLoop: events with fallback ToolResult { content, error type ToolExecutionError, success false } else result_is_defined CallToolExecutor-->>AgentLoop: events with result end AgentLoop->>AgentLoop: continue loop with updated messages ``` #### Class diagram for updated tool invocation result handling ```mermaid classDiagram class PluginTypesActionImpl { +invokeBuiltinTool(payload) ToolResult +invokeDefaultTypePlugin(id, payload) string } class ToolResult { +string content +ToolError error +boolean success } class ToolError { +string type +string message } class CallToolExecutor { +executeTool(toolName, payload, toolOperationId, chatToolPayload, state, context) ToolResult } PluginTypesActionImpl ..> ToolResult : returns PluginTypesActionImpl ..> ToolError : creates CallToolExecutor ..> ToolResult : consumes_and_may_create_fallback ToolResult o--> ToolError : has ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Return a structured error result from builtin tool invocation when no executor is found instead of returning undefined. |
  • Log when no executor is found for a builtin tool remains, but the function now returns a non-success result object instead of undefined.
  • The returned object includes a human-readable content string indicating the tool is not available.
  • The error field is populated with a ToolNotFound error type and message, and success is explicitly set to false.
| `src/store/chat/slices/plugin/actions/pluginTypes.ts` | | Add a defensive fallback in the call_tool executor to handle undefined or null tool execution results and surface a meaningful error to the agent loop. |
  • Before checking success, short-circuit when the tool result is undefined or null and synthesize a fallback error result object with content, error, and success: false.
  • If a toolOperationId exists, mark the operation as failed with a ToolExecutionError and an appropriate message.
  • Push a tool_result event with the fallback result and return updated agent state using the latest messages from dbMessagesMap without proceeding to normal result handling.
| `src/store/chat/agents/createAgentExecutors.ts` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Plumbs skill metadata from operation creation through the runtime and context engineering layers so that all installed skills (not just enabled plugins) are injected into the system prompt, enabling AI-side discovery and activation via activateSkill. #### Sequence diagram for skillMetas and skillsConfig propagation to context engineering ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant AiAgentService participant AgentRuntimeService participant RuntimeExecutors participant ServerMessagesEngine participant ContextEngineering Client->>AiAgentService: startOperation AiAgentService->>AiAgentService: build skillMetas from lobehubSkillManifests AiAgentService->>AgentRuntimeService: createOperation(skillMetas) AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: store skillMetas in operation metadata Client->>RuntimeExecutors: execute operation RuntimeExecutors->>RuntimeExecutors: read state.metadata.skillMetas RuntimeExecutors->>RuntimeExecutors: build skillsConfig.enabledSkills from skillMetas RuntimeExecutors->>ServerMessagesEngine: serverMessagesEngine(skillsConfig) ServerMessagesEngine->>ServerMessagesEngine: include skillsConfig when present ServerMessagesEngine->>ContextEngineering: invoke contextEngineering(skillsConfig) ContextEngineering->>ContextEngineering: inject enabledSkills into available_skills in system prompt ContextEngineering-->>Client: AI can discover and activate installed skills ``` #### Updated class diagram for skillMetas and skillsConfig plumbing ```mermaid classDiagram class OperationCreationParams { +string operationId +number maxSteps +any modelRuntimeConfig +Array~SkillMetaLite~ skillMetas } class SkillMetaLite { +string description +string identifier +string name } class AgentRuntimeService { +createOperation(params OperationCreationParams) Operation } class OperationMetadata { +Array~SkillMetaLite~ skillMetas +any userMemory +any deviceSystemInfo +string userTimezone } class RuntimeExecutors { +execute(state OperationState) void } class OperationState { +OperationMetadata metadata } class SkillsConfig { +Array~SkillMeta~ enabledSkills } class SkillMeta { +string description +string identifier +string name } class ServerMessagesEngineParams { +SkillsConfig skillsConfig +ServerToolsConfig toolsConfig +string systemRole } class ServerMessagesEngine { +serverMessagesEngine(params ServerMessagesEngineParams) ContextEngineInput } class ContextEngineInput { +SkillsConfig skillsConfig +ToolsDiscoveryConfig toolsConfig } class ContextEngineering { +contextEngineering(input ContextEngineInput) void } class SkillEngine { +getAllSkills() Array~SkillMeta~ +getEnabledSkills(plugins Array~string~) Array~SkillMeta~ } class AiAgentService { +startOperation() void } class LobeHubSkillManifest { +SkillMeta meta +string identifier } OperationCreationParams --> SkillMetaLite : uses AgentRuntimeService --> OperationCreationParams : createOperation params OperationMetadata --> SkillMetaLite : contains OperationState --> OperationMetadata : metadata RuntimeExecutors --> OperationState : reads RuntimeExecutors --> SkillsConfig : builds ServerMessagesEngineParams --> SkillsConfig : contains ServerMessagesEngine --> ServerMessagesEngineParams : accepts ServerMessagesEngine --> ContextEngineInput : builds ContextEngineInput --> SkillsConfig : contains ContextEngineering --> ContextEngineInput : accepts AiAgentService --> AgentRuntimeService : createOperation AiAgentService --> LobeHubSkillManifest : reads AiAgentService --> SkillMetaLite : maps manifests to skillMetas ContextEngineering --> SkillEngine : uses SkillEngine --> SkillMeta : returns ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Inject all installed skills into skillsConfig for instead of only plugin-enabled skills. |
  • Change frontend context engineering to use createSkillEngine().getAllSkills() for skillsConfig.enabledSkills.
  • Ensure skillsConfig is always present in the context engine input when there are any installed skills, independent of the agent plugins configuration.
| `src/services/chat/mecha/contextEngineering.ts` | | Thread skill metadata (skillMetas) from operation creation into runtime execution metadata. |
  • Extend OperationCreationParams to accept an optional skillMetas array with description, identifier, and name.
  • Include skillMetas when creating operations in AgentRuntimeService and store them in state metadata for later use by executors.
| `src/server/services/agentRuntime/types.ts`
`src/server/services/agentRuntime/AgentRuntimeService.ts` | | Use stored skillMetas in runtime executors to configure skillsConfig for the context engine. |
  • Read skillMetas from state.metadata inside RuntimeExecutors.
  • If any skillMetas exist, construct skillsConfig.enabledSkills from them and pass it as part of the contextEngineInput.
| `src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts` | | Extend the server messages/context engine interface to carry skillsConfig through to the messages engine. |
  • Add an optional skillsConfig field with enabledSkills: SkillMeta[] to ServerMessagesEngineParams.
  • Accept skillsConfig in serverMessagesEngine parameters and forward it to the underlying MessagesEngine only when enabledSkills is non-empty.
| `src/server/modules/Mecha/ContextEngineering/types.ts`
`src/server/modules/Mecha/ContextEngineering/index.ts` | | Populate skillMetas at AI agent service level from installed LobeHub skills. |
  • Map lobehubSkillManifests to a normalized skillMetas array containing identifier, name, and description.
  • Pass the resulting skillMetas into the operation creation parameters so it can be used for injection downstream.
| `src/server/services/aiAgent/index.ts` | ### Assessment against linked issues | Issue | Objective | Addressed | Explanation | | ------ | ------- | ----- | ----- | | https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/12848 | When an agent has all skills, tools, and related features disabled, no built-in skills should be included in the system prompt/context (i.e., no tokens consumed by 'Skill Settings' and no tools reported as available). | ❌ | The PR changes the client and server context engineering to inject all installed skills into the skills configuration (`skillsConfig.enabledSkills = getAllSkills()` and `skillMetas`), making them available in `` regardless of whether they are enabled for the agent. This is the opposite of the requested behavior, which is to have zero skills in context when everything is disabled. | | https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/issues/12848 | Ensure that newly created agents have a completely empty default context with no built-in skills or tools implicitly enabled or advertised. | ❌ | The PR does not modify the default agent configuration to remove built-in skills or tools. Instead, it introduces logic to always include all installed skills in the available skills metadata for AI discovery. Thus, new agents will still have skills exposed in context rather than an empty context. | ---
