## Reviewer's Guide Implements a robust market OIDC re‑authentication flow for tools by adding refresh-token handling in the MarketAuthProvider, wiring 401 detection from both lambda and tools tRPC clients through a new event emitter, and converting market tool router errors into TRPC UNAUTHORIZED errors to trigger the auth flow instead of hard-failing tool calls. #### Sequence diagram for market tool call with OIDC reauthentication on 401 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ToolCaller as Tool_or_Agent participant ToolsClient as ToolsTRPCClient participant ServerToolsRouter as ToolsRouter_market participant Sandbox as SandboxService participant LambdaClient as LambdaTRPCClient participant MarketRouter as MarketAPIRouter participant MarketAuthProvider participant MarketAuthEvents as MarketAuthEventEmitter User->>ToolCaller: Trigger market tool execution ToolCaller->>ToolsClient: market.execInSandbox ToolsClient->>ServerToolsRouter: market.execInSandbox ServerToolsRouter->>Sandbox: execInSandbox request with accessToken Sandbox-->>ServerToolsRouter: error success=false, code=invalid_token ServerToolsRouter->>ServerToolsRouter: Detect invalid_token ServerToolsRouter->>ToolsClient: TRPCError UNAUTHORIZED ToolsClient->>ToolsClient: errorHandlingLink ToolsClient->>MarketAuthEvents: emit market-unauthorized MarketAuthEvents-->>MarketAuthProvider: market-unauthorized callback MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: handleUnauthorized MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: refreshToken (from DB) alt Refresh successful MarketAuthProvider->>LambdaClient: market.oidc.refreshToken LambdaClient->>MarketRouter: refreshToken MarketRouter-->>LambdaClient: new accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn LambdaClient-->>MarketAuthProvider: tokens MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: saveMarketTokensToDB, update session MarketAuthProvider-->>ToolCaller: handleUnauthorized returns true else Refresh failed MarketAuthProvider->>User: Show market auth dialog (signIn) User-->>MarketAuthProvider: Complete authorization or cancel alt User authorized MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: update session with new tokens MarketAuthProvider-->>ToolCaller: handleUnauthorized returns true else User cancelled or error MarketAuthProvider-->>ToolCaller: handleUnauthorized returns false end end ToolCaller->>ToolsClient: Retry market.execInSandbox after successful reauth ``` #### Sequence diagram for market token initialization and auto refresh ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant MarketAuthProvider participant MarketDB as MarketTokenStorage participant LambdaClient as LambdaTRPCClient participant MarketRouter as MarketAPIRouter participant MarketUserInfoAPI as MarketUserInfoEndpoint MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: useEffect on isUserStateInit MarketAuthProvider->>MarketDB: getMarketTokensFromDB alt No tokens MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: setStatus unauthenticated else Has tokens alt Token expired alt Has refreshToken MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: tryRefreshToken(refreshTokenValue) MarketAuthProvider->>LambdaClient: market.oidc.refreshToken LambdaClient->>MarketRouter: refreshToken MarketRouter-->>LambdaClient: accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn LambdaClient-->>MarketAuthProvider: tokens MarketAuthProvider->>MarketDB: saveMarketTokensToDB MarketAuthProvider->>MarketUserInfoAPI: fetchUserInfo(accessToken) MarketUserInfoAPI-->>MarketAuthProvider: userInfo MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: setSession, setStatus authenticated else No refreshToken MarketAuthProvider->>MarketDB: clearMarketTokensFromDB MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: setStatus unauthenticated end else Token not expired MarketAuthProvider->>MarketUserInfoAPI: fetchUserInfo(accessToken) alt userInfo valid MarketUserInfoAPI-->>MarketAuthProvider: userInfo MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: setSession, setStatus authenticated else userInfo invalid alt Has refreshToken MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: tryRefreshToken(refreshTokenValue) MarketAuthProvider->>LambdaClient: market.oidc.refreshToken LambdaClient->>MarketRouter: refreshToken MarketRouter-->>LambdaClient: tokens LambdaClient-->>MarketAuthProvider: tokens MarketAuthProvider->>MarketDB: saveMarketTokensToDB MarketAuthProvider->>MarketUserInfoAPI: fetchUserInfo(accessToken) MarketUserInfoAPI-->>MarketAuthProvider: userInfo MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: setSession, setStatus authenticated else No refreshToken or refresh failed MarketAuthProvider->>MarketDB: clearMarketTokensFromDB MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: setStatus unauthenticated end end end end rect rgba(200,200,255,0.2) MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: useEffect auto refresh MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: compute timeUntilRefresh alt timeUntilRefresh <= 0 MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: refreshToken immediately else timeUntilRefresh > 0 MarketAuthProvider->>MarketAuthProvider: setTimeout(refreshToken, timeUntilRefresh) end end ``` #### Class diagram for MarketAuthProvider, context types, and event emitter ```mermaid classDiagram class MarketAuthState { +MarketAuthSession~session~ +string status +boolean showConfirmModal +boolean isDesktop } class MarketUserInfo { <> +number id +string email +string name } class MarketUserProfile { <> +string nickname +string avatar } class MarketAuthSession { <> +string accessToken +number expiresAt +number expiresIn +string scope +string tokenType +MarketUserInfo userInfo } class MarketAuthContextType { <> +MarketAuthSession session +string status +function getAccessToken() string +function getCurrentUserInfo() MarketUserInfo +function getRefreshToken() string +function handleUnauthorized() Promise~boolean~ +function openProfileSetup(onSuccess) void +function refreshToken() Promise~boolean~ +function signIn() Promise~number|null~ } class MarketAuthEventType { <> +market-unauthorized } class MarketUnauthorizedEvent { +string path +number timestamp } class EventCallback { <> +function callback(event) void } class MarketAuthEventEmitter { -Map~MarketAuthEventType, Set~EventCallback~~ listeners +function on(event, callback) function +function emit(event, data) void } class MarketAuthProviderComponent { <> +MarketAuthState state +function initializeSession() Promise~void~ +function tryRefreshToken(refreshTokenValue) Promise~boolean~ +function refreshToken() Promise~boolean~ +function handleUnauthorized() Promise~boolean~ +function signIn() Promise~number|null~ +function getAccessToken() string +function getRefreshToken() string +function getCurrentUserInfo() MarketUserInfo } MarketAuthProviderComponent ..|> MarketAuthContextType MarketAuthProviderComponent --> MarketAuthSession MarketAuthProviderComponent --> MarketUserInfo MarketAuthProviderComponent --> MarketUserProfile MarketAuthEventEmitter o--> MarketAuthEventType MarketAuthEventEmitter o--> MarketUnauthorizedEvent MarketAuthEventEmitter o--> EventCallback class LambdaTRPCClient { +function market_oidc_refreshToken(clientId, refreshToken) Promise~tokens~ } class ToolsTRPCClient { +function market_execInSandbox(args) Promise~result~ +function market_exportAndUploadFile(args) Promise~result~ } MarketAuthProviderComponent --> LambdaTRPCClient : uses ToolsTRPCClient --> MarketAuthEventEmitter : emits 401 events LambdaTRPCClient --> MarketAuthEventEmitter : emits 401 events ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add full refresh-token based recovery and auto-refresh logic to MarketAuthProvider and expose a handleUnauthorized helper in the auth context. |
  • Introduce tryRefreshToken to refresh tokens during session initialization when stored access token is expired or user info fetch fails.
  • Implement a reusable refreshToken method using useCallback that reads the refresh token from storage, calls the market OIDC refresh endpoint, persists new tokens, updates session state, and clears tokens on failure.
  • Add handleUnauthorized callback that first attempts token refresh and then falls back to interactive signIn if refresh fails, with proper logging and error handling.
  • Wrap signIn in useCallback and add an effect to auto-refresh tokens 5 minutes before expiry for non-trusted clients.
  • Subscribe to market-unauthorized events via useEffect so MarketAuthProvider can react to 401s emitted from tRPC clients, and extend context type to include handleUnauthorized.
| `src/layout/AuthProvider/MarketAuth/MarketAuthProvider.tsx`
`src/layout/AuthProvider/MarketAuth/types.ts` | | Introduce a lightweight event bus for market auth and hook both lambda and tools tRPC clients into it for debounced 401 handling without affecting main app auth. |
  • Create MarketAuthEventEmitter with on/emit APIs and a market-unauthorized event payload for path/timestamp.
  • Update lambda tRPC client errorHandlingLink to distinguish market.* calls from others, debounce market 401s separately from global 401s, and emit market-unauthorized instead of logging out the main user session.
  • Add a tools client errorHandlingLink that watches for 401s on market.* procedures, debounces them, and emits market-unauthorized events.
  • Ensure both clients still propagate the original TRPC error downstream after emitting events.
| `src/layout/AuthProvider/MarketAuth/events.ts`
`src/libs/trpc/client/lambda.ts`
`src/libs/trpc/client/tools.ts` | | Normalize market tool router error handling to surface authentication problems as TRPC UNAUTHORIZED errors that can trigger the new auth flow. |
  • In execInSandboxHandler, inspect response.error.code/message to detect invalid/expired tokens and throw TRPCError(UNAUTHORIZED) with a guidance message; otherwise return structured error details using normalized errorCode/errorMessage variables.
  • In execInSandboxHandler catch block, rethrow existing TRPCError (e.g., UNAUTHORIZED), detect auth-related error messages, and convert them into TRPC UNAUTHORIZED when they come from generic exceptions.
  • In exportAndUploadFile, similarly detect auth errors in the sandbox response and thrown exceptions, converting them into TRPC UNAUTHORIZED, while normalizing other errors to return consistent error messages.
  • Preserve original error names/messages where appropriate for non-auth failures while routing auth errors into the centralized 401 handling path.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds a new SQL migration that creates BM25 full‑text search indexes with ICU tokenizer across 14 tables, wired into the migration journal and snapshot metadata so search can leverage Tantivy-backed indexes with efficient user- and role-based filter pushdown. #### Sequence diagram for search using BM25 indexes with filter pushdown ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant AppServer participant Postgres participant TantivyIndex User->>AppServer: Submit search query with user context AppServer->>Postgres: SELECT ... FROM messages WHERE user_id = current_user AND content @@ bm25_query Postgres->>TantivyIndex: BM25 search request with ICU tokenization and filters user_id, role TantivyIndex-->>Postgres: Ranked document ids Postgres-->>AppServer: Rows from messages ordered by BM25 score AppServer-->>User: Search results ``` #### ER diagram for tables with new BM25 ICU indexes ```mermaid erDiagram agents { int id text title text description text slug jsonb tags text system_role uuid user_id } topics { int id text title text content text description uuid user_id } files { int id text name uuid user_id text file_type } knowledge_bases { int id text name text description uuid user_id } user_memories { int id text title text summary text details uuid user_id } chat_groups { int id text title text #### Flow diagram for migration 0093 BM25 index creation ```mermaid flowchart TD start["Application startup"] checkMeta["Load migration journal _journal.json"] needs093{"Has migration 0093 run?"} json_fields tags fast keyword user_id"] t2["topics: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS topics_bm25_idx"] t2c["CREATE BM25 index on topics key_field id text_fields title, content, description fast keyword user_id"] t5c["CREATE BM25 index on user_memories key_field id text_fields title, summary, details fast keyword user_id"] t6["chat_groups: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS chat_groups_bm25_idx"] t6c["CREATE BM25 index on t8c["CREATE BM25 index on user_memories_preferences key_field id text_fields conclusion_directives, suggestions fast keyword user_id"] t9["user_memories_activities: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS user_memories_activities_bm25_idx"] t9c["CREATE BM25 index on user_memories_activities key_field id text_fields notes, narrative, feedback fast keyword user_id"] t10["user_memories_identities: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS user_memories_identities_bm25_idx"] t10c["CREATE BM25 index on user_memories_identities key_field id text_fields description, role fast keyword user_id"] t11["user_memories_experiences: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS user_memories_experiences_bm25_idx"] t11c["CREATE BM25 index on user_memories_experiences key_field id text_fields situation, reasoning, possible_outcome, action, key_learning fast keyword user_id"] t12["user_memory_persona_documents: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS user_memory_persona_documents_bm25_idx"] t12c["CREATE BM25 index on user_memory_persona_documents key_field id text_fields tagline, persona fast keyword user_id"] t13["documents: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS documents_bm25_idx"] t13c["CREATE BM25 index on documents (large) key_field id text_fields title, description, content, slug fast keyword user_id, file_type"] t14["messages: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS messages_bm25_idx"] t14c["CREATE BM25 index on messages (largest) key_field id text_fields content fast keyword user_id, role"] done["Update migration snapshot 0093_snapshot.json and journal"] endNode["Application continues startup"] start --> checkMeta --> needs093 needs093 -- yes --> run093 needs093 -- no --> endNode run093 --> t1 --> t1c --> t2 --> t2c --> t3 --> t3c --> t4 --> t4c --> t5 --> t5c --> t6 --> t6c --> t7 --> t7c --> t8 --> t8c --> t9 --> t9c --> t10 --> t10c --> t11 --> t11c --> t12 --> t12c --> t13 --> t13c --> t14 --> t14c --> done --> endNode ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce BM25 full-text indexes with ICU tokenizer across 14 core tables for improved search and filter performance. |
  • Adds DROP INDEX IF EXISTS/CREATE INDEX bm25 definitions for 14 tables, each using a bm25 access method with a key_field of id.
  • Configures text_fields per table (titles, descriptions, content, etc.) predominantly with ICU tokenizer plus English stemmer and stopwords for better relevance.
  • Configures json_fields where applicable (e.g., tags) to be indexed via ICU tokenizer.
  • Marks user_id (and role for messages) as fast keyword fields to support efficient filter pushdown in Tantivy index scans.
  • Orders index creation so that large tables (documents, messages) are processed last and adds statement-breakpoint markers between statements for migration tooling.
| `packages/database/migrations/0093_add_bm25_indexes_with_icu.sql` | | Register the new migration in the migration journal and snapshot metadata. |
  • Appends migration 0093 to the meta _journal so it participates in the migration sequence.
  • Adds a 0093_snapshot.json describing the schema state after the BM25 index creation.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds a new custom SQL migration that creates BM25 full-text search indexes with ICU tokenizer and fast keyword fields across 14 tables, wiring it into the migration journal. #### Entity relationship diagram for BM25-indexed tables and fields ```mermaid erDiagram agents { int id text title text description text slug jsonb tags text system_role uuid user_id } topics { int id text title text content text description uuid user_id } files { int id text name uuid user_id text file_type } knowledge_bases { int id text name text description uuid user_id } user_memories { int id { int id text tagline text persona uuid user_id } documents { int id text title text description text content text slug uuid user_id text file_type text source_type } messages { int id text content text summary uuid user_id text role } ``` #### Flow diagram for BM25 index migration execution order ```mermaid flowchart TD Startup[Application_startup] --> CheckMigrations[Check_pending_migrations] CheckMigrations -->|Migration_0093_pending| Run0093[Run_migration_0093_add_bm25_indexes_with_icu] CheckMigrations -->|Migration_0093_not_pending| ContinueApp[Continue_normal_startup] subgraph Migration_0093 Run0093 --> Agents[Create_agents_bm25_idx] Agents --> Topics[Create_topics_bm25_idx] Topics --> Files[Create_files_bm25_idx] Files --> KB[Create_knowledge_bases_bm25_idx] KB --> UM[Create_user_memories_bm25_idx] UM --> ChatGroups[Create_chat_groups_bm25_idx] ChatGroups --> UMCtx[Create_user_memories_contexts_bm25_idx] UMCtx --> UMPrefs[Create_user_memories_preferences_bm25_idx] UMPrefs --> UMActs[Create_user_memories_activities_bm25_idx] UMActs --> UMIds[Create_user_memories_identities_bm25_idx] UMIds --> UMExps[Create_user_memories_experiences_bm25_idx] UMExps --> UMPD[Create_user_memory_persona_documents_bm25_idx] UMPD --> Docs[Create_documents_bm25_idx] Docs --> Msgs[Create_messages_bm25_idx] Msgs --> Done[Migration_0093_complete] end Done --> ContinueApp ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce BM25 full-text search indexes with ICU tokenizer across core domain tables for improved search and filter pushdown. |
  • Create a custom SQL migration 0093_add_bm25_indexes_with_icu.sql that defines BM25 indexes on 14 tables, each with a key_field of id.
  • Configure ICU tokenizer (with English stemmer/stopwords where relevant) for main text columns such as titles, descriptions, content, and summaries.
  • Add user_id to all indexes as a keyword field with fast=true to enable efficient per-user filtering during index scan.
  • Mark enum-like/filter columns (e.g., type, status, memory_layer, memory_category, relationship, source_type, role, file_type) as keyword+fast fields to support filter pushdown.
  • Use keyword tokenizer for categorical JSONB tags on agents.tags to enable label-based search.
  • Precede each CREATE INDEX with DROP INDEX IF EXISTS to make the migration idempotent and reorder creation so large tables (documents, messages) are indexed last to reduce lock impact.
| `packages/database/migrations/0093_add_bm25_indexes_with_icu.sql` | | Register the new migration in the migration metadata so it participates in the migration pipeline. |

  • Add a 0093_snapshot.json metadata file to describe the schema state after this migration.

E[Record migration 0093 in journal metadata] E --> Z[Continue startup] subgraph T[BM25 index configuration highlights] direction TB T1[user_id field keyword tokenizer fast flag] --> T3[Filter pushdown into tantivy index scan] T2[Enum and status fields keyword tokenizer fast flag] --> T3 T4[ICU tokenizer English stemmer English stopwords] --> T5[Multilingual and normalized text search] end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce BM25 full-text search indexes with ICU tokenizer and filter-pushdown fields across key application tables via a new SQL migration. |
  • Create migration 0093_add_bm25_indexes_with_icu.sql that drops any existing BM25 indexes and recreates them for 14 tables using the bm25 index type
  • Configure text fields on each table to use the ICU tokenizer, often with English stemmer and stopwords, and map jsonb tags for agents as searchable JSON fields
  • Mark user_id and enumerated/filter columns (e.g., type, status, memory_layer, memory_category, relationship, source_type, role, file_type) as keyword tokenized with fast=true for efficient filtering in Tantivy index scans
  • Extend search coverage by including chat_groups.content (system prompt) and messages.summary as indexed text fields
  • Order index creation statements so that large tables (documents, messages) are processed last to reduce blocking on smaller tables
  • Wrap each CREATE INDEX in a preceding DROP INDEX IF EXISTS for idempotent migration runs and add the corresponding 0093 snapshot and journal metadata entries

## Reviewer's Guide Refactors navigation-related components to centralize all dev-mode and feature-flag–dependent layout decisions into a new useNavLayout hook, while also adjusting the footer layout, user panel menu contents, home page dev-only modules, and fixing the LangButton alignment/behavior. #### Class diagram for centralized navigation layout via useNavLayout hook ```mermaid classDiagram class NavItem { bool devOnly bool hidden any icon bool isNew string key void onClick() string title string url } class FooterConfig { bool hideGitHub string layout bool showEvalEntry bool showSettingsEntry } class UserPanelConfig { bool showDataImporter bool showMemory } class NavLayout { NavItem[] topNavItems NavItem[] bottomMenuItems FooterConfig footer UserPanelConfig userPanel } class UseNavLayoutHook { NavLayout useNavLayout() NavItem[] filterByMode(NavItem[] items, bool isDevMode) } class NavComponent { +render() } class BottomMenuComponent { +render() } class FooterComponent { +render() } class UserPanelMenuHook { +useMenu() } class HomeFeaturesComponent { +render() } NavLayout "1" --> "*" NavItem : contains NavLayout "1" --> "1" FooterConfig : has NavLayout "1" --> "1" UserPanelConfig : has UseNavLayoutHook --> NavLayout : returns UseNavLayoutHook <.. NavComponent : uses UseNavLayoutHook <.. BottomMenuComponent : uses UseNavLayoutHook <.. FooterComponent : uses UseNavLayoutHook <.. UserPanelMenuHook : uses HomeFeaturesComponent ..> NavItem : uses_dev_mode_sections ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce useNavLayout hook to compute navigation layout from dev mode and feature flags. |
  • Create NavItem and NavLayout types describing top nav, bottom menu, footer, and user panel configuration.
  • Read isDevMode, feature flags, and server config once and derive topNavItems, bottomMenuItems, footer, and userPanel settings via useMemo.
  • Implement devOnly metadata and filterByMode helper to filter items differently in dev vs simplified mode, including gating pages/video/image/settings/memory and user panel entries.
| `src/hooks/useNavLayout.ts` | | Simplify Nav and BottomMenu components to render from useNavLayout instead of local configuration. |
  • Replace local useMemo item definitions in Nav with topNavItems from useNavLayout and remove direct feature flag and global store dependencies.
  • Replace local BottomMenu items with bottomMenuItems from useNavLayout and adjust navigation handlers to work with optional url.
  • Tighten NavItem prop typing by casting hook-provided icon to NavItemProps['icon'] where needed.
| `src/routes/(main)/home/_layout/Header/components/Nav.tsx`
`src/routes/(main)/home/_layout/Body/BottomMenu/index.tsx` | | Refactor Footer to use centralized footer layout config from useNavLayout and add an expanded layout variant. |
  • Replace local isDevMode and hideGitHub reads with footer layout state from useNavLayout, including hideGitHub, layout, showEvalEntry, and showSettingsEntry.
  • Gate help menu items (Settings, GitHub, Eval entry) based on footer flags and layout mode instead of raw dev mode checks.
  • Introduce an expanded footer layout that shows inline Help, GitHub, Eval icons and a ThemeButton, while keeping the compact dropdown-only layout for simplified mode.
  • Wrap feedback/product-hunt handlers in useCallback and update help menu memo dependencies accordingly.
| `src/routes/(main)/home/_layout/Footer/index.tsx` | | Adjust UserPanel menus to respect centralized userPanel flags from useNavLayout. |
  • Use userPanel.showMemory to conditionally render the Memory menu entry in the user menu.
  • Use userPanel.showDataImporter (with login check) to conditionally render the DataImporter entry and a trailing divider.
  • Wire useNavLayout into useMenu so user panel items are consistent with dev/simplified mode behavior.
| `src/features/User/UserPanel/useMenu.tsx` | | Restore and gate home page modules behind dev mode. |
  • Re-enable RecentTopic, RecentPage, CommunityAgents, and RecentResource imports and JSX on the home page.
  • Compute isDevMode from user settings and use it (with isLogin) to show the appropriate sections only for dev-mode users.
  • Keep the existing inputActiveMode logic while using CSS display toggling to avoid unnecessary unmounting.
| `src/routes/(main)/home/features/index.tsx` | | Refine LangButton styling and interaction to align with UserPanel items and change dropdown behavior. |
  • Replace the inner Menu-based trigger with a custom Flexbox-based clickable row matching other menu items (specific height, padding, margins, border radius, and hover background).
  • Use secondary text color for icons and label and adjust layout to have icon, label, and chevron aligned.
  • Change DropdownMenu to open on hover and disable its popup transition animation for a snappier feel.
| `src/features/User/UserPanel/LangButton.tsx` | ---

You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).

## Reviewer's Guide Adjusts ConversationStore sendMessage to clear the input immediately on send (preserving drafts typed during streaming) and fixes operation cancellation matching so null/undefined topic/thread contexts are treated as equivalent, with tests added for both behaviors. #### Sequence diagram for updated sendMessage input clearing behavior ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ConversationStore participant Editor participant ChatStore User->>Editor: Type first message Editor->>ConversationStore: updateInputMessage("first message") ConversationStore->>ConversationStore: store.inputMessage = "first message" User->>ConversationStore: sendMessage(message) ConversationStore->>ConversationStore: validate message ConversationStore->>ConversationStore: set({ inputMessage: "" }) ConversationStore->>Editor: clear visible input ConversationStore->>ChatStore: sendMessage(context, message) activate ChatStore ChatStore-->>ConversationStore: pending streaming promise User->>Editor: Type draft during streaming Editor->>ConversationStore: updateInputMessage("draft during streaming") ConversationStore->>ConversationStore: store.inputMessage = "draft during streaming" ChatStore-->>ConversationStore: streaming completes deactivate ChatStore ConversationStore->>ConversationStore: run hooks.onAfterSendMessage() Note over ConversationStore: inputMessage is not cleared again ConversationStore-->>Editor: keep draft during streaming Editor-->>User: Shows "draft during streaming" after completion ``` #### Class diagram for OperationActionsImpl cancelOperations matching changes ```mermaid classDiagram class OperationContext { string agentId string messageId string groupId string~ | null topicId string~ | null threadId } class Operation { string operationId string type string status OperationContext context } class OperationFilter { string agentId string messageId string groupId string~ | null topicId string~ | null threadId string status string[] type } class OperationActionsImpl { +cancelOperations(filter OperationFilter) void -matchesFilter(op Operation, filter OperationFilter) bool } class isSameNullableContextValue { <> +isSameNullableContextValue(left string~ | null, right string~ | null) bool } OperationActionsImpl "1" --> "*" Operation : manages Operation "1" --> "1" OperationContext : has OperationActionsImpl ..> OperationFilter : uses OperationActionsImpl ..> isSameNullableContextValue : uses for topicId, threadId comparison ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Clear conversation input at send start instead of after streaming completes to avoid overwriting drafts typed during generation. |
  • Move the inputMessage clearing logic to execute before the async streaming lifecycle in the ConversationStore sendMessage action.
  • Ensure ConversationStore state stays in sync with the editor by clearing input immediately when sendMessage is invoked.
  • Remove the previous input clearing at the end of the sendMessage flow.
| `src/features/Conversation/store/slices/message/action/sendMessage.ts` | | Normalize nullable context values when cancelling operations so null and undefined topic/thread identifiers are treated as the same context. |
  • Introduce a helper that compares nullable context values by normalizing undefined to null.
  • Use the helper when matching topicId and threadId in cancelOperations filtering logic.
  • Ensure cancellation correctly finds and cancels operations in null-topic contexts.
| `src/store/chat/slices/operation/actions.ts` | | Add and update tests to cover draft preservation during streaming and cancellation behavior in null-topic contexts. |
  • Extend ConversationStore tests to verify that input drafts typed while a send is pending are preserved after streaming completes.
  • Add a useOperationState hook test that validates isInputLoading is cleared when cancelling an operation in a null-topic context.
  • Add an operation actions test confirming null and undefined topicId are treated as the same context during cancellation filtering.
  • Mock useChatStore.sendMessage in ConversationStore tests to simulate a pending send lifecycle.
| `src/features/Conversation/store.test.ts`
`src/hooks/useOperationState.test.ts`
`src/store/chat/slices/operation/__tests__/actions.test.ts` | ---

## Reviewer's Guide Centralizes the "new screen" behavior into a virtual-list-level spacer hook, refactors scroll behavior to pin the latest user message more robustly, and gates auto-scroll mounting based on settings and spacer state while removing the legacy per-message hook and prop. #### Sequence diagram for the new conversation spacer and auto scroll behavior ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI as ConversationUI participant VL as VirtualizedList participant VList as VList participant Store as ConversationStore participant Spacer as useConversationSpacer participant ScrollHook as useScrollToUserMessage participant AS as AutoScroll participant RO as ResizeObserver User->>UI: Send message UI->>Store: Append user message UI->>Store: Append assistant placeholder Store-->>VL: Updated dataSource VL->>ScrollHook: useScrollToUserMessage({dataSourceLength, isSecondLastMessageFromUser, scrollToIndex}) ScrollHook->>ScrollHook: Detect 2 new messages ScrollHook->>VList: scrollToIndex(userMessageIndex, align start, smooth) ScrollHook->>VList: Retry scroll with delays (0, 32, 96ms) VL->>Spacer: useConversationSpacer(dataSource) Spacer->>Store: Read displayMessages, virtuaScrollMethods Spacer->>Spacer: Detect 2 new messages (user + assistant) Spacer->>Spacer: Store userMessageIndex, assistantMessageIndex Spacer->>VList: getViewportSize, getItemOffset, getItemSize VList-->>Spacer: viewportHeight, offsets, sizes Spacer->>Spacer: Calculate spacerHeight Spacer-->>VL: listData (dataSource + spacerId), spacerActive true, spacerHeight VL->>VList: Render listData VList->>VL: Item(messageId, index) VL->>VL: If isSpacerMessage(messageId) VL->>VL: Render spacer div with height spacerHeight VL->>AS: Mount AutoScroll only when VL->>VL: isLastItem && isAutoScrollEnabled && !spacerActive AS->>Store: Read isAIGenerating, isScrolling, atBottom AS->>AS: shouldAutoScroll = atBottom && isGenerating && !isScrolling Spacer->>RO: Attach ResizeObserver to user and assistant message elements RO-->>Spacer: resize events during streaming Spacer->>Spacer: Recalculate spacerHeight alt spacerHeight becomes 0 Spacer->>Spacer: Set height 0 Spacer->>Spacer: Schedule unmount after CONVERSATION_SPACER_TRANSITION_MS Spacer-->>VL: spacerActive false VL->>AS: AutoScroll now allowed for last item end ``` #### Class diagram for updated virtualized list, scroll methods, and conversation spacer hook ```mermaid classDiagram class VirtualizedListProps { +string[] dataSource +(index number, id string) => ReactElement itemContent } class VirtuaScrollMethods { +getItemOffset(index number) number +getItemSize(index number) number +getScrollOffset() number +getScrollSize() number +getViewportSize() number +scrollTo(offset number) void +scrollToIndex(index number, options ScrollToIndexOptions) void } class ConversationStore { +virtuaScrollMethods VirtuaScrollMethods +registerVirtuaScrollMethods(methods VirtuaScrollMethods) void +isAIGenerating boolean +displayMessages UIChatMessage[] } class VirtualizedList { -Ref virtuaRef -Ref scrollEndTimerRef -boolean isAutoScrollEnabled -boolean spacerActive -number spacerHeight +constructor(props VirtualizedListProps) +handleScroll() void +handleScrollEnd() void } class useConversationSpacerReturn { +(id string) boolean isSpacerMessage +string[] listData +boolean spacerActive +number spacerHeight } class useConversationSpacer { +CONVERSATION_SPACER_ID string +CONVERSATION_SPACER_TRANSITION_MS number +useConversationSpacer(dataSource string[]) useConversationSpacerReturn } class useScrollToUserMessageOptions { +number dataSourceLength +boolean isSecondLastMessageFromUser +(index number, options ScrollToIndexOptions) => void scrollToIndex } class useScrollToUserMessage { +PIN_RETRY_DELAYS number[] +useScrollToUserMessage(options useScrollToUserMessageOptions) void } class AutoScroll { +shouldAutoScroll boolean } class ChatItemProps { +string id +ReactNode message +boolean editing +boolean loading +"left"|"right" placement +Date time +() => void onAvatarClick +(event DivMouseEvent) => void onDoubleClick } class ChatItem { +ChatItem(props ChatItemProps) } class useAutoScrollEnabled { +useAutoScrollEnabled() boolean } class ScrollToIndexOptions { +string align_start_center_end +boolean smooth } ConversationStore o-- VirtuaScrollMethods VirtualizedList ..|> VirtualizedListProps VirtualizedList --> ConversationStore : uses VirtualizedList --> useConversationSpacer : calls VirtualizedList --> useScrollToUserMessage : calls VirtualizedList --> useAutoScrollEnabled : calls VirtualizedList --> AutoScroll : conditionally mounts useConversationSpacer --> ConversationStore : reads state useConversationSpacer --> useConversationSpacerReturn : returns useScrollToUserMessage --> useScrollToUserMessageOptions : uses ChatItem ..|> ChatItemProps ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce centralized conversation spacer that appends a synthetic spacer item to the virtualized list to implement the new-screen effect. |
  • Added useConversationSpacer hook that tracks the latest user+assistant pair and computes a dynamic spacer height based on viewport and item offsets or DOM measurements.
  • Injects a synthetic spacer item (with a fixed ID) into the VList data source when active, and exposes helpers to identify spacer rows and determine whether the spacer is active.
  • Uses ResizeObserver plus a content-signature heuristic to recompute spacer height while the assistant message streams, unmounting the spacer once its height reaches zero.
| `src/features/Conversation/ChatList/hooks/useConversationSpacer.ts`
`src/features/Conversation/ChatList/components/VirtualizedList.tsx`
`src/features/Conversation/store/slices/virtuaList/initialState.ts` | | Refine virtualized list wiring to support spacer rendering and more complete scroll method exposure. |
  • Wraps the VList data prop with listData from useConversationSpacer and renders a WideScreenContainer-based spacer row when the spacer ID is encountered.
  • Extends registered Virtua scroll methods to include getItemOffset, getItemSize, and scrollTo so hooks like useConversationSpacer can compute heights from the virtualizer.
  • Gates AutoScroll rendering on both the global auto-scroll setting and spacer activity to avoid conflicts while the spacer is active.
| `src/features/Conversation/ChatList/components/VirtualizedList.tsx`
`src/features/Conversation/store/slices/virtuaList/initialState.ts`
`src/features/Conversation/ChatList/components/AutoScroll/index.tsx`
`src/features/Conversation/ChatList/components/AutoScroll/useAutoScrollEnabled.ts` | | Refactor scroll-to-user-message behavior to be store-agnostic and more robust via retry pinning. |
  • Updated useScrollToUserMessage to accept explicit parameters instead of reading from the store, improving composability and testability.
  • Implemented multiple delayed scrollToIndex calls using a fixed retry schedule to ensure the user message stays pinned as layout stabilizes.
  • Adjusted unit tests to use fake timers and assert the multiple invocations of scrollToIndex for both single and multiple user-message scenarios.
| `src/features/Conversation/ChatList/hooks/useScrollToUserMessage.ts`
`src/features/Conversation/ChatList/hooks/useScrollToUserMessage.test.ts` | | Remove legacy per-message new-screen hook and ChatItem min-height prop usage. |
  • Deleted the useNewScreen hook and its tests, removing per-message min-height calculations.
  • Dropped the newScreenMinHeight prop from ChatItemProps and removed the associated minHeight styling application.
  • Simplified Assistant, Supervisor, AssistantGroup, and Task message components by eliminating isLatestItem-related logic and useNewScreen integration.
| `src/features/Conversation/Messages/components/useNewScreen.ts`
`src/features/Conversation/Messages/components/useNewScreen.test.ts`
`src/features/Conversation/ChatItem/type.ts`
`src/features/Conversation/ChatItem/ChatItem.tsx`
`src/features/Conversation/Messages/Assistant/index.tsx`
`src/features/Conversation/Messages/Supervisor/index.tsx`
`src/features/Conversation/Messages/AssistantGroup/index.tsx`
`src/features/Conversation/Messages/Task/index.tsx` | | Miscellaneous cleanup and DX adjustments. |
  • Ensured AutoScroll no longer checks the auto-scroll setting internally, relying instead on the outer VirtualizedList to gate mounting.
  • Updated the Vite envRestartKeys plugin to ignore test files during dev-server restart to avoid noisy reloads when editing tests.
  • Removed debug logging related to scrolling/auto-scroll (per PR description), reducing console noise during development.
| `src/features/Conversation/ChatList/components/AutoScroll/index.tsx`
`plugins/vite/envRestartKeys.ts`

## Reviewer's Guide Adjusts how default tools are handled in manual skill-activation mode so that only discovery tools are disabled while other default tools remain available, adds support for excluding specific default tool IDs in the tools engine, and updates the UI to clarify auto/manual modes with tooltips. #### Sequence diagram for tool selection in auto vs manual skill-activation modes ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant ChatUI as ChatInput_SkillActivateMode participant Executor as StreamingExecutorActionImpl participant AgentService as AiAgentService participant ToolsEngine participant BuiltinTools as BuiltinToolsConfig User->>ChatUI: Select skillActivateMode (auto or manual) ChatUI-->>User: Show tooltip for selected mode rect rgb(230,255,230) Note over User,ToolsEngine: Auto mode User->>Executor: Send message (auto mode) Executor->>ToolsEngine: generateToolsDetailed(model, provider, toolIds, skipDefaultTools=disableTools, excludeDefaultToolIds=undefined) ToolsEngine->>BuiltinTools: Read defaultToolIds BuiltinTools-->>ToolsEngine: defaultToolIds including discovery tools ToolsEngine-->>Executor: ToolsGenerationResult with all default tools end rect rgb(230,230,255) Note over User,ToolsEngine: Manual mode User->>Executor: Send message (manual mode, client) Executor->>ToolsEngine: generateToolsDetailed(model, provider, toolIds, skipDefaultTools=disableTools, excludeDefaultToolIds=manualModeExcludeToolIds) ToolsEngine->>BuiltinTools: Read defaultToolIds BuiltinTools-->>ToolsEngine: defaultToolIds including discovery tools ToolsEngine->>ToolsEngine: Filter defaultToolIds by excludeDefaultToolIds ToolsEngine-->>Executor: ToolsGenerationResult without discovery tools end rect rgb(255,240,230) Note over User,ToolsEngine: Server-side execution User->>AgentService: Trigger server agent execution AgentService->>ToolsEngine: generateToolsDetailed(model, provider, toolIds, skipDefaultTools=false, excludeDefaultToolIds=manualModeExcludeToolIds when manual) ToolsEngine-->>AgentService: ToolsGenerationResult respecting mode end ``` #### Class diagram for updated tools generation and manual mode handling ```mermaid classDiagram class ToolsEngine { - string[] defaultToolIds + ToolsGenerationResult generateToolsDetailed(GenerateToolsParams params) } class GenerateToolsParams { + ToolsGenerationContext context + string[] excludeDefaultToolIds + string model + string provider + boolean skipDefaultTools + string[] toolIds } class StreamingExecutorActionImpl { + void executeStreaming() } class AiAgentService { + void execAgent() } class BuiltinToolsConfig { + string[] defaultToolIds + string[] alwaysOnToolIds + string[] manualModeExcludeToolIds } ToolsEngine --> GenerateToolsParams : uses StreamingExecutorActionImpl --> ToolsEngine : calls generateToolsDetailed AiAgentService --> ToolsEngine : calls generateToolsDetailed ToolsEngine --> BuiltinToolsConfig : reads defaultToolIds BuiltinToolsConfig <.. StreamingExecutorActionImpl : uses manualModeExcludeToolIds BuiltinToolsConfig <.. AiAgentService : uses manualModeExcludeToolIds ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Refine always-on and manual-mode tool configuration for built-in tools. |
  • Extend always-on tool list to include the skill store manifest so it is always enabled as a core system tool.
  • Introduce a manual-mode exclusion list containing tool and skill discovery tools so they are disabled when manual skill activation is selected.
| `packages/builtin-tools/src/index.ts` | | Allow the tools engine to exclude specific default tool IDs when generating tools. |
  • Extend GenerateToolsParams with an excludeDefaultToolIds field and document its purpose.
  • Compute effectiveDefaultToolIds by filtering defaultToolIds against excludeDefaultToolIds when provided.
  • Use effectiveDefaultToolIds instead of defaultToolIds when merging user tool IDs with defaults.
| `packages/context-engine/src/engine/tools/ToolsEngine.ts`
`packages/context-engine/src/engine/tools/types.ts` | | Clarify skill activation mode UI labels using tooltips instead of plain titles. |
  • Replace icon/title option props with label elements that wrap icons in Tooltip components for both auto and manual options.
| `src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/Tools/SkillActivateMode.tsx` | | Change manual skill-activation behavior to only exclude discovery tools while preserving other default tools if enabled externally. |
  • In the chat streaming executor, stop using skipDefaultTools for manual mode and instead pass manualModeExcludeToolIds via excludeDefaultToolIds while keeping skipDefaultTools tied only to the global disableTools flag.
  • In the AI agent service, remove skipDefaultTools usage for manual mode and similarly pass manualModeExcludeToolIds so manual mode no longer disables all default tools.

reads RuntimeExecutors --> ToolExecutionResult : consumes RuntimeExecutors --> MessageModel : persists MessageModel --> MessageMetadata : stores ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | ## Reviewer's Guide Adds first-class video generation support for additional providers (Zhipu, MiniMax, Volcengine, xAI) by defining video model cards and runtimes, introduces polling-based video completion handling (including immediate URL providers) with unified async task + billing flow, and enhances the video config UI and parameter schema (notably duration enums) to support the new models. #### Sequence diagram for video generation with polling vs webhook providers ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI as WebApp_UI participant API as videoRouter participant MR as ModelRuntime participant Prov as VideoProvider participant VGS as VideoGenerationService participant GM as GenerationModel participant ATM as AsyncTaskModel participant Billing as BillingService User->>UI: Configure video model and params UI->>API: createVideoGenerationRequest API->>ATM: create AsyncTask status Pending API->>GM: create Generation and Batch records API->>MR: createVideo(model, params) MR->>Prov: Provider specific video API request Prov-->>MR: CreateVideoResponse MR-->>API: CreateVideoResponse alt Provider returns videoUrl immediately (polling based) API->>VGS: processVideoForGeneration(videoUrl) VGS-->>API: processed asset metadata API->>GM: createAssetAndFile(generationId, asset, file, FileSourceVideoGeneration) API->>ATM: update AsyncTask ATM-->>API: status Success, duration, inferenceId API->>Billing: chargeAfterGenerate(model, provider, userId, latency, computePriceParams) Billing-->>API: billing complete API-->>UI: respond with Success and asset info else Provider uses webhook callback only API->>ATM: update AsyncTask status Processing, set inferenceId ATM-->>API: updated API-->>UI: respond with Accepted and asyncTaskId note over Prov,API: Later webhook call Prov-->>API: POST /api/webhooks/video/provider API->>MR: handleCreateVideoWebhook(body) MR-->>API: webhook result with videoUrl and inferenceId API->>VGS: processVideoForGeneration(videoUrl) VGS-->>API: processed asset metadata API->>GM: createAssetAndFile(...) API->>ATM: update AsyncTask status Success API->>Billing: chargeAfterGenerate(...) end ``` #### Class diagram for video runtime types and provider specific createVideo implementations ```mermaid classDiagram class CreateVideoPayload { +string model +RuntimeVideoGenParams params } class CreateVideoResponse_Base { +string inferenceId } class CreateVideoResponse_Immediate { +string inferenceId +string videoUrl } class CreateVideoResponse { } class RuntimeVideoGenParams { +string prompt +string imageUrl +string endImageUrl +number duration +string aspectRatio +boolean generateAudio +string resolution } class CreateVideoOptions { +string apiKey +string baseURL } class TaskResult~T~ { +T data +Error error +string status } class AsyncifyPolling~T,R~ { +TaskResult~R~ asyncifyPolling(checkStatus, pollingQuery, initialInterval, maxInterval, maxRetries, logger) } class MiniMaxVideoCreateResponse { +number status_code +string status_msg +string task_id } class MiniMaxVideoStatusResponse { +number status_code +string status_msg +string status +string file_id +number duration +number video_height +number video_width } class MiniMaxFileRetrieveResponse { +number status_code +string status_msg +string file_id +string download_url } class ZhipuVideoStatusResponse { +string id +string request_id +string task_status +string error_code +string error_message +string video_url +string cover_image_url } class XAIVideoStatusResponse { +string model +string status +string error_code +string error_message +string video_url +number duration } class LobeMinimaxAI { +createMiniMaxVideo(payload, options) CreateVideoResponse } class LobeZhipuAI { +createZhipuVideo(payload, options) CreateVideoResponse } class LobeXAI { +createXAIVideo(payload, options) CreateVideoResponse } class createMiniMaxVideo { +createMiniMaxVideo(payload, options) CreateVideoResponse } class createZhipuVideo { +createZhipuVideo(payload, options) CreateVideoResponse } class createXAIVideo { +createXAIVideo(payload, options) CreateVideoResponse } class queryVideoStatus_MiniMax { +queryVideoStatus(taskId, options) MiniMaxVideoStatusResponse } class retrieveVideoFile_MiniMax { +retrieveVideoFile(fileId, options) string } class queryVideoStatus_Zhipu { +queryVideoStatus(inferenceId, options) ZhipuVideoStatusResponse } class queryVideoStatus_XAI { +queryVideoStatus(requestId, options) XAIVideoStatusResponse } CreateVideoResponse <|-- CreateVideoResponse_Base CreateVideoResponse <|-- CreateVideoResponse_Immediate AsyncifyPolling~MiniMaxVideoStatusResponse,string~ ..> TaskResult~string~ AsyncifyPolling~ZhipuVideoStatusResponse,CreateVideoResponse~ ..> TaskResult~CreateVideoResponse~ AsyncifyPolling~XAIVideoStatusResponse,CreateVideoResponse~ ..> TaskResult~CreateVideoResponse~ LobeMinimaxAI ..> createMiniMaxVideo : uses LobeZhipuAI ..> createZhipuVideo : uses LobeXAI ..> createXAIVideo : uses createMiniMaxVideo ..> CreateVideoPayload createMiniMaxVideo ..> CreateVideoOptions createMiniMaxVideo ..> MiniMaxVideoCreateResponse createMiniMaxVideo ..> MiniMaxVideoStatusResponse createMiniMaxVideo ..> MiniMaxFileRetrieveResponse createMiniMaxVideo ..> AsyncifyPolling~MiniMaxVideoStatusResponse,string~ createMiniMaxVideo ..> queryVideoStatus_MiniMax createMiniMaxVideo ..> retrieveVideoFile_MiniMax createZhipuVideo ..> CreateVideoPayload createZhipuVideo ..> CreateVideoOptions createZhipuVideo ..> ZhipuVideoStatusResponse createZhipuVideo ..> AsyncifyPolling~ZhipuVideoStatusResponse,CreateVideoResponse~ createZhipuVideo ..> queryVideoStatus_Zhipu createXAIVideo ..> CreateVideoPayload createXAIVideo ..> CreateVideoOptions createXAIVideo ..> XAIVideoStatusResponse createXAIVideo ..> AsyncifyPolling~XAIVideoStatusResponse,CreateVideoResponse~ createXAIVideo ..> queryVideoStatus_XAI ``` #### Class diagram for video model parameter metadata and UI duration configuration ```mermaid classDiagram class VideoModelParamsMetaSchema { +number default +string description +number[] enum +number max +number min +number step +string type } class DurationParamMeta { +number default +number[] enum +number max +number min +number step } class useVideoGenerationConfigParam_Duration { +number value +number min +number max +number step +number[] enumValues +setValue(nextValue) } class DurationItem { +DurationItem() } class Segmented { +render(options, value, onChange) } class SliderWithInput { +render(value, min, max, step, onChange) } class I18nVideoNamespace { +string config_duration_seconds } VideoModelParamsMetaSchema <|-- DurationParamMeta DurationItem ..> useVideoGenerationConfigParam_Duration : uses DurationItem ..> Segmented : uses when enumValues not empty DurationItem ..> SliderWithInput : uses when enumValues empty DurationItem ..> I18nVideoNamespace : uses t config_duration_seconds useVideoGenerationConfigParam_Duration --> DurationParamMeta : returns meta ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce Zhipu video models and runtime implementation with polling-based video generation. |
  • Add multiple Zhipu video model cards with parameters and pricing and include them in the exported allModels list.
  • Implement createZhipuVideo with polling via asyncifyPolling, mapping standard video params to Zhipu CogVideoX API and returning a direct video URL when ready.
  • Wire Zhipu provider runtime to use createZhipuVideo and support polling from the generic video pipeline.
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/zhipu.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/providers/zhipu/index.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/providers/zhipu/createVideo.ts` | | Add MiniMax video models and runtime implementation with internal polling and file retrieval. |
  • Extend MiniMax model cards with several video models (Hailuo series and I2V/T2V variants) and include them in allModels.
  • Implement createMiniMaxVideo which creates a video task, polls task status via query/video_generation, then resolves a file_id to a download_url via files/retrieve, returning inferenceId + videoUrl.
  • Register createMiniMaxVideo on the MiniMax runtime so it participates in the common video generation flow.
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/minimax.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/providers/minimax/index.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/providers/minimax/createVideo.ts` | | Add Volcengine/Seedance and xAI video model cards plus xAI runtime support. |
  • Define multiple Volcengine Seedance video model cards (Pro/Pro Fast/Lite I2V/T2V) sharing or inlining parameter schemas, and add them to the volcengine allModels export.
  • Introduce an xAI Grok Imagine Video model card with duration/aspect ratio/resolution parameters and pricing and include it in allModels.
  • Implement createXAIVideo with polling against xAI /videos endpoints and register it on the xAI runtime.
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/volcengine.ts`
`packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/xai.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/providers/xai/index.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/providers/xai/createVideo.ts` | | Extend video generation pipeline to support providers that return finished video URLs directly as well as webhook-based flows. |
  • Broaden CreateVideoResponse type to optionally include a videoUrl field for polling-based providers.
  • Update the video lambda route to detect responses with videoUrl, immediately process and persist the video via VideoGenerationService, create associated file/asset records, mark the asyncTask as Success with duration, and trigger post-generation billing; otherwise fall back to the existing webhook-based Processing flow.
  • Initialize ModelRuntime for webhooks with a placeholder apiKey to satisfy runtime construction.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/types/video.ts`
`src/server/routers/lambda/video/index.ts`
`src/app/(backend)/api/webhooks/video/[provider]/route.ts`
`src/server/services/generation/video/* (usage)` | | Update shared video parameter schema and frontend config UI to support enum-based duration selection and localized labels. |
  • Relax VideoModelParamsMetaSchema.duration to optionally use an enum of numbers instead of required min/max, allowing models with fixed duration values.
  • Adjust ConfigPanel DurationItem to read enumValues from useVideoGenerationConfigParam and render a Segmented control of discrete second options when present, falling back to the existing SliderWithInput otherwise.
  • Add a localized suffix for seconds in the video translations used for the segmented duration labels.
| `packages/model-bank/src/standard-parameters/video.ts`
`src/routes/(main)/video/_layout/ConfigPanel/index.tsx`
`src/locales/default/video.ts` | ### Possibly linked issues - **#[Request] Support text-to-video and image-to-video generation models**: The PR implements Seedance and other video models, enabling text/image-to-video generation as requested in the issue. ---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).

body:
@hezhijie0327

1. The advantage of webhooks is that there's no limit on server response time. Vercel's free tier supports a maximum of 5 minutes, so for models that take a long time to process, it's easy to time out — especially in video generation scenarios. That's why I originally implemented video support using webhooks.
2. It looks like most of your implementation uses HTTP polling. I see you're directly calling the async `processVideoPolling` synchronously. First, you're not using Vercel's `after` method, which could cause the polling to be killed mid-way by Vercel. Also, our async task flow could actually follow the image generation flow — just add an async route.

---
> This comment was translated by Claude.

<details>
<summary>Original Content</summary>

@hezhijie0327

1. webhook 的优点在于对服务器响应时间没限制，vercel 免费版支持最长 5min， 对于某些耗时很长的模型就很容易超时，尤其是视频场景，所以对于视频，我一开始就是用 webhook 支持的
2. 你这边好像大都是采用 http poll 实现的， 我看你是直接同步调用异步的 processVideoPlling, 首先你没使用 vercel after 方法， 这可能会导致 polling 到一半被 vercel 直接 kill，然后我们 async task 的流程其实可以参考 image 生成流程， 加个 async route
</details>

## Reviewer's Guide Adds a comprehensive Vitest test suite for the topic reference server runtime, exercising the factory’s context validation and the TopicReferenceExecutionRuntime.getTopicContext business logic across success, fallback, and error paths using mocked TopicModel and MessageModel. ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce unit tests for topicReferenceRuntime identifier and factory validation logic. |
  • Mock TopicModel and MessageModel using vi.mock with shared spies for findById and query methods.
  • Assert runtime identifier matches TopicReferenceIdentifier and its literal value.
  • Verify factory throws when required context properties (serverDB, userId) are missing.
  • Verify factory returns a runtime instance exposing a getTopicContext function when context is valid.
| `src/server/services/toolExecution/serverRuntimes/__tests__/topicReference.test.ts` | | Add exhaustive tests for getTopicContext behavior covering topic lookup, context generation, and error handling. |
  • Initialize runtime in a beforeEach with a minimal valid ToolExecutionContext and reset all mocks between tests.
  • Validate input handling for missing or undefined topicId, expecting structured error responses.
  • Cover topic-not-found behavior, ensuring proper error message and correct call to TopicModel.findById.
  • Test happy path where topic has historySummary, ensuring correctly formatted markdown content and that messages are not queried.
  • Test fallback path when historySummary is absent, including agentId/groupId propagation to MessageModel.query and defaulting to undefined when not present on the topic.
  • Assert message list truncation to the last 30 entries and filtering out empty/whitespace/null message contents.
  • Verify role-based formatting for user/assistant and generic lowercased role rendering for other roles like system and tool.
  • Exercise error handling for TopicModel and MessageModel failures, including both Error instances and non-Error throw values, asserting error response shape and message content.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds batch query helper methods to UserModel and MessageModel to efficiently fetch users by multiple IDs and check which users have messages, with empty-input guards and consistent static method patterns. #### Class diagram for updated UserModel and MessageModel batch query methods ```mermaid classDiagram class UserModel { +static findByEmail(db LobeChatDatabase, email string) Promise +static findByIds(db LobeChatDatabase, ids string[]) Promise +static getUserApiKeys(db LobeChatDatabase, id string) Promise } class MessageModel { +static checkUsersHaveMessages(db LobeChatDatabase, userIds string[]) Promise> } class LobeChatDatabase class User class UserApiKey UserModel ..> LobeChatDatabase : uses MessageModel ..> LobeChatDatabase : uses UserModel ..> User : returns UserModel ..> UserApiKey : returns MessageModel ..> Set : returns MessageModel ..> string : userIds ``` #### Flow diagram for MessageModel.checkUsersHaveMessages logic ```mermaid flowchart TD A[start checkUsersHaveMessages] --> B[Receive db and userIds] B --> C{userIds length == 0?} C -- Yes --> D[Return new empty Set] C -- No --> E[Run SELECT userId FROM messages WHERE userId IN userIds GROUP BY userId] E --> F[Map result rows to userId list] F --> G[Return new Set from userId list] D --> H[end] G --> H[end] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce a batch message-existence check for multiple users. |
  • Add static method that takes a DB handle and list of user IDs and returns a Set of IDs that have at least one message.
  • Guard against empty user ID arrays by returning an empty Set early.
  • Implement query using SELECT of userId from messages with WHERE userId IN (...) and GROUP BY userId to deduplicate results.
| `packages/database/src/models/message.ts` | | Introduce a batch user lookup by IDs. |
  • Add static method that takes a DB handle and array of user IDs and returns matching user records.
  • Guard against empty ID arrays by returning an empty array early.
  • Implement query using users.findMany with WHERE id IN (...), following existing query patterns.
| `packages/database/src/models/user.ts` | ---

You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. ## Reviewer's Guide Adds a lightweight browser-based device fingerprint utility for referral anti-abuse, introduces a new pending_reward referral status in user preference types, and extends subscription locale copy with reward delay messaging. #### Sequence diagram for device fingerprint generation flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant DeviceFingerprint as getDeviceFingerprint participant Signals as collectRawSignals participant Canvas as getCanvasFingerprint participant WebGL as getWebGLInfo participant Hasher as hashString participant Crypto as crypto.subtle participant Fallback as djb2Hex Caller->>DeviceFingerprint: getDeviceFingerprint() activate DeviceFingerprint DeviceFingerprint->>Signals: collectRawSignals() activate Signals Signals->>Canvas: getCanvasFingerprint() activate Canvas Canvas-->>Signals: canvasDataUrl or empty deactivate Canvas Signals->>WebGL: getWebGLInfo() activate WebGL WebGL-->>Signals: vendorRenderer or ## Reviewer's Guide This PR updates the xAI provider runtime to strip unsupported penalty parameters from payloads for xAI reasoning models (e.g., grok-4) across both Chat Completions and Responses flows, while leaving non-reasoning models untouched and adding regression tests to verify the behavior. #### Sequence diagram for xAI chatCompletion payload pruning ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Developer participant LobeXAI participant ChatRuntime participant PayloadHandler participant XAIClient Developer->>LobeXAI: chat(requestPayload) LobeXAI->>ChatRuntime: handle chatCompletion ChatRuntime->>PayloadHandler: handlePayload(payload) PayloadHandler->>PayloadHandler: pruneUnsupportedReasoningParameters(payload) PayloadHandler-->>ChatRuntime: sanitizedPayload ChatRuntime->>XAIClient: chat.completions.create(sanitizedPayload) XAIClient-->>ChatRuntime: ReadableStream ChatRuntime-->>LobeXAI: stream LobeXAI-->>Developer: response stream ``` #### Class diagram for updated xAI provider runtime payload handling ```mermaid classDiagram class LobeXAI { } class XAIModelCard { +string id } class ChatStreamPayload { +string model +float frequency_penalty +float presence_penalty +string[] stop } class UtilityFunctions { +bool isXAIReasoningModel(string model) +ChatStreamPayload pruneUnsupportedReasoningParameters(ChatStreamPayload payload) } class ChatCompletionConfig { +ChatStreamPayload handlePayload(ChatStreamPayload payload) +bool useResponse } class ResponsesConfig { +ChatStreamPayload handlePayload(ChatStreamPayload payload) } class OpenAICompatibleRuntimeConfig { +string baseURL +ChatCompletionConfig chatCompletion +ResponsesConfig responses } LobeXAI --> OpenAICompatibleRuntimeConfig : created_with OpenAICompatibleRuntimeConfig o--> ChatCompletionConfig OpenAICompatibleRuntimeConfig o--> ResponsesConfig ChatCompletionConfig ..> UtilityFunctions : uses_pruneUnsupportedReasoningParameters ResponsesConfig ..> UtilityFunctions : uses_pruneUnsupportedReasoningParameters UtilityFunctions ..> ChatStreamPayload XAIModelCard ..> LobeXAI : used_by_runtime ``` #### Flow diagram for pruning unsupported reasoning parameters ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start pruneUnsupportedReasoningParameters] --> B[Read payload.model] B --> C{isXAIReasoningModel?} C -- No --> D[Return original payload] C -- Yes --> E[Create new payload copy] E --> F[Set frequency_penalty to undefined] F --> G[Set presence_penalty to undefined] G --> H[Set stop to undefined] H --> I[Return pruned payload] subgraph isXAIReasoningModel J[Input model string] J --> K{model includes non-reasoning?} K -- Yes --> L[Return false] K -- No --> M{model equals grok-3-mini or grok-4 or grok-code-fast-1 or contains multi-agent or contains reasoning} M -- Yes --> N[Return true] M -- No --> O[Return false] end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add centralized helpers to detect xAI reasoning models and prune unsupported parameters before sending requests. |
  • Introduce an isXAIReasoningModel helper that identifies xAI reasoning models by exact ID or naming patterns while explicitly excluding non-reasoning variants.
  • Add pruneUnsupportedReasoningParameters that, for reasoning models, clones the payload and nulls out frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, and stop fields to avoid xAI rejections.
  • Wire pruneUnsupportedReasoningParameters into the chatCompletion.handlePayload hook so all chat-completion requests for reasoning models are sanitized before hitting the client.
  • Apply pruneUnsupportedReasoningParameters inside responses.handlePayload while preserving the existing enabledSearch/tool augmentation behavior.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/xai/index.ts` | | Extend xAI provider tests to cover penalty pruning for reasoning vs. non-reasoning models and to stub chat.completions calls. |
  • Spy on instance.client.chat.completions.create and responses.create to avoid real network calls and allow payload inspection.
  • Add a chatCompletion.handlePayload test that verifies frequency_penalty and presence_penalty are removed for grok-4 reasoning models.
  • Add a complementary test that verifies penalty parameters pass through unchanged for non-reasoning models such as grok-4-fast-non-reasoning.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/xai/index.test.ts` | ### Possibly linked issues - **#Grok AI Error**: PR prunes presence/frequency penalties for xAI reasoning models, directly resolving the Grok presencePenalty error described. ---

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide This PR updates the OpenAI-compatible message conversion pipeline to strip internal `thinking` content parts from user/assistant message histories before building chat payloads, while preserving all other content types and provider-supported reasoning fields, to prevent DeepSeek/OpenAI-compatible requests from failing on unsupported message variants. #### Sequence diagram for OpenAI-compatible message conversion with thinking filter ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller participant OpenAIContextBuilder participant isInternalThinkingContentPart participant convertMessageContent participant OpenAIAPI Caller->>OpenAIContextBuilder: convertOpenAIMessages(messages, options) loop for each message alt message.content is string OpenAIContextBuilder-->>OpenAIContextBuilder: use content as is else message.content is array loop for each contentPart in message.content OpenAIContextBuilder->>isInternalThinkingContentPart: check contentPart isInternalThinkingContentPart-->>OpenAIContextBuilder: isThinking alt isThinking is true OpenAIContextBuilder-->>OpenAIContextBuilder: skip contentPart else isThinking is false OpenAIContextBuilder->>convertMessageContent: convert contentPart convertMessageContent-->>OpenAIContextBuilder: convertedPart end end end end OpenAIContextBuilder-->>OpenAIAPI: create chat completion payload OpenAIAPI-->>Caller: response ``` #### Class diagram for updated OpenAI context builder content handling ```mermaid classDiagram class OpenAIContextBuilder { +convertMessageContent(content, options) +convertOpenAIMessages(messages, options) +convertOpenAIResponseInputs(messages, options) +isInternalThinkingContentPart(content) } class ExtendedChatCompletionContentPart { } class OpenAI_ChatCompletionContentPart { } class UserMessageContentPart { +type } class OpenAICompatibleContentPart { <> } OpenAIContextBuilder ..> ExtendedChatCompletionContentPart : uses OpenAIContextBuilder ..> OpenAI_ChatCompletionContentPart : uses OpenAIContextBuilder ..> UserMessageContentPart : uses OpenAIContextBuilder ..> OpenAICompatibleContentPart : uses OpenAICompatibleContentPart o-- ExtendedChatCompletionContentPart : option OpenAICompatibleContentPart o-- OpenAI_ChatCompletionContentPart : option OpenAICompatibleContentPart o-- UserMessageContentPart : option OpenAIContextBuilder ..> UserMessageContentPart : filters type thinking ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Filter internal `thinking` content parts from OpenAI-compatible message payloads while leaving other content processing intact. |
  • Extended type imports to include UserMessageContentPart and defined a unified OpenAICompatibleContentPart union type for content-part handling.
  • Introduced an isInternalThinkingContentPart type guard to identify internal `thinking` content parts among supported content variants.
  • Updated convertOpenAIMessages to filter out `thinking` content parts from message.content arrays before invoking convertMessageContent, ensuring they are never serialized into outgoing payloads.
  • Updated convertOpenAIResponseInputs to early-return undefined for `thinking` content parts during async mapping over message.content, effectively omitting them from the final request payload while preserving all other content-type behavior.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/contextBuilders/openai.ts` |

You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Adds a new jsonb `settings` column to the `agent_bot_providers` table (and schema) with a default empty object, via an idempotent SQL migration, and updates schema docs/metadata accordingly. #### ER diagram for updated agent_bot_providers table with settings column ```mermaid erDiagram agent_bot_providers { uuid id PK uuid agentId text platform text applicationId text credentials jsonb settings "DEFAULT {}" boolean enabled "DEFAULT true NOT NULL" timestamptz createdAt timestamptz updatedAt } agents { uuid id PK } agents ||--o{ agent_bot_providers : has_many ``` #### Class diagram for updated agentBotProviders schema with settings field ```mermaid classDiagram class agentBotProviders { +uuid id +uuid agentId +string platform +string applicationId +string credentials +Record~string, unknown~ settings +boolean enabled +Date createdAt +Date updatedAt } class AgentBotProviderSettings { +unknown value +Record~string, unknown~ toRecord() } agentBotProviders "1" *-- "1" AgentBotProviderSettings : has_settings ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add typed jsonb `settings` field with default to the agent bot providers application schema. |
  • Extend the Drizzle schema for agentBotProviders to include a jsonb `settings` column typed as Record.
  • Set a default value of an empty object for the new `settings` column so existing rows get `{}`.
  • Slightly generalize an existing index comment from webhook-specific to generic lookup wording.
| `packages/database/src/schemas/agentBotProvider.ts` | | Introduce an idempotent database migration to add the `settings` column at the SQL level and register it in migration metadata and docs. |
  • Create migration SQL that alters `agent_bot_providers` to add a jsonb `settings` column with default '{}'::jsonb, guarded by IF NOT EXISTS for safe re-runs.
  • Add/update DBML schema documentation to reflect the new `settings` column on agent_bot_providers.

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide This PR adds two new unit test suites for the server utilities in `packages/utils/src/server/`, significantly expanding coverage for SSE formatting/writing helpers and authentication header/token extraction logic, including various edge cases and error conditions. ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add unit tests for SSE utilities covering event formatting, headers, and writer helpers. |
  • Introduce a comprehensive test suite for `formatSSEEvent`, including optional fields, multiline data, JSON serialization, and invalid inputs.
  • Add tests for `createSSEWriter` helper methods (`writeEvent`, `writeConnection`, `writeError`, `writeHeartbeat`, `writeStreamEvent`) verifying emitted SSE strings and error behavior.
  • Add tests for `createSSEHeaders` to validate correct header generation and failure modes.
| `packages/utils/src/server/sse.test.ts` | | Add unit tests for auth utilities covering token extraction from headers with edge cases. |
  • Add tests for `extractBearerToken` to cover standard, malformed, and edge-case Authorization headers, including case-insensitivity, extra whitespace, and null/undefined inputs.
  • Add tests for `extractOidcAuthToken` mirroring bearer token scenarios to ensure consistent behavior across token types.
  • Mock server-only imports (e.g., `next/headers`, `@/auth`) to keep tests pure and isolated from framework behavior.
| `packages/utils/src/server/auth.test.ts` |

wiring them into both interactive and headless contexts. #### Sequence diagram for LexicalRenderer headless rendering of action and topic tags ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant RichTextMessage participant LexicalRenderer participant ActionTagNode participant ReferTopicNode participant ActionTagView participant ReferTopicView participant ChatStore participant TopicSelectors RichTextMessage->>RichTextMessage: compute value from editorState RichTextMessage->>LexicalRenderer: render(extraNodes=[ActionTagNode, ReferTopicNode], value) loop for each ActionTagNode in document LexicalRenderer->>ActionTagNode: renderHeadless(context) ActionTagNode->>ActionTagView: createElement(category, label, key) ActionTagView-->>LexicalRenderer: ReactElement end loop for each ReferTopicNode in document LexicalRenderer->>ReferTopicNode: renderHeadless(context) ReferTopicNode->>ReferTopicView: createElement(topicId, fallbackTitle, key) ReferTopicView->>ChatStore: useChatStore(selector) ReferTopicView->>TopicSelectors: getTopicById(topicId) ChatStore-->>ReferTopicView: topic state ReferTopicView-->>LexicalRenderer: ReactElement end LexicalRenderer-->>RichTextMessage: rendered React tree ``` #### Class diagram for refactored user message rendering and headless nodes ```mermaid classDiagram direction LR class RichTextMessage { +editorState unknown +value SerializedEditorState +render() } class LexicalRenderer { +extraNodes ActionTagNode[] +extraNodes ReferTopicNode[] +value SerializedEditorState +variant string +render() }
