body:
## Reviewer's Guide Implements desktop-specific version reporting in the About screen by fetching the Electron app version via a new IPC method, exposing it through the electron system service, and centralizing the version selection logic in a small helper so the UI shows the desktop version (with canary suffix) when available and falls back to the web version otherwise. #### Sequence diagram for fetching and displaying desktop app version in About screen ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant VersionComponent participant ElectronSystemService participant IpcSystemChannel participant SystemController participant ElectronApp User->>VersionComponent: Open About screen activate VersionComponent VersionComponent->>ElectronSystemService: getAppVersion() activate ElectronSystemService ElectronSystemService->>IpcSystemChannel: system.getAppVersion() activate IpcSystemChannel IpcSystemChannel->>SystemController: getAppVersion() activate SystemController SystemController->>ElectronApp: getVersion() activate ElectronApp ElectronApp-->>SystemController: version_with_optional_canary deactivate ElectronApp SystemController-->>IpcSystemChannel: version_with_optional_canary deactivate SystemController IpcSystemChannel-->>ElectronSystemService: version_with_optional_canary deactivate IpcSystemChannel ElectronSystemService-->>VersionComponent: version_with_optional_canary deactivate ElectronSystemService VersionComponent->>VersionComponent: displayVersion = getDisplayVersion(desktopAppVersion, CURRENT_VERSION) VersionComponent-->>User: Render Tag v{displayVersion} deactivate VersionComponent ``` #### Updated class diagram for desktop version retrieval and display ```mermaid classDiagram class SystemController { +getLocale() string +getAppVersion() string +updateLocale(locale string) void } class ElectronApp { +getVersion() string } class ElectronSystemService { +getAppState() Promise~any~ +getAppVersion() Promise~string~ +closeWindow() Promise~void~ } class VersionComponent { -isDesktop boolean -updaterState UpdaterState -buildChannel string -desktopAppVersion string +render() JSXElement } class VersionDisplayHelper { +getDisplayVersion(desktopAppVersion string, webVersion string) string } SystemController ..> ElectronApp : calls ElectronSystemService ..> SystemController : IPC system.getAppVersion VersionComponent ..> ElectronSystemService : uses VersionComponent ..> VersionDisplayHelper : uses getDisplayVersion ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | About screen now displays a computed display version that prefers the desktop app version over the web version when running in the desktop app. |
  • Introduce local state to store the desktop app version alongside the existing updater state and build channel state.
  • Compute a displayVersion value via a new helper that takes both the desktop and web versions and chooses the desktop value when present.
  • Use the computed displayVersion in the Tag instead of directly rendering the web CURRENT_VERSION.
  • Add a desktop-only effect to request the app version from the electron system service and store it in state.
| `src/routes/(main)/settings/about/features/Version.tsx` | | Expose the Electron app version over IPC and through the electron system service for use in the renderer. |
  • Add a new IPC method on the desktop SystemController that returns app.getVersion().
  • Add a corresponding getAppVersion method on ElectronSystemService that calls into the new IPC endpoint.
| `apps/desktop/src/main/controllers/SystemCtr.ts`
`src/services/electron/system.ts` | | Centralize display-version selection logic in a small utility and cover it with tests. |
  • Create a getDisplayVersion helper that trims the desktop app version and falls back to the web version when the desktop version is missing or empty.
  • Add a unit test file for the version display helper to validate fallback and normalization behavior.
| `src/routes/(main)/settings/about/features/versionDisplay.ts`
`src/routes/(main)/settings/about/features/versionDisplay.test.ts` | ---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. ## Reviewer's Guide Adds OpenCode Zen as a first-class, OpenAI-compatible model provider, wiring its model catalog into the model bank defaults and provider runtime map so it appears as a selectable provider and uses the shared OpenAI-compatible runtime implementation. #### Sequence diagram for chat request via OpenCodeZen provider ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant Settings as SettingsUI participant ModelBank as ModelBank_opencodezen participant RuntimeMap as providerRuntimeMap participant Runtime as LobeOpenCodeZenAI participant API as OpenCodeZen_API User->>Settings: Select OpenCodeZen provider and model Settings->>ModelBank: Load opencodezen allModels ModelBank-->>Settings: Return model metadata (pricing, abilities) User->>Settings: Send chat message Settings->>RuntimeMap: Resolve runtime for provider id opencodezen RuntimeMap-->>Settings: Return LobeOpenCodeZenAI Settings->>Runtime: createChatCompletion(request) Runtime->>API: POST /chat or /responses (baseURL https://opencode.ai/zen/v1) API-->>Runtime: Model response Runtime-->>Settings: Normalized chat result Settings-->>User: Render assistant reply ``` #### Class diagram for OpenCodeZen provider integration ```mermaid classDiagram class ModelProvider { <> +OpenAI +OpenCodeZen +Ollama +OllamaCloud +OpenRouter +Perplexity +PPIO } class ModelProviderCard { <> +string id +string name +string description +string url +string apiKeyUrl +string modelsUrl +object modelList +string checkModel +object settings +AIChatModelCard[] chatModels } class OpenCodeZenProviderCard { +string id = opencodezen +string name = OpenCode~space~Zen +string description +string url = https://opencode.ai/zen +string apiKeyUrl = https://opencode.ai/auth +string modelsUrl = https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models +object modelList +string checkModel = gpt-5.4-mini +object settings +AIChatModelCard[] chatModels = [] } class AIChatModelCard { <> +string id +string displayName +string description +boolean enabled +number contextWindowTokens +number maxOutput +object abilities +object pricing +string type } class OpenCodeZenChatModels { +AIChatModelCard[] opencodezenChatModels +AIChatModelCard[] allModels } class providerRuntimeMap { +LobeOpenCodeZenAI opencodezen } class LobeOpenCodeZenAI { +string baseURL = https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 +ModelProvider provider = ModelProvider.OpenCodeZen +object debug } class createOpenAICompatibleRuntime { +LobeOpenCodeZenAI create(config) } ModelProvider <|-- OpenCodeZenProviderCard : uses_enum ModelProvider <.. LobeOpenCodeZenAI : identifies_provider ModelProviderCard <|.. OpenCodeZenProviderCard AIChatModelCard "*" <.. OpenCodeZenChatModels : contains OpenCodeZenChatModels ..> OpenCodeZenProviderCard : provides_models createOpenAICompatibleRuntime ..> LobeOpenCodeZenAI : constructs providerRuntimeMap o--> LobeOpenCodeZenAI : opencodezen_key OpenCodeZenProviderCard ..> ModelProvider : OpenCodeZen ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce OpenCode Zen chat model catalog with metadata and pricing, and export it through the model bank. |
  • Define OpenCode Zen chat models with abilities, context windows, pricing strategies, and enablement flags, including default-free and paid models
  • Aggregate all OpenCode Zen models into a single exported list
  • Wire the new OpenCode Zen model list into the global AI model exports and default model list builder

  • Add OpenCode Zen to the default provider list and default model list so it is available out of the box
  • Export the OpenCode Zen provider card from the provider index

body:
## Reviewer's Guide Adds a new GitHub Actions workflow that uses the existing Claude Code integration to automatically assign PR reviewers based on changed files, team assignment rules, and related issues, plus a new prompt guide describing the reviewer-assignment procedure. #### Sequence diagram for PR event to automatic reviewer assignment ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor Developer participant GitHub participant Workflow as claude_pr_assign_workflow participant Job as assign_reviewer_job participant ClaudeAction as claude_code_action participant GitHubAPI Developer->>GitHub: Open PR or add label trigger:assign GitHub-->>Workflow: pull_request_target event Workflow->>Workflow: Check actor_type != Bot Workflow->>Workflow: Check action == opened or labeled(trigger:assign) alt Conditions satisfied Workflow->>Job: Start job assign-reviewer Job->>Job: Set permissions contents, pull-requests, issues Job->>Job: actions/checkout@v6 Job->>Job: Copy prompts to /tmp/claude-prompts Job->>ClaudeAction: Run anthropics/claude-code-action with prompts and tokens ClaudeAction->>GitHubAPI: gh pr view PR_NUMBER ClaudeAction->>GitHubAPI: gh issue view ISSUE_NUMBER (if referenced) ClaudeAction->>ClaudeAction: Map files to feature areas ClaudeAction->>ClaudeAction: Determine reviewers using team-assignment ClaudeAction->>GitHubAPI: gh pr comment PR_NUMBER with reviewer mentions opt Event was labeled trigger:assign Job->>GitHubAPI: gh pr edit PR_NUMBER --remove-label trigger:assign end else Conditions not satisfied Workflow-->>GitHub: Job skipped end ``` #### Flow diagram for Claude reviewer assignment decision logic ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start assignment PR_NUMBER, REPOSITORY, PR_AUTHOR known] --> B[Call gh pr view PR_NUMBER Get title, body, files, labels, author] B --> C[Analyze changed file paths Map to feature areas using team_assignment] C --> D[From title, body, paths Infer primary and secondary areas] D --> E{Does PR body reference issue} E -->|No| H[Candidate reviewers from feature area owners] E -->|Yes| F[Extract ISSUE_NUMBER from PR body] F --> G[Call gh issue view ISSUE_NUMBER Get author and commenters] G --> H2[Intersect issue participants with team_assignment members] H2 --> H H --> I[Filter out PR_AUTHOR from candidate reviewers] I --> J{Any candidates left} J -->|Yes| K[Select primary reviewer and optional secondary based on areas] J -->|No| L[Fallback reviewer @arvinxx] K --> M[Build single comment body mentioning all reviewers] L --> M M --> N[Call gh pr comment PR_NUMBER with comment body] N --> O[End One comment posted, no PR labels modified] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce Claude-powered PR reviewer auto-assignment workflow in CI. |
  • Add a pull_request_target-based workflow that runs on PR open or when a trigger label is added, while skipping bot-authored PRs
  • Configure permissions, repo checkout, and prompt copying for Claude Code to run with repository and PR context
  • Invoke anthropics/claude-code-action with security rules, restricted tool usage, and a prompt tailored for PR reviewer selection and commenting
  • Automatically remove the trigger:assign label after manual triggering to keep PR labels clean
| `.github/workflows/claude-pr-assign.yml` | | Define a prompt guide for how Claude should determine and assign PR reviewers. |
  • Document a stepwise process for fetching PR metadata and changed files via gh CLI
  • Describe heuristics to map changed file paths and feature-related keywords to feature areas and team members using team-assignment.md
  • Specify use of related issue participants as preferred reviewers and fallback logic when ownership is unclear
  • Constrain behavior to posting a single reviewer-mention comment without modifying labels or assigning the PR author
| `.claude/prompts/pr-assign.md` | ---
Tips and commands #### Interacting with Sourcery - **Trigger a new review:** Comment `@sourcery-ai review` on the pull request. - **Continue discussions:** Reply directly to Sourcery's review comments. - **Generate a GitHub issue from a review comment:** Ask Sourcery to create an issue from a review comment by replying to it. You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Adds a new unit test suite for hashApiKey in apiKeyHash.ts, validating HMAC-SHA256 hashing behavior, error handling, determinism, and sensitivity to inputs and secrets via environment-variable-based configuration. ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Introduce comprehensive unit tests for hashApiKey covering normal behavior, edge cases, and error paths. |
  • Add a new Jest test file for the apiKeyHash server utility
  • Mock process environment variables in beforeEach/afterEach to control the API key secret used by hashApiKey
  • Assert that an error is thrown when the required secret env var is missing
  • Verify correct behavior with an empty-string secret value
  • Check that hash outputs are 64-character lowercase hex strings

## Reviewer's Guide Adds full support for Xiaomi MiMo V2 models (mimo-v2-pro, mimo-v2-omni, enhanced mimo-v2-flash) including pricing/metadata, provider payload handling for reasoning content, built‑in search tools, and streaming support for XiaomiMiMo-specific citation annotations and debugging, with expanded tests across provider, model list, and OpenAI stream handling. #### Sequence diagram for XiaomiMiMo streaming annotations and grounding events ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant Backend participant OpenAIStream participant XiaomiMiMoAPI Client->>Backend: Send chat request (model mimo-v2-omni) Backend->>XiaomiMiMoAPI: POST /chat.completions XiaomiMiMoAPI-->>Backend: Streaming response (ReadableStream) Backend->>OpenAIStream: Wrap XiaomiMiMo stream loop For each incoming chunk XiaomiMiMoAPI-->>OpenAIStream: Chunk with choices[0].delta OpenAIStream->>OpenAIStream: Increment streamContext.chunkIndex alt First chunk with annotations OpenAIStream->>OpenAIStream: Detect delta.annotations in chunkIndex 0 OpenAIStream-->>Backend: StreamProtocolChunk type grounding Backend-->>Client: SSE event grounding with citations else Subsequent chunks with text OpenAIStream->>OpenAIStream: Extract delta.content OpenAIStream-->>Backend: StreamProtocolChunk type text Backend-->>Client: SSE event text with partial content end alt Chunk with finish_reason OpenAIStream->>OpenAIStream: Map finish_reason to stop OpenAIStream-->>Backend: StreamProtocolChunk type stop Backend-->>Client: SSE event stop end end ``` #### Updated class diagram for XiaomiMiMo V2 chat model cards ```mermaid classDiagram class AIChatModelCard { +string id +string displayName +string description +boolean enabled +number contextWindowTokens +number maxOutput +Abilities abilities +Pricing pricing +Settings settings +string type +string releasedAt } class Abilities { +boolean functionCall +boolean reasoning +boolean search +boolean structuredOutput +boolean vision +boolean video } class Pricing { +string currency +PricingUnit[] units } class PricingUnit { +string name +string unit +string strategy +number rate +Lookup lookup } class Lookup { +Record~string, number~ prices +string[] pricingParams } class Settings { +string[] extendParams +string searchImpl } class XiaomiMiMoProModel { +id = "mimo-v2-pro" +displayName = "MiMo-V2 Pro" XiaomiMiMoFlashModel { +id = "mimo-v2-flash" +displayName = "MiMo-V2 Flash" +contextWindowTokens = 262144 +maxOutput = 65536 } AIChatModelCard <|-- XiaomiMiMoProModel AIChatModelCard <|-- XiaomiMiMoOmniModel AIChatModelCard <|-- XiaomiMiMoFlashModel AIChatModelCard --> Abilities AIChatModelCard --> Pricing AIChatModelCard --> Settings Pricing --> PricingUnit PricingUnit --> Lookup ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Enhance XiaomiMiMo provider payload handling to support built-in web search, reasoning_content mapping, and keep existing sampling/stream defaults. |
  • Extend handlePayload to accept enabledSearch and tools, injecting a XiaomiMiMo web_search tool when enabledSearch is true.
  • Map assistant message.reasoning.content into reasoning_content, including empty strings when thinking mode is enabled, ensuring assistant history messages carry reasoning_content.
  • Normalize messages by stripping the original reasoning field while preserving/deriving reasoning_content when present.
  • Continue mapping max_tokens to max_completion_tokens, defaulting stream to true, and clamping temperature and top_p within provider-specific ranges.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/xiaomimimo/index.ts` | | Expand XiaomiMiMo model metadata to include mimo-v2-pro and mimo-v2-omni and update mimo-v2-flash capabilities, pricing, and limits. |
  • Add a full configuration card for mimo-v2-pro with long context window, reasoning/search/structured output abilities, pricing tiers, and reasoning/search settings.
  • Add a full configuration card for the multimodal mimo-v2-omni model with vision/video support, pricing, and reasoning/search settings.
  • Update the existing mimo-v2-flash card with richer description, explicit pricing, adjusted maxOutput, and search/structuredOutput abilities.
| `packages/model-bank/src/aiModels/xiaomimimo.ts` | | Support XiaomiMiMo-specific annotations (url_citation) in the OpenAI-style streaming protocol by emitting grounding events from the first chunk’s citations. |
  • Introduce chunkIndex in StreamContext and increment it per chunk within transformOpenAIStream to detect the first chunk.
  • When the first chunk’s delta.annotations is a non-empty array, emit a single grounding event containing simplified citation objects (title and url) instead of treating them as text.
  • Ensure subsequent chunks emit only text events without duplicating annotations.
  • Slightly refactor processMarkdownBase64Images to compute cleanedText inline without a separate mutable variable.
| `packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/openai/openai.ts`
`packages/model-runtime/src/core/streams/protocol.ts` | | Broaden XiaomiMiMo provider and OpenAI stream tests to cover new models, reasoning_content transformations, debug toggling, and XiaomiMiMo annotations handling. |
  • Switch provider tests from using gpt-4o to mimo-v2-flash as the default model id for payload handling checks.
  • Add tests ensuring reasoning objects are transformed into reasoning_content strings, including for empty reasoning content and messages without reasoning.
  • Add a Debug Configuration test block for DEBUG_XIAOMIMIMO_CHAT_COMPLETION toggling.
  • Rewrite and extend models-list tests to use a mock client and validate behavior for multiple, single, empty, and heterogeneous XiaomiMiMo model ids while preserving API-provided properties.
  • Add an OpenAIStream test that simulates XiaomiMiMo url_citation annotations over three chunks and asserts the grounding and text events sequence.
  • Keep existing MiniMax annotations tests intact for regression coverage.

body:
Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide This PR updates multiple dataset presets so that an optional `case_id` field is recognized and preserved during dataset ingestion, enabling external tools and internal case tracking to reliably associate records by ID. #### Sequence diagram for dataset ingestion with optional case_id capture ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI as DatasetUploadUI participant Importer as DatasetImporter participant Presets as DatasetPresetConfig participant Store as DatasetStorage participant Tracker as CaseTrackingService User->>UI: Upload dataset file UI->>Importer: sendFile(file) Importer->>Presets: getPreset(formatKey) Presets-->>Importer: DatasetPreset(requiredFields, optionalFields) Importer->>Importer: validate requiredFields Importer->>Importer: map fields including optional case_id alt row has case_id Importer->>Store: saveRecord(input, expected, case_id) Store-->>Importer: recordId Importer->>Tracker: linkCase(recordId, case_id) else row missing case_id Importer->>Store: saveRecord(input, expected) Store-->>Importer: recordId end Importer-->>UI: ImportResult(total, successes, failures) ``` #### Flow diagram for dataset presets recognizing optional case_id ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Start dataset ingestion] --> B[Select dataset preset] B --> C{Preset supports case_id in optionalFields?} C -->|Yes| D[Check row for case_id column] C -->|No| G[Ignore case_id in incoming rows] D --> E{Row has case_id value?} E -->|Yes| F[Attach case_id to internal record for tracking] E -->|No| H[Create record without case_id] G --> H H --> I[Finish ingestion with created records] F --> I ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Enable optional case ID tracking in general QA-style presets that previously had no optional fields. |
  • Add `case_id` to the `optionalFields` array for the basic question/answer preset with required `question`, `answer`, `problem_topic`, `canary`.
  • Add `case_id` to the `optionalFields` for the preset with required `Question`, `Answer` and optional `Topic`, `canary`.
  • Add `case_id` to the `optionalFields` for the preset with required `instance_id`, `query`, `evaluation`, `language`.
  • Add `case_id` to the `optionalFields` for the preset with required `problem`, `answer`, `problem_category`, `answer_type`.
  • Add `case_id` to the `optionalFields` for the preset with required `question`, `answer`, `topic`, `canary`.
| `src/routes/(main)/eval/config/datasetPresets.ts` | | Extend classification-style presets to include optional case IDs alongside existing metadata fields. |
  • Add `case_id` to the `optionalFields` for the preset with required `question`, `answer`, `raw_subject`, `category` and optional `canary`.
  • Add `case_id` to the `optionalFields` for the preset with required `question`, `answer`, `raw_subject`, `category`, `Verified_Classes` and optional `canary`.
| `src/routes/(main)/eval/config/datasetPresets.ts` |

You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. strategy plus explicit cache-write pricing, while keeping original Xiaomi provider cards updated and consistent. #### Updated class diagram for AIChatModelCard pricing and Xiaomi MiMo LobeHub-hosted cards ```mermaid classDiagram class AIChatModelCard { abilities contextWindowTokens description displayName enabled id maxOutput pricing releasedAt settings type } class Pricing { units } class PricingUnit { name strategy rate tiers unit } class PricingTier { rate upTo } class PricingStrategy { fixed tiered } class XiaomiProviderXiaomimimoModels { xiaomimimoChatModels : AIChatModelCard[] } class LobeHubHostedXiaomimimoModels { xiaomimimoChatModels : AIChatModelCard[] } class LobehubChatModelsModule { lobehubChatModels : AIChatModelCard[] } AIChatModelCard --> Pricing : has Pricing --> PricingUnit : contains PricingUnit --> PricingTier : uses for_tiered PricingUnit --> PricingStrategy : uses XiaomiProviderXiaomimimoModels --> AIChatModelCard : defines_CNY_pricing LobeHubHostedXiaomimimoModels --> AIChatModelCard : defines_USD_pricing LobehubChatModelsModule --> LobeHubHostedXiaomimimoModels : aggregates LobehubChatModelsModule --> AIChatModelCard : exposes ``` #### Architecture flow diagram for LobeHub chat registry including Xiaomi MiMo-hosted models ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph ProviderModules AAnthropic["anthropicChatModels"] AGoogle["googleChatModels"] AOpenAI["openaiChatModels"] ABedrock["bedrockChatModels"] ADeepseek["deepseekChatModels"] AMinimax["minimaxChatModels"] AMoonshot["moonshotChatModels"] AXai["xaiChatModels"] AXiaomiProvider["xiaomimimoChatModels (Xiaomi provider, CNY)"] end subgraph LobeHubHostedXiaomiMiMo AXiaomiLobeHub["xiaomimimoChatModels (LobeHub-hosted, USD)"] end subgraph LobeHubChatRegistry LModels["lobehubChatModels"] end AAnthropic --> LModels AGoogle --> LModels AOpenAI --> LModels ABedrock --> LModels ADeepseek --> LModels AXai --> LModels AMinimax --> LModels AMoonshot --> LModels AXiaomiLobeHub --> LModels AXiaomiProvider -. parallel_infra .- AXiaomiLobeHub ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Align Xiaomi MiMo provider pricing for mimo-v2-pro to a tiered strategy instead of lookup while keeping descriptions formatted. |
  • Reformats long description strings for MiMo-V2 Pro/Omni/Flash to multi-line literals for readability.

  • Keeps existing CNY pricing values and thresholds but expresses them using the tiered pricing structure.

## Reviewer's Guide Adds cross-page select-all support and UI hints to the Resource Manager explorer (list and masonry views), centralizes selection logic in the resource store (including resolve-all-IDs and delete-by-query flows), enhances bulk knowledge-base operations to respect select-all, and introduces safer immutable updates and new backend endpoints for resolving and deleting resources by query. #### Sequence diagram for resolving select-all IDs and performing bulk delete ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI_Explorer as UI_Explorer participant RM_Store as ResourceManagerStore participant ResourceService as ResourceService participant FileService as FileService participant Lambda_FileRouter as LambdaFileRouter participant KnowledgeRepo as KnowledgeRepo participant DocumentService as DocumentService participant FileModel as FileModel participant FileStorageService as FileStorageService User->>UI_Explorer: Click toolbar checkbox then Select all UI_Explorer->>RM_Store: setSelectAllState(all) RM_Store-->>UI_Explorer: selectAllState = all User->>UI_Explorer: Trigger Delete action UI_Explorer->>RM_Store: onActionClick(delete) RM_Store->>FileService: get queryParams from useFileStore alt selectAllState is all RM_Store->>ResourceService: deleteResourcesByQuery(queryParams) ResourceService->>FileService: deleteKnowledgeItemsByQuery(backendParams) FileService->>Lambda_FileRouter: deleteKnowledgeItemsByQuery(input) loop batched query Lambda_FileRouter->>KnowledgeRepo: query(input with limit and offset) KnowledgeRepo-->>Lambda_FileRouter: knowledgeItems Lambda_FileRouter->>Lambda_FileRouter: filterKnowledgeItems Lambda_FileRouter->>Lambda_FileRouter: split fileIds and documentIds end Lambda_FileRouter->>DocumentService: deleteDocuments(documentIds) DocumentService-->>Lambda_FileRouter: documents deleted Lambda_FileRouter->>FileModel: deleteMany(fileIds, REMOVE_GLOBAL_FILE) FileModel-->>Lambda_FileRouter: needToRemoveFileList Lambda_FileRouter->>FileStorageService: deleteFiles(fileUrls) FileStorageService-->>Lambda_FileRouter: files deleted Lambda_FileRouter-->>FileService: { count } FileService-->>ResourceService: { count } ResourceService-->>RM_Store: { count } RM_Store->>RM_Store: clearSelectAllState and selectedFileIds else normal selection RM_Store->>FileService: deleteResources(selectedFileIds) FileService-->>RM_Store: deletion complete RM_Store->>RM_Store: set selectedFileIds [] end RM_Store-->>UI_Explorer: updated state UI_Explorer-->>User: List refreshed with items removed ``` #### Sequence diagram for select-all add to knowledge base with ID resolution ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant UI_Explorer as UI_Explorer participant RM_Store as ResourceManagerStore participant AddKBModal as AddFilesToKnowledgeBaseModal participant SelectForm as SelectForm participant ResourceService as ResourceService participant FileService as FileService participant Lambda_FileRouter as LambdaFileRouter participant KnowledgeRepo as KnowledgeRepo participant KB_Store as KnowledgeBaseStore User->>UI_Explorer: Click Select all UI_Explorer->>RM_Store: setSelectAllState(all) RM_Store-->>UI_Explorer: selectAllState = all User->>UI_Explorer: Choose Add to knowledge base UI_Explorer->>RM_Store: ## Reviewer's Guide Refactors agent execution snapshot storage and viewing to use an incremental baseline+delta message format, strip redundant/heavy data from events and context engine payloads, and add utilities plus minor API changes so tooling can reconstruct full message history while significantly reducing snapshot size and staying backward compatible. #### Sequence diagram for recording incremental snapshot steps with baseline+delta messages ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AgentRuntimeService participant AgentState participant RuntimeExecutors participant SnapshotStore AgentRuntimeService->>RuntimeExecutors: executeStep(currentContext) RuntimeExecutors-->>AgentRuntimeService: stepResult(newState, events) AgentRuntimeService->>AgentState: read messages (prevMessages) AgentRuntimeService->>AgentState: apply newState AgentState-->>AgentRuntimeService: messagesAfter AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: detect isCompression (compression_complete event) AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: compute isBaseline (stepIndex==0 or isCompression) AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: compute messagesDelta = isBaseline ? afterMessages : afterMessages.slice(prevMessages.length) AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: strip llm_stream from events AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: strip finalState.messages from done events AgentRuntimeService->>AgentRuntimeService: strip toolResults from context.payload AgentRuntimeService->>SnapshotStore: append StepSnapshot { isCompressionReset, messagesBaseline (when isBaseline), messagesDelta, events (stripped), context.payload (stripped) } ``` #### Sequence diagram for inspecting snapshots and reconstructing messages ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant InspectCLI participant SnapshotStore participant ViewerModule participant ReconstructUtils User->>InspectCLI: agent-tracing inspect --step N [--message-index M] InspectCLI->>SnapshotStore: load ExecutionSnapshot SnapshotStore-->>InspectCLI: snapshot(steps) alt show single message InspectCLI->>ViewerModule: renderMessageDetail(stepN, msgIndex, source, allSteps) ViewerModule->>ViewerModule: resolveStepMessages(stepN, allSteps) alt legacy format ViewerModule-->>ViewerModule: use step.messages/messagesAfter else incremental format ViewerModule->>ReconstructUtils: reconstructMessages(allSteps, stepIndex) ReconstructUtils-->>ViewerModule: {messages, messagesAfter} end ViewerModule-->>InspectCLI: rendered message detail else show step detail InspectCLI->>ViewerModule: renderStepDetail(stepN, {allSteps, flags}) ViewerModule->>ViewerModule: resolveStepMessages(stepN, allSteps) alt legacy format ViewerModule-->>ViewerModule: use step.messages else incremental format ViewerModule->>ReconstructUtils: reconstructMessages(allSteps, stepIndex) ReconstructUtils-->>ViewerModule: {messages, messagesAfter} end ViewerModule-->>InspectCLI: rendered step detail end InspectCLI-->>User: print output to terminal ``` #### Class diagram for incremental StepSnapshot format and reconstruction utilities ```mermaid classDiagram class ExecutionSnapshot { +string id +StepSnapshot[] steps +number createdAt } class StepSnapshot { +number stepIndex +string stepType +number startedAt +number completedAt +number executionTimeMs +number totalTokens +number totalCost +number inputTokens +number outputTokens +boolean isCompressionReset +any[] messages %% deprecated: legacy format +any[] messagesAfter %% deprecated: legacy format +any[] messagesBaseline +any[] messagesDelta +any[] events +any[] toolsResult +string reasoning } class ReconstructUtils { +isIncrementalFormat(snapshot ExecutionSnapshot) boolean +reconstructMessages(steps StepSnapshot[], targetStepIndex number) any +expandSnapshot(snapshot ExecutionSnapshot) ExecutionSnapshot } class AgentRuntimeService { +AgentRuntimeService(db LobeChatDatabase, userId string, options AgentRuntimeServiceOptions) +runAgentOperation() +appendStepToPartial() } class RuntimeExecutors { +createRuntimeExecutors(deps any) any +serverMessagesEngine(contextEngineInput any) Promise~any[]~ } class AiAgentService { +AiAgentService(db LobeChatDatabase, userId string, options AiAgentServiceOptions) +runAgent() } class ViewerModule { +renderStepDetail(step StepSnapshot, options any) string +renderMessageDetail(step StepSnapshot, msgIndex number, source string, allSteps StepSnapshot[]) string +resolveStepMessages(step StepSnapshot, allSteps StepSnapshot[]) any } class InspectCLI { +registerInspectCommand(program Command) } ExecutionSnapshot "1" o-- "*" StepSnapshot ReconstructUtils ..> StepSnapshot ReconstructUtils ..> ExecutionSnapshot AgentRuntimeService ..> ExecutionSnapshot : creates/updates AgentRuntimeService ..> StepSnapshot : builds incremental fields RuntimeExecutors ..> AgentRuntimeService : used by RuntimeExecutors ..> StepSnapshot : emits events used in snapshots AiAgentService ..> AgentRuntimeService : constructs with runtimeOptions ViewerModule ..> StepSnapshot : reads ViewerModule ..> ReconstructUtils : calls reconstructMessages InspectCLI ..> ViewerModule : calls renderStepDetail InspectCLI ..> ExecutionSnapshot : loads from store ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Store step snapshots using messages baselines plus per-step deltas instead of full message arrays, with compression reset support. |
  • Introduce StepSnapshot fields isCompressionReset, messagesBaseline, and messagesDelta while keeping messages/messagesAfter as deprecated fields for backwards compatibility.
  • In AgentRuntimeService, compute per-step prevMessages and afterMessages, mark baseline steps (step 0 or compression), and persist only messagesDelta plus optional messagesBaseline.
  • Flag compression steps via isCompressionReset so reconstruction logic can restart from a new baseline after compression.
| `packages/agent-tracing/src/types.ts`
`src/server/services/agentRuntime/AgentRuntimeService.ts` | | Strip large or redundant data from snapshot events and context engine payloads to prevent oversized snapshots. |
  • Filter llm_stream events out of stepResult.events before persisting snapshots.
  • Remove finalState.messages from done events while preserving other state such as tool manifests.
  • Drop toolResults from context.payload since they are already stored separately in step.toolsResult.
  • In context_engine_result events, omit messages and toolsConfig from input, replacing them with a lightweight structure containing remaining params and toolCount, and store only outputMessageCount instead of full output messages.
| `src/server/services/agentRuntime/AgentRuntimeService.ts`
`src/server/modules/AgentRuntime/RuntimeExecutors.ts` | | Add utilities to detect incremental snapshots and reconstruct full messages for both library consumers and CLI viewer. |
  • Implement isIncrementalFormat to detect whether any step uses messagesDelta.
  • Implement reconstructMessages to walk the baseline+delta chain (handling compression baselines) and return messages/messagesAfter for a target step.
  • Implement expandSnapshot to materialize legacy-style messages/messagesAfter for all steps when given an incremental snapshot.
  • Add vitest coverage for reconstructMessages, isIncrementalFormat, and expandSnapshot including compression, multiple steps, empty deltas, and legacy passthrough.
  • Export the new utilities from the agent-tracing package public API.
| `packages/agent-tracing/src/utils/reconstruct.ts`
`packages/agent-tracing/src/utils/reconstruct.test.ts`
`packages/agent-tracing/src/index.ts` | | Update the tracing viewer and CLI inspection to work with both legacy and incremental snapshot formats. |
  • Add resolveStepMessages helper in the viewer layer to return messages/messagesAfter from either legacy fields or reconstructMessages using all steps.
  • Adjust renderMessageDetail and renderStepDetail to call resolveStepMessages and accept an allSteps option so they can render messages from incremental snapshots.
  • Wire snapshot.steps through inspect CLI so message/step rendering functions can reconstruct messages when only deltas are stored.
  • Ensure fallback rendering (when no context_engine_result event) still works by resolving messages via the new helper.
| `packages/agent-tracing/src/viewer/index.ts`
`packages/agent-tracing/src/cli/inspect.ts` | | Allow AiAgentService to inject AgentRuntimeService runtime options for better configurability in tests and runtime. |
  • Extend AiAgentService constructor to accept an optional options object containing runtimeOptions.

## Reviewer's Guide Introduces a generalized external lifecycle hooks system for the agent runtime that works in both local (in‑memory) and production (webhook/QStash) modes, wiring it through agent execution and adding comprehensive tests. #### Sequence diagram for completion hooks dispatch in local vs production mode ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AgentRuntimeService participant HookDispatcher participant QueueRuntime as QueueRuntimeMode participant LocalHandler as AgentHook.handler participant QStash participant WebhookEndpoint AgentRuntimeService->>HookDispatcher: dispatchCompletionHooks(operationId, state, reason) activate HookDispatcher HookDispatcher->>QueueRuntime: isQueueAgentRuntimeEnabled() alt Local mode (queue disabled) HookDispatcher-->>LocalHandler: call handler(event) for each AgentHook LocalHandler-->>HookDispatcher: Promise resolved (errors logged only) else Production mode (queue enabled) HookDispatcher-->>WebhookEndpoint: deliverWebhook via fetch (if delivery == fetch) WebhookEndpoint-->>HookDispatcher: 2xx/4xx/5xx (ignored, only logged) HookDispatcher-->>QStash: publishJSON (if delivery == qstash) QStash-->>WebhookEndpoint: POST payload WebhookEndpoint-->>QStash: response (ignored by main flow) end HookDispatcher-->>AgentRuntimeService: hooks dispatched AgentRuntimeService->>HookDispatcher: unregister(operationId) HookDispatcher-->>AgentRuntimeService: cleanup done deactivate HookDispatcher ``` #### Class diagram for the new agent runtime hooks system ```mermaid classDiagram class HookDispatcher { - Map~string, AgentHook[]~ hooks + dispatch(operationId string, type AgentHookType, event AgentHookEvent, serializedHooks SerializedHook[] ) Promise~void~ + getSerializedHooks(operationId string) SerializedHook[] + hasHooks(operationId string) boolean + register(operationId string, hooks AgentHook[]) void + unregister(operationId string) void } class AgentHook { + string id + AgentHookType type + AgentHookWebhook webhook + handler(event AgentHookEvent) Promise~void~ } class AgentHookWebhook { + string url + string delivery + Record~string, unknown~ body } class AgentHookEvent { + string agentId + number cost + number duration + string errorDetail + string errorMessage + string lastAssistantContent + number llmCalls + Record~string, unknown~ metadata + string operationId + string reason + boolean shouldContinue + string status + number stepIndex + number steps + string stepType + number toolCalls + string topicId + number totalTokens + string userId } class SerializedHook { + string id + AgentHookType type + AgentHookWebhook webhook } class AgentRuntimeService { + dispatchCompletionHooks(operationId string, state any, reason string) Promise~void~ } class AiAgentService { + execAgent(..., hooks AgentHook[], ...) Promise~void~ } class AgentState { + any metadata } HookDispatcher --> AgentHook : manages HookDispatcher --> SerializedHook : returns AgentHook --> AgentHookWebhook : optional AgentHook --> AgentHookEvent : handler(event) AgentRuntimeService --> HookDispatcher : uses AgentRuntimeService --> AgentState : persists metadata._hooks AiAgentService --> AgentRuntimeService : passes hooks AgentState --> SerializedHook : metadata._hooks ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Wire external lifecycle hooks through agent runtime and AI agent service APIs. |
  • Extend OperationCreationParams and InternalExecAgentParams to accept an optional hooks array of AgentHook definitions.
  • Propagate hooks from AiAgentService.execAgent parameters into AgentRuntimeService.createOperation calls so hooks are registered at operation creation time.
| `src/server/services/agentRuntime/types.ts`
`src/server/services/aiAgent/index.ts` | | Register and persist hooks on operation creation and dispatch them on completion/error. |
  • Pass hooks into AgentRuntimeService when creating operations and register them with a shared HookDispatcher instance.
  • On registration, serialize webhook-capable hooks and persist them into agent state metadata._hooks so they survive across steps in production/queue mode.
  • On successful completion and on failure, dispatch onComplete (and onError on failures) hooks using a new dispatchCompletionHooks helper, then fall back to the legacy onComplete callback.
  • Ensure hook dispatch is fire-and-forget: errors are logged but never thrown, and hooks are cleaned up after completion.
| `src/server/services/agentRuntime/AgentRuntimeService.ts` | | Implement HookDispatcher and the hook type system to support local handlers and production webhooks/QStash delivery. |
  • Introduce AgentHook, AgentHookEvent, AgentHookType, AgentHookWebhook, and SerializedHook types to describe hook lifecycles, payloads, and serialization for persistence.
  • Implement HookDispatcher with in-memory hook storage, registration/unregistration, local dispatch (calling handler functions), and production dispatch (sending webhooks based on serialized configuration).
  • Add webhook delivery logic that resolves relative URLs using INTERNAL_APP_URL/APP_URL, prefers QStash delivery when configured, and falls back to plain fetch with robust error logging.
  • Provide a singleton hookDispatcher instance exported from the hooks module for use across the agent runtime.
| `src/server/services/agentRuntime/hooks/types.ts`
`src/server/services/agentRuntime/hooks/HookDispatcher.ts`
`src/server/services/agentRuntime/hooks/index.ts` | | Add comprehensive tests for HookDispatcher behavior in local and production modes. |
  • Mock queue mode toggling via isQueueAgentRuntimeEnabled to test both local (in-process handlers) and production (webhook) dispatch paths.
  • Verify hook registration semantics, handler invocation rules per hook type, error isolation between hooks, and behavior when no hooks are registered.
  • Test webhook serialization, payload merging with custom webhook.body, that local handlers are not called in production mode, and that only webhook-configured hooks are serialized.
  • Cover all supported hook types: beforeStep, afterStep, onComplete, and onError.
| `src/server/services/agentRuntime/hooks/__tests__/HookDispatcher.test.ts` | ---

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide Configures the Docker release GitHub Actions workflow to publish a floating `canary` Docker tag for canary prerelease GitHub releases, while preserving existing tagging behavior for stable and other prereleases. #### Sequence diagram for Docker image tagging on GitHub release ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant GitHubReleaseEvent as GitHubReleaseEvent participant ReleaseDockerWorkflow as ReleaseDockerWorkflow participant DockerBuildx as DockerBuildx participant DockerRegistry as DockerRegistry GitHubReleaseEvent->>ReleaseDockerWorkflow: Trigger with release(prerelease, tag_name) ReleaseDockerWorkflow->>DockerBuildx: Build image DockerBuildx->>DockerRegistry: Push semver tag pattern {{version}} alt prerelease is false ReleaseDockerWorkflow->>DockerBuildx: Enable latest tag DockerBuildx->>DockerRegistry: Push tag latest else prerelease is true ReleaseDockerWorkflow-->>DockerBuildx: Disable latest tag end alt tag_name contains -canary. ReleaseDockerWorkflow->>DockerBuildx: Enable canary tag DockerBuildx->>DockerRegistry: Push tag canary DockerBuildx->>DockerRegistry: Push tag tag_name else tag_name does not contain -canary. ReleaseDockerWorkflow-->>DockerBuildx: Disable canary tag DockerBuildx->>DockerRegistry: Push tag tag_name end ``` #### Flow diagram for Docker tag enablement rules in release workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[GitHub release event\nprerelease, tag_name] --> B{prerelease?} B -- No --> C[Enable latest tag\nPush latest] B -- Yes --> D[Disable latest tag] A --> E{tag_name contains -canary.?} E -- Yes --> F[Enable canary tag\nPush canary] E -- No --> G[Disable canary tag] A --> H[Enable version tag for prerelease\nPush tag_name] ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Add a floating `canary` Docker image tag for canary prerelease GitHub releases in the Docker publish workflow. |
  • Extend the `tags` configuration to include a `type=raw,value=canary` tag for images built during releases.
  • Gate the `canary` tag so it is only enabled when the GitHub release tag name contains the `-canary.` substring, ensuring only canary prereleases receive this floating tag.
  • Mirror the new `canary` tag rule in both Docker publish steps so behavior is consistent across all build matrix entries.
| `.github/workflows/release-docker.yml` |

You can also reply to a review comment with `@sourcery-ai issue` to create an issue from it. - **Generate a pull request title:** Write `@sourcery-ai` anywhere in the pull request title to generate a title at any time. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai title` on the pull request to (re-)generate the title at any time. - **Generate a pull request summary:** Write `@sourcery-ai summary` anywhere in the pull request body to generate a PR summary at any time exactly where you want it. You can also comment `@sourcery-ai summary` on the pull request to (re-)generate the summary at any time. - **Generate reviewer's guide:** Comment `@sourcery-ai guide` on the pull request to (re-)generate the reviewer's guide at any time. - **Resolve all Sourcery comments:** Comment `@sourcery-ai resolve` on the pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore. - **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review! #### Customizing Your Experience Access your [dashboard](https://app.sourcery.ai) to: - Enable or disable review features such as the Sourcery-generated pull request summary, the reviewer's guide, and others. - Change the review language. - Add, remove or edit custom review instructions. - Adjust other review settings. #### Getting Help - [Contact our support team](mailto:support@sourcery.ai) for questions or feedback. - Visit our [documentation](https://docs.sourcery.ai) for detailed guides and information. - Keep in touch with the Sourcery team by following us on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/SourceryAI), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/sourcery-ai/) or [GitHub](https://github.com/sourcery-ai).

## Reviewer's Guide Refines Xiaomi MiMo chat payload handling (message sanitization, reasoning transformation, and web search support), hardens AI provider creation and initialization around uniqueness and conflicts, and applies several UI/UX tweaks including form validation, badge-visibility logic, referral copy updates, and minor style/content adjustments. #### Sequence diagram for AI provider creation with duplicate ID handling ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant CreateNewProviderForm as CreateNewProviderForm participant AiInfraStore as AiInfraStore participant TRPCClient as TRPCClient participant AiProviderRouter as aiProviderRouter participant AiProviderModel as AiProviderModel participant PostgreSQL as PostgreSQL User->>CreateNewProviderForm: Enter provider id CreateNewProviderForm->>AiInfraStore: getState AiInfraStore-->>CreateNewProviderForm: aiProviderList CreateNewProviderForm->>CreateNewProviderForm: Validate id format and uniqueness alt Duplicate id found on client CreateNewProviderForm-->>User: Show createNewAiProvider.id.duplicate error else Unique id on client User->>CreateNewProviderForm: Submit form CreateNewProviderForm->>TRPCClient: createAiProvider(input) TRPCClient->>AiProviderRouter: createAiProvider(input) AiProviderRouter->>AiProviderModel: create(input, encrypt) AiProviderModel->>PostgreSQL: INSERT aiProviders alt PostgreSQL unique violation PostgreSQL-->>AiProviderModel: Error code 23505 AiProviderModel-->>AiProviderRouter: Throw error AiProviderRouter->>AiProviderRouter: Catch error and map to TRPCError CONFLICT AiProviderRouter-->>TRPCClient: TRPCError CONFLICT TRPCClient-->>CreateNewProviderForm: Error Provider already exists CreateNewProviderForm-->>User: Show createNewAiProvider.id.duplicate error else Insert succeeds PostgreSQL-->>AiProviderModel: New provider row AiProviderModel-->>AiProviderRouter: id AiProviderRouter-->>TRPCClient: id TRPCClient-->>CreateNewProviderForm: Success CreateNewProviderForm-->>User: Close modal and refresh list end end ``` #### Sequence diagram for Xiaomi MiMo chat payload sanitization and web search ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client as ClientApp participant XiaomiParams as XiaomiParams participant Sanitize as sanitizeXiaomiMessages participant Transform as transformXiaomiMessage Client->>XiaomiParams: handlePayload(payload) XiaomiParams->>XiaomiParams: Extract enabledSearch, messages, tools, thinking XiaomiParams->>Sanitize: sanitizeXiaomiMessages(messages, thinking.type) loop For each message Sanitize->>Transform: transformXiaomiMessage(message, thinking.type) Transform-->>Sanitize: transformedMessage Sanitize->>Sanitize: Filter user messages with hasMessageContent end loop Drop trailing assistant Sanitize->>Sanitize: Pop last assistant message while role is assistant end Sanitize-->>XiaomiParams: sanitizedMessages XiaomiParams->>XiaomiParams: Merge tools with web_search when enabledSearch XiaomiParams-->>Client: Payload { messages, tools, webSearchEnabled, stream, temperature } ``` #### Class diagram for Xiaomi MiMo message sanitization and payload handling ```mermaid classDiagram class XiaomiParams { +chatCompletion any } class sanitizeXiaomiMessagesFn { +sanitizeXiaomiMessages(messages, thinkingType) any[] } class transformXiaomiMessageFn { +transformXiaomiMessage(message, thinkingType) any } class hasMessageContentFn { +hasMessageContent(content) bool } XiaomiParams --> sanitizeXiaomiMessagesFn : uses sanitizeXiaomiMessagesFn --> transformXiaomiMessageFn : maps sanitizeXiaomiMessagesFn --> hasMessageContentFn : filters class ChatCompletionHandler { +handlePayload(payload) any } XiaomiParams o-- ChatCompletionHandler : chatCompletion class Payload { +messages any[] +enabledSearch bool +tools any[] +thinking any +temperature number +stream bool } ChatCompletionHandler --> Payload : transforms class XiaomiRequestBody { +messages any[] +stream bool +tools any[] +webSearchEnabled bool +temperature number } ChatCompletionHandler --> XiaomiRequestBody : returns ``` #### Class diagram for AI provider model and TRPC router conflict-safe initialization ```mermaid classDiagram class AiProviderModel { -db any -userId string +isBuiltInProvider(id) bool +getAiProviderById(id) any } class AiProvidersTable { +id string +source string +userId string } AiProviderModel --> AiProvidersTable : inserts class Database { +insert(table) DatabaseInsert } class DatabaseInsert { +values(row) DatabaseInsert +onConflictDoNothing() DatabaseInsert } AiProviderModel --> Database : uses Database --> DatabaseInsert : returns class AiProviderRouter { +createAiProvider(input, ctx) Promise~string~ +getAiProviderById(id, ctx) Promise~any~ } class GateKeeper { +encrypt(value) string } class AiProviderContext { +aiProviderModel AiProviderModel +gateKeeper GateKeeper } AiProviderRouter --> AiProviderContext : depends on AiProviderContext --> AiProviderModel : provides AiProviderContext --> GateKeeper : provides class TRPCError { +code string +message string } AiProviderRouter --> TRPCError : throws class CreateAiProviderInput { +id string } AiProviderRouter --> CreateAiProviderInput : consumes ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Improve Xiaomi MiMo provider payload sanitization and add web search support. |
  • Refactored Xiaomi message transformation into reusable helpers to normalize reasoning_content and filter messages.
  • Filtered out empty user messages and dropped trailing assistant messages that Xiaomi rejects.
  • Enabled Xiaomi web search flag when enabledSearch is true and merged web_search tool into existing tools.

- `packages/model-bank/` – new model definitions and provider configs

- `src/features/ModelSwitchPanel/` – new ReasoningTokenSlider32k/80k components
- `src/services/chat/` – modelParamsResolver updates
- `locales/` – i18n updates

### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/8b47c7710319d9f6bdfce1e3779eac957533a5c3/src/features/Electron/connection/DeviceGateway.tsx#L84 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Treat authenticating as in-progress in gateway UI** `GatewayClient` emits an `authenticating` state after socket open and before `connected`, but this component only treats `connecting`/`reconnecting` as in-progress. During that phase the popover renders the device as disconnected and the switch as off, which is misleading and allows users to re-trigger connect while a handshake is already underway. Include `authenticating` in the in-progress/checked logic. --- https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/8b47c7710319d9f6bdfce1e3779eac957533a5c3/apps/desktop/src/main/services/gatewayConnectionSrv.ts#L116-L117 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Short-circuit connect during authentication phase** `connect()` only no-ops for `connected` and `connecting`, so a call received while status is `authenticating` will run `doConnect()` again, forcibly disconnecting the current client and restarting the handshake. This can cause avoidable reconnect churn when connect is triggered twice during startup/handshake; `authenticating` (and usually `reconnecting`) should be treated as already in progress.

body:
Hi @BillionClaw, two things to address before merge:

1. **Please add a regression test.** `src/store/image/slices/generationConfig/action.test.ts` already has an `Aspect Ratio Setting` describe block — add a case there that seeds `parameters.resolution` (e.g. `'4K'`) with a schema exposing a `resolution` enum, calls `setAspectRatio('16:9')`, and asserts the resolution is preserved. Otherwise this bug can silently regress.

2. **Validate the preserved value against the schema's enum.** The current patch unconditionally copies `parameters.resolution` into `newParams`. If the (current or later-applied) `parametersSchema.resolution.enum` doesn't contain the previous value, we end up carrying an invalid value forward. Please check membership in `parametersSchema.resolution.enum` before copying, and fall back to the schema default (or drop the field) when it's not a valid option.

body: Self-hosted repro on lobehub/lobehub:latest: I reproduced the same root cause in a Docker deployment. In my case the model metadata already had the real context window in storage (for example GPT-5.4 at ~1M tokens), but the GeneralChatAgent compression path did not populate compressionConfig.maxWindowToken before shouldCompress() ran, so it fell back to DEFAULT_MAX_CONTEXT=128k and triggered compression around 64k with the default 0.5 ratio. This is not OpenAI-specific: Claude models are affected too as long as they go through the same GeneralChatAgent path with enableContextCompression=true. After locally patching the runtime to pass modelRuntimeConfig.contextWindowTokens into compressionConfig.maxWindowToken, the trigger point correctly scales with the real model window instead of the hardcoded 128k fallback.

body:
Thanks, @Innei !

Two categories of test breakage patched in this commit:

E2E selectors (`e2e/src/steps/page/`): The "New Page" button in the Pages sidebar is rendered by `@lobehub/ui`'s `ActionIcon`, which outputs `<div role="button">` rather than a native `<button>`. The old selectors (`button:has(svg.lucide-square-pen)`, `input[placeholder*="Search"]`) were both dead — the first matched no element, and the search bar is a click-handler `NavItem`, not an `<input>`. Fixed to `[role="button"]:has(svg.lucide-square-pen)`.

Unit test mocks (`apps/desktop/.../LocalFileCtr.test.ts`, `RemoteServerConfigCtr.test.ts`): The `net.fetch` change routes HTTP calls through Electron's networking stack instead of `globalThis.fetch`. The tests were patching `global.fetch` / using `vi.stubGlobal`, which no longer intercepted anything. Fixed by hoisting the fetch mock and pointing `vi.mock('@/utils/net-fetch', ...)` at it directly.

**Claude finished @sudongyuer's task in 1m 33s** —— [View job](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/actions/runs/23784486881)

---
### Code Review

- [x] Gather context
- [x] Read source code changes
- [x] Review locale changes
- [x] Post review feedback

---

This PR makes minimal, focused changes: 3 source files and 78 locale files for translation coverage. Here's the review:

---

### Source Code (`src/`)

**`src/business/server/mobile-routers/mobileSubscription.ts`** (new)

```ts
import { router } from '@/libs/trpc/lambda';
export const mobileSubscriptionRouter = router({});
```

This is identical in structure to the existing `src/business/server/lambda-routers/subscription.ts` — a placeholder router awaiting cloud implementation. The pattern is consistent with the codebase. No issues here.

**`src/server/routers/mobile/index.ts`**

The `subscription: mobileSubscriptionRouter` registration is clean and alphabetically ordered correctly in the router object. The import is added at the top appropriately.

**`src/locales/default/subscription.ts`**

Three new keys added:
```ts
'crossPlatform.desc': 'This subscription was purchased through the mobile app...'
'crossPlatform.manageOnMobile': 'Manage on mobile device'
'crossPlatform.title': 'Cross-Platform Subscription'
```
The keys follow existing naming conventions and the copy is clear and user-friendly.

---

### Locale Files

78 locale files across 18 languages were updated. The `crossPlatform.*` keys are present and consistent across all languages. The other locale changes (models.json, providers.json, etc.) appear to be routine i18n sync from the CI pipeline, not manually authored.

---

### Observations

1. **Empty router is intentional** — The placeholder `router({})` will get procedures merged in from `lobehub-cloud`. This is a valid pattern already used in this codebase. Worth noting that since the router has no procedures, adding it to the mobile router causes no behavioral change until cloud extends it.

2. **No type-check risk** — The empty router is valid TypeScript and tRPC will handle it correctly. The import path `@/business/server/mobile-routers/mobileSubscription` is consistent with neighboring files.

3. **Unrelated locale diffs** — Some locale files (e.g., `models.json`, `plugin.json`, `onboarding.json`) include diffs beyond the `crossPlatform.*` keys. These appear to be auto-generated i18n sync changes, which is expected per the CLAUDE.md workflow ("CI handles it"). Not a concern, but the PR scope is wider than the summary suggests.

---

### Verdict

**Looks good.** The implementation is minimal, correct, and consistent with existing patterns. The i18n keys are well-formed and properly translated. No bugs, security issues, or structural concerns.

### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/blob/d5d92c6888a9875e5a40f8da984f4813c14fc410/src/hooks/useNavLayout.ts#L75 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Keep market tab hidden when showMarket is false** This change moves the community entry into `bottomMenuItems` and sets `hidden: !showMarket`, but the bottom-menu renderer (`src/routes/(main)/home/_layout/Body/BottomMenu/index.tsx`) does not consume `hidden` (it always maps every item to a link). That means the marketplace tab is now rendered even when `showMarket` is disabled, regressing the feature-flag gating that previously worked when this item lived in `topNavItems`.

body:
Code review findings after verifying against full source code:

## Issues

**1. [high] `wan2.6-image` lost image-required validation — `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/qwen/createImage.ts`**

`imageRequiredModels` includes `/^wan2\.6-image/`, but the validation check only exists inside `createHTTPSyncGeneration` (~line 236). Since the default route changed from sync to async, `wan2.6-image` now goes through `createHTTPAsyncGenerationTask`, which **completely bypasses the image-required validation**. Users calling `wan2.6-image` without providing an image will no longer get a helpful error message — they'll get a raw Alibaba API error instead.

Suggestion: move the `imageRequiredModels` validation up to the `createQwenImage` entry point, or duplicate it in `createHTTPAsyncGenerationTask`.

**2. [medium] Default route changed from sync to async — behavioral change affects existing models**

Previously, unmatched models defaulted to `multimodal-generation/generation` (sync). Now they default to `image-generation/generation` (async polling). Affected existing models include `wan2.6-image` and `wan2.6-t2i`. New models (wan2.7, kling) are added by this PR so they should be fine, but `wan2.6-*` models existed before — please confirm they work correctly on the new async `image-generation` endpoint.

**3. [low] Error double-wrapping in `createLegacySynthesisTask`** (pre-existing)

`createLegacySynthesisTask` throws `AgentRuntimeError.createImage(...)` directly for its missing-imageUrls validation (~line 102), but the outer `createQwenImage` catch wraps it again with `AgentRuntimeError.createImage(...)`. This nests one `AgentRuntimeError` inside another, losing the inner `errorType`. By contrast, `createHTTPAsyncGenerationTask` throws plain `Error` which avoids this. Pre-existing issue, but could be cleaned up during this refactor.

**4. [low] Redundant `/r2v$/` in `image2VideoModels` — `packages/model-runtime/src/providers/qwen/createVideo.ts`**

`/r2v$/` appears in both `image2VideoModels` and `reference2VideoModels`. Due to the `else if` chain, `reference2VideoModels` (branch 5) is checked before `image2VideoModels` (branch 7), so r2v models always get reference-to-video treatment. The `/r2v$/` entry in `image2VideoModels` is redundant and misleading — it could be removed without changing any behavior.

**5. [low] Missing `$` anchors on `syncOnlyModels` regexes**

`/^qwen-image-(edit|max)/`, `/^qwen-image-2\.0/`, `/^z-image-turbo/` all use prefix matching without `$`. This works for all current models, but future models with the same prefix but different API requirements would be silently misrouted. Consider adding a comment to clarify this is intentional prefix matching.

body:
After testing, when disabling the historical reasoning content toggle for qwen3.6-plus, the input tokens decreased from 5,643 to 4,962, a reduction of 681 ≈ 676 (the deep thinking token count from historical conversations).

Switching to a different conversation, when disabling the glm-4.7 toggle, the input tokens decreased from 4983 to 4352, a reduction of 631.

Additionally, I noticed that Qwen removes the thinking content from all historical messages, while GLM appears to retain the thinking content from the last historical message.

The current strategy is for the backend to pass the full historical message reasoning content to the model upstream, along with parameters, letting the upstream decide which reasoning content to use.

-----

Additionally, the build memory has currently been adjusted to around 6500, and after multiple retries, the build may succeed.

body:
I don't think this PR is ready to merge yet.

The main remaining issue is the `preserveThinking` semantics. The new switch reads like it controls whether historical assistant thinking/reasoning is replayed to the upstream model, but the current Qwen and Zhipu adapters still convert stored `message.reasoning.content` into `reasoning_content` unconditionally.

That means these cases still replay historical reasoning:

```ts
preserveThinking === false
preserveThinking === undefined
```

For Qwen, `preserve_thinking: false` is sent only when the flag is explicitly false, but the payload has already included `reasoning_content`. For Zhipu, `thinking.clear_thinking` is similarly controlled by the flag, but the historical `reasoning_content` conversion is also unconditional.

If the intended product behavior is "turn this off to avoid sending historical thinking", the adapter should only derive/send `reasoning_content` when `preserveThinking === true`. The current tests also appear to lock the opposite behavior, e.g. preserving `reasoning_content` when `preserveThinking` is absent, so those tests should be inverted.

A separate smaller point: the `llmPayload.preserveThinking` override path is not a formal runtime payload contract right now. I couldn't find a production caller that puts `preserveThinking` into `context.payload`, and `CallLLMPayload` / `GeneralAgentCallLLMInstructionPayload` don't declare it. Either formalize that override with types and a real call path, or remove the override read and rely on `ctx.agentConfig.chatConfig.preserveThinking`.
author: tjx666

body:
@tjx666 Regarding the first point, I had also considered not passing the reasoning content when the switch is turned off. But after further thought, I believe that passing all historical reasoning content in full and letting the API upstream decide whether to use it based on parameters would better preserve the upstream's intended behavior without disrupting it. There is no need for LobeHub to pre-trim it.

The second point has been fixed, thank you for raising it.

---
> This comment was translated by Claude.

<details>
<summary>Original Content</summary>

@tjx666 关于第一点，我此前也想过关闭开关时不传递推理内容。但后来经过思考，认为将历史推理内容全量传递，由 API 上游根据参数决定是否使用应当更能不破坏上游推荐意图行为。不必由 LobeHub 提前裁剪。

第二点已修复，感谢提出。
</details>

body:
Added a test case that covers the chunk-splitting scenario.

The test encodes `{"generation":"Hello 🌍","generation_token_count":1}` and splits the bytes at offset 23 — right in the middle of the 4-byte 🌍 emoji. `TextDecoder` with `stream: true` buffers the incomplete multi-byte sequence, but the resulting string is still incomplete JSON (`{"generation":"Hello ` — missing closing quote). Without the buffer, `JSON.parse` fails and the old code yields the raw string, which causes `transformLlamaStream` to read `chunk.generation` as `undefined`.

The test asserts that the buffered parser correctly reassembles the split chunks and produces `data: "Hello 🌍"` in the SSE output.

body:
@overpod Hi, I have a question: if the `enableResponseApi` toggle is turned off, would this cause GPT-5.5 Pro to also use Chat Completions, thereby resulting in an error?

A more reasonable approach might be to strictly limit the models in `responsesAPIModels` to only those that must use the Response endpoint (e.g., removing gpt-5.5 and keeping gpt-5.5-pro).

If the goal is to **prioritize** the Response endpoint for new GPT models, using `responsesAPIModels` might not be the best idea; we should look into a different solution instead.

cc @arvinxx
author: sxjeru

body: @sxjeru good point I think. What's your suggestions?
author: arvinxx

body:
@arvinxx tests added in `cabf03c6` — 10 unit tests covering the `shouldUseResponsesAPI` priority chain (P0 user override through P5 regex match), plus a regression guard that the user override wins even against factory-level `flagUseResponse`.

@sxjeru you raise a fair point, and I want to address it directly rather than route around it.

**On the gpt-5.5-pro concern:** if a user disables the toggle, this PR does send Pro models through `/v1/chat/completions`, which would fail. But I'd argue that's the *expected* outcome of an explicit user opt-out — the same way disabling streaming sends a non-streaming request even if it's slower. The toggle is documented as the user's API mode preference; honoring it for some models but not others is the surprising behavior.

**On the broader design question** — you're right that mixing "must use Responses" and "prefers Responses" into a single `responsesAPIModels` set is the root issue. Looking at the current set in `const/models.ts`, it already conflates two cohorts:

- *Genuinely required* — `o1-pro`, `o3-pro`, `*-deep-research`, `codex-mini-latest`, `computer-use-*`, `gpt-5-pro`, `gpt-5.x-pro`, `gpt-5.x-codex` (these have no Chat Completions equivalent)
- *Preferred but functional via Chat* — `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, `gpt-5.4-nano`, `gpt-5.5` (third-party proxies route these to `/v1/chat/completions` successfully today)

I see two paths forward and would defer to you on which fits the project direction:

**Path A — narrow the set** (your suggestion). Move models like `gpt-5.5` out of `responsesAPIModels`. Keeps the current "no override" contract. Drawback: the set needs ongoing curation as new models ship, and "prefers Responses" semantics are lost.

**Path B — split into required/preferred sets.** Introduce `responsesAPIRequiredModels` (hard, no override — Pro/research/codex) and let `responsesAPIModels` become the soft-preferred set that respects `enableResponseApi`. Encodes both intents explicitly. This PR's logic plus a curated `Required` set covers both your case (Pro stays on Responses) and mine (proxies can opt out for the rest).

Path A is smaller and ships now. Path B is more durable. Happy to refactor toward whichever you prefer — or close this PR if Path A is the direction and the curation is something you'd rather own internally.

cc @arvinxx — would appreciate your direction here.
author: overpod

body:
@sxjeru you're right, and I undersold this in my previous reply — disabling the toggle would have sent `gpt-5.5-pro` to chat/completions, where it has no endpoint. That's a real regression for Pro-tier models, not an "expected user opt-out" as I framed it.

I went with Path B (split into required vs preferred sets) in `dffffa89` since it cleanly handles both cases. Summary:

- New `responsesAPIRequiredModels` — hard set, ignores the toggle. Holds Pro / deep-research / codex / computer-use models that have no chat/completions equivalent (`o1-pro`, `o3-pro`, `gpt-5-pro`, `gpt-5.x-pro`, `*-codex`, `*-deep-research`, `computer-use-*`).
- `responsesAPIModels` — superset (required + soft-preferred), honors the toggle. Soft-preferred = `gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, `gpt-5.4-nano`, `gpt-5.5` — the ones that work fine through chat/completions.

So:
- Pro models stay on Responses API regardless of the toggle (your concern).
- Soft-preferred models default to Responses but can be opted out via the toggle (the proxy use case from #13513).
- All existing consumers (Azure, GitHub Copilot, newapi/aihubmix/opencodeZen routing, `src/services/chat`) read the superset, so default behavior is preserved without changes on their side.

Added tests in this commit:
- `shouldUseResponsesAPI`: required-model override-immunity (`gpt-5.5-pro` + `userApiMode='chatCompletion'` still uses Responses), soft-preferred override-honoring (`gpt-5.5` + `userApiMode='chatCompletion'` uses chat/completions).
- New `const/models.test.ts`: subset invariant (required ⊆ preferred), explicit checks that Pro models are required and `gpt-5.x` non-Pro are not.

Happy to adjust the membership of the required set if you'd like a different cut — I leaned on "no chat/completions endpoint exists" as the criterion.

cc @arvinxx

body:
Great feature! A few findings after reviewing the full source code:

## Issues

**1. [high] Missing concurrency guard — `src/features/PromptRewrite/usePromptRewrite.ts`**

`runTransform` doesn't check `isRewriting` before starting a new request. The `Action` component (`src/features/ChatInput/ActionBar/components/Action.tsx:58-61`) still fires `onClick` when `loading=true`, and line 72 only skips dropdown rendering for `disabled`, not `loading`. Rapid clicks will trigger multiple concurrent streams writing to the same `rewrittenPrompt` variable, producing garbled output in `onPromptChange`.

Suggestion: add `if (isRewriting) return;` at the top of `runTransform`.

**2. [medium] `isEnabled` OR logic allows disabled actions — `src/features/PromptRewrite/usePromptRewrite.ts`**

```ts
const isEnabled = (rewriteConfig?.enabled ?? false) || (translateConfig?.enabled ?? false);
```

If `promptRewrite` is disabled but `translation` is enabled, the rewrite button still appears and is clickable — it will send a request using the disabled `promptRewrite` config. Each action should check its own config's `enabled` state independently.

**3. [low] Unnecessary `useTranslation` namespace change in wrong component — `src/routes/(main)/(create)/video/features/PromptInput/index.tsx`**

The diff changes `SeedItem`'s `useTranslation('video')` to `useTranslation(['video', 'common'])`, but `SeedItem` only uses `video` namespace keys. `PromptTransformAction` has its own `useTranslation('common')` internally. Same for the image `PromptInput` — the `'common'` addition is unnecessary.

**4. [low] Missing unit test for `chainRewriteGenerationPrompt`**

Other chain functions in `packages/prompts/src/chains/__tests__/` (e.g., `rewriteQuery.test.ts`, `translate.test.ts`) all have corresponding tests. The new `rewriteGenerationPrompt.ts` should follow the same pattern.

## Question: Custom prompt support?

Currently the settings page renders `<SystemAgentForm allowDisable systemAgentKey="promptRewrite" />` without `allowCustomPrompt`, so users can only choose model/provider and toggle on/off. The rewrite system prompts for image/video/text are hardcoded in `chainRewriteGenerationPrompt`.

Meanwhile, the existing `queryRewrite` agent supports `allowCustomPrompt` (as shown in the settings UI). Would you be willing to also add `allowCustomPrompt` for:

1. **Prompt Rewrite** — letting users customize how prompts are rewritten (though this may need per-mode support for image/video/text scenarios)
2. **Translate** — the target language is currently hardcoded to `'English'`, a custom prompt would give users more flexibility

No pressure if you'd prefer to keep the scope small for this PR and address it in a follow-up.

body:
@tjx666 added a test commit (671ca6e). Coverage now explicitly fences the JPEG format-preservation behaviour:

- `compressImage` with `type='image/jpeg'` calls `toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.85)`
- `compressImage` with `type='image/png'` calls `toDataURL('image/png')` (no quality arg)
- `compressImage` with no type defaults to PNG
- `compressImageFile` with a large JPEG produces a `File` with `type === 'image/jpeg'` (regression fence for the previously hardcoded `'image/png'` MIME in `dataUrlToFile`)
- `compressImageFile` with a WebP input still falls back to PNG (documents the deliberate choice)

Existing PNG tests preserved.

FYI. 1. Fixed the suggestions for items 1, 5, 6, 7 2. Suggestion 2: Qwen has recommended using the Qwen-Image-2.0 series, which supports both image generation and image editing 3. Suggestion 3: This is intentional design logic — when `imageUrls` has only one image and `endImageUrl` is provided, some supported models pass the parameter as a first-frame reference image; the rest pass directly due to multi-image reference support 4. Suggestion 4: The original logic has already been covered — `wan2.7-r2v` will pass `imageUrls` and thus go directly to `reference_image` --- > This comment was translated by Claude.
Original Content FYI. 1. 修正第 1, 5, 6, 7 的建议 2. 第 2 个建议: Qwen 已推荐使用 Qwen-Image-2.0 系列,同时支持生图和改图功能 3. 第 3 个建议: 这是故意设计的逻辑,当 `imageUrls` 只有一个图片且 `endImageUrl` 传参时,部分支持的模型穿参为首帧参考图; 其余因为支持多图参考直接传参 4. 第 4 个建议: 已经涵盖了原始逻辑, `wan2.7-r2v` 将传参 `imageUrls` 故会直接走到 `reference_image`
